definition_zh: 假设；假说；前提；待验证的猜想
definition_en: a proposed explanation or premise that is put forward as a starting point and still has to be tested or proved
core_image: 先在下面垫一块地基，再把论点垒在上面
scene: 实验室的白板上写着一句可以被实验推翻的预测，旁边是涂层样本。 Before the experiment began, the team wrote one sentence on the whiteboard: the new coating should halve the rate of corrosion. That sentence was their hypothesis.
sceneCN: 这里 hypothesis 是「科学假说」（第 1 个义项：提出一个可检验的候选解释）；句意：实验开始前，团队在白板上写下一句话：新涂层应能把腐蚀速度减半。这句话就是他们的假说。

pos.zh: 假设；假说（尤指可检验的科学解释）
前提；被当作论证起点的命题

forms.label: 名词复数（希腊语式，-is 变 -es）

derivatives.zh: 假设的（较少用，与 hypothetical 同义）

senses.title: Scientific hypothesis: a testable explanation
senses.titleCN: 科学假说：可被检验的解释
senses.definition: a proposed explanation for observed facts that can be tested by experiment or further evidence
senses.definitionCN: 针对观察到的事实提出的解释，可通过实验或进一步证据来检验
senses.example: The hypothesis that the coating slows corrosion will be tested on twenty steel plates.
senses.exampleCN: “涂层能减缓腐蚀”这一假说将在二十块钢板上接受检验。
senses.why: A hypothesis is laid under a question the way a foundation is laid under a building: it is put in place first, and the experiment is built on top of it.
senses.whyCN: 假说被垫在一个问题下面，就像地基被垫在房屋下面：它先被放好，实验再在它上面搭建。

senses.title: Logical premise: assumed as a base
senses.titleCN: 逻辑前提：被当作论证底座
senses.definition: a proposition taken as true for the sake of an argument, so that other statements can be built on it
senses.definitionCN: 为了进行论证而被当作真的命题，其他陈述可建立在它之上
senses.example: The proof rests on the hypothesis that every finite set has a largest element.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明建立在“每个有限集都有最大元素”这一前提之上。
senses.why: In logic the word keeps its Greek shape: something is placed underneath the reasoning and left there while the argument stands on it.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑学里，这个词保留了希腊语的形态：某物被放在推理的下方并留在那里，论证则站在它上面。

senses.title: Everyday conjecture: an unproved guess
senses.titleCN: 日常猜想：未经证实的推测
senses.definition: a guess or suggestion offered without enough evidence, in ordinary speech
senses.definitionCN: 日常言谈中在证据不足时提出的猜测或设想
senses.example: My hypothesis is that the keys are still in the car.
senses.exampleCN: 我猜钥匙还在车里。
senses.why: The scientific word has loosened into daily use: any explanation put forward before proof counts as a hypothesis, even when no experiment will follow.
senses.whyCN: 这个科学词已经松动到日常用法里：任何在证实之前提出的解释都算假设，即使后面并不会做实验。

senses.title: Working hypothesis: a temporary guide
senses.titleCN: 工作假设：临时的行动依据
senses.definition: a provisional explanation accepted for the time being because it guides investigation, even if it may later be replaced
senses.definitionCN: 因能指导调查而暂时接受的解释，即使以后可能被替换
senses.example: As a working hypothesis, we assume the leak comes from the north pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 作为工作假设，我们先假定泄漏来自北侧管道。
senses.why: A foundation can be temporary. The working hypothesis is laid down not because it is proved, but because building can start on it today.
senses.whyCN: 地基可以是临时的。工作假设之所以被铺下，不是因为它已被证明，而是因为今天就能在它上面开工。

senses.title: Statistics: the null hypothesis
senses.definition: in statistics, the default proposition that there is no effect or no difference, which a test tries to reject
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中默认“没有效应、没有差异”的命题，检验试图将它推翻
senses.example: The null hypothesis states that the two groups perform equally well.
senses.exampleCN: 原假设称两组表现同样好。
senses.why: Here the word is used backwards: the hypothesis laid underneath the test is the dull one, and the whole apparatus is built to knock it down.
senses.whyCN: 这里的用法是反向的：垫在检验下面的假设是最平淡的那一个，整套装置却是为了把它推倒而搭起来的。

senses.title: Plural hypotheses: rival explanations
senses.titleCN: 复数假说：并排的候选解释
senses.definition: the plural form hypotheses, used when several candidate explanations are held side by side
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式 hypotheses，用于同时持有多个候选解释时
senses.example: The team listed three hypotheses and designed one test to separate them.
senses.exampleCN: 团队列出三个假说，并设计了一项能区分它们的检验。
senses.why: The Greek plural keeps the original -is to -es shift. Once several foundations are laid, the question is which one the evidence will stand on.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语式复数保留了 -is 变 -es 的变化。一旦铺下好几块地基，问题就变成证据会站在哪一块上。

senses.title: Mathematics: a conjecture awaiting proof
senses.definition: in mathematics, a statement believed to be true but not yet proved, such as a named conjecture
senses.definitionCN: 数学中相信为真但尚未证明的陈述，如以人名命名的猜想
senses.example: The Riemann hypothesis has resisted proof for more than a century.
senses.exampleCN: 黎曼猜想已有一个多世纪未能被证明。
senses.why: The mathematical hypothesis is a foundation laid under a whole building that does not yet exist: if it holds, a large structure of proofs can be raised.
senses.whyCN: 数学猜想是垫在一整座尚未存在的建筑下面的地基：只要它成立，一大片证明就能被垒起来。

senses.title: On the hypothesis that: a supposition for argument
senses.titleCN: 以假设为前提：为了推论而假定
senses.definition: in the phrase 'on the hypothesis that', used to grant a supposition temporarily and then reason from it
senses.definitionCN: 在短语 on the hypothesis that 中，暂时承认某一设想并由此推理
senses.example: On the hypothesis that demand stays flat, the new factory would still lose money.
senses.exampleCN: 假定需求保持不变，新工厂仍然会亏损。
senses.why: The phrase marks the foundation being laid on purpose: everyone agrees to stand on it for the length of the argument, and no longer.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语标记的是有意铺下的地基：大家同意在论证期间站上去，论证一结束就不再站了。

senses.title: Original sense: a groundwork
senses.definition: in the earliest English use, a particular statement or groundwork on which other statements rest
senses.definitionCN: 在最早的英语用法中，指承载其他陈述的某一说法或基础
senses.example: The old logic text calls the first principle the hypothesis of the whole argument.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧逻辑教材把第一原理称为整个论证的基础。
senses.why: Greek hypothesis literally meant 'a placing under', the base or groundwork of a building. The logical sense grew from that physical picture.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 hypothesis 字面意为“放在下面”，即建筑的地基或底座。逻辑义正是从这幅物理画面长出来的。

intro.en: Hypothesis is a Greek word borrowed through French and Latin, and its parts are still visible: hypo- 'under' plus thesis 'a placing'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hypothesis 是经法语和拉丁语借入的希腊词，构词成分至今可见：hypo-“在下”加 thesis“放置”。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'a particular statement'. The word entered through French hypothese and directly from Late Latin hypothesis.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 16 世纪 90 年代，意为“某一具体陈述”。这个词经法语 hypothese 并直接由晚期拉丁语 hypothesis 进入英语。

items.en: The sense 'a proposition assumed and taken for granted, used as a premise' is recorded, the sense that still governs logic and argument.
items.cn: 记录到“被假定并视为当然、用作前提的命题”这一义项，这也是至今支配逻辑与论证的义项。

items.en: Greek hypothesis meant 'base, groundwork, foundation', and in extended use 'basis of an argument, supposition', literally 'a placing under'.
items.cn: 希腊语 hypothesis 意为“底座、地基、基础”，引申为“论证的基础、设想”，字面即“放在下面”。

items.en: The word joins hypo- 'under' and thesis 'a placing, proposition'. Thesis goes back to a reduplicated form of PIE *dhe- 'to set, put', the root also behind do, deed, and theme.
items.cn: 这个词由 hypo-“在下”与 thesis“放置、命题”组合而成。thesis 可追溯到原始印欧语 *dhe-“放置、安放”的重复形式，该词根也是 do、deed、theme 的来源。

items.en: The narrower scientific sense, an explanation to be tested, is recorded. From this point the word belongs to experiment as much as to logic.
items.cn: 较窄的科学义“待检验的解释”有记录。自此这个词既属于逻辑，也属于实验。

items.en: The Greek plural hypotheses is kept unchanged, unlike most English nouns. Hypothetical (1580s) and hypothesize (1738) build the rest of the family; theory and thesis remain distinct neighbours.
items.cn: 希腊语式复数 hypotheses 原样保留，与大多数英语名词不同。hypothetical（16 世纪 80 年代）与 hypothesize（1738）补足了词族；theory 与 thesis 仍是各自独立的邻词。

note.en: The first group separates the plural, the adjective, and the verb built on hypothesis; the second group compares words for explanations and for premises.
note.cn: 第一组把复数、形容词和由 hypothesis 构成的动词分开；第二组比较表示“解释”与“前提”的词。

entries.definition: the plural of hypothesis, not a different word. Greek nouns in -is regularly become -es, so one hypothesis becomes two hypotheses.
entries.definitionCN: hypothesis 的复数，不是另一个词。以 -is 结尾的希腊语名词通常变 -es，所以一个假说变成两个假说。

entries.definition: based on a hypothesis or imagined for the sake of argument. It describes a situation, not a scientific claim, and is often close to 'imaginary'.
entries.definitionCN: 基于假设的，或为论证而设想的。它描述一种情形，而不是一条科学主张，常接近“虚构的”。

entries.definition: to form a hypothesis. The verb names the act of laying the foundation; the noun names the foundation itself.
entries.definitionCN: 提出假说。动词命名“铺地基”的动作，名词命名地基本身。

entries.definition: a coherent set of principles that explains a broad class of facts. A theory is a finished building; a hypothesis is the foundation stone laid before the building is tested.
entries.definitionCN: 解释一大类事实的连贯原理体系。theory 是建成的房屋；hypothesis 是房屋受检前铺下的奠基石。

entries.definition: a proposition put forward and defended in argument, or a long research essay. It shares Greek thesis 'a placing' with hypothesis, but stands on its own rather than under something else.
entries.definitionCN: 在论证中提出并加以辩护的命题，或长篇研究论文。它与 hypothesis 共享希腊语 thesis“放置”，但它是自己站着的，而不是垫在别物之下。

entries.definition: something assumed to be true for the sake of reasoning. It is a near translation of Greek hypothesis and carries less scientific weight.
entries.definitionCN: 为推理而假定为真的事。它几乎是希腊语 hypothesis 的译法，科学分量更轻。

entries.definition: an opinion formed from incomplete evidence. A conjecture is openly a guess; a hypothesis is a guess set up so that it can be tested.
entries.definitionCN: 根据不完整证据形成的看法。conjecture 明说是猜测；hypothesis 则是为了让其可被检验而搭起来的猜测。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: hypo- 'under', thesis 'a placing', the Greek plural hypotheses, and the family hypothetical / hypothesize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：hypo-“在下”、thesis“放置”、希腊语式复数 hypotheses，以及 hypothetical／hypothesize 词族。

normal.en: hypo- means 'under' and thesis means 'a placing'. A hypothesis is something placed under a question so that reasoning can stand on it.
normal.cn: hypo- 表示“在下”，thesis 表示“放置”。hypothesis 就是被放在问题下面、让推理可以站上去的东西。

normal.en: The plural is hypotheses, not hypothesises: Greek -is becomes -es, as in analysis and basis.
normal.cn: 复数是 hypotheses，不是 hypothesises：希腊语式 -is 变 -es，如 analysis、basis 一样。

normal.en: Hypothetical means 'assumed for the sake of argument', and hypothesize means 'to lay that foundation down'.
normal.cn: hypothetical 意为“为论证而假设的”，hypothesize 意为“把这块地基铺下去”。

normal.en: A hypothesis and a thesis share thesis 'a placing', but a thesis stands up to be defended while a hypothesis lies underneath to be tested.
normal.cn: hypothesis 与 thesis 共享 thesis“放置”，但 thesis 立起来供人辩护，hypothesis 则躺在下面等着被检验。

normal.en: The null hypothesis is the dull foundation: it says there is no effect, and the experiment is built to knock it down.
normal.cn: 原假设是最平淡的地基：它宣称没有效应，而实验正是为了把它推倒而搭起来的。

abstract.en: Picture a stone slab laid in soft ground. Nothing is built yet, and the slab may sink or hold, but every later brick depends on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石板被铺进软土里。上面还没有建筑，石板可能下沉也可能撑住，但后来的每一块砖都依赖它。

abstract.en: A hypothesis is a bet you can lose: the good ones are laid where a test can reach them, not where they are safe from evidence.
abstract.cn: 假说是一场你可以输掉的赌：好的假说被铺在检验够得着的地方，而不是铺在证据碰不到的安全角落。

abstract.en: When several foundations lie side by side, the experiment is not looking for support but for separation: which slab alone can carry the building?
abstract.cn: 当好几块地基并排铺着，实验要找的不是支撑而是区分：哪一块独自能承起这座建筑？

examples.en: Every experiment begins with a hypothesis, but few survive the first week.
examples.cn: 每个实验都从一个假说开始，但很少有假说能熬过第一周。

examples.en: She treated the rumour as a working hypothesis and went to check the records.
examples.cn: 她把这个传闻当作工作假设，然后去查记录。

examples.en: The two hypotheses predict different results, which is exactly why the test is worth running.
examples.cn: 两个假说预测出不同的结果，这正是这项检验值得做的原因。

dict_mnemonic.text: “嗨，破塞西斯”——嗨，先破开地面、塞一块石板在下面当底座，上面再放待验的想法 → hypothesis 假设、前提

root: 源自希腊语 hypothesis“垫在下面的地基”，由 hypo-“在下”+ thesis“放置”构成，核心是“先垫一块地基，让论点立在上面”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of hypothesis, all from one gesture: something is placed underneath — a question, an argument, a test, a proof — so that reasoning can stand on it and later be knocked down.
sensesIntro.cn: hypothesis 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：把某物垫在下面——问题、论证、检验、证明——让推理站上去，并在以后被推倒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slab laid under a structure that is still to be built and tested.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块石板铺在尚待建造、尚待检验的结构之下。

branches.en: TESTABLE CLAIMS: science and mathematics lay a claim underneath and then try to break it with evidence or proof.
branches.cn: 可检验的主张：科学与数学把一条主张垫在下面，再用证据或证明去击打它。

branches.en: FOUNDATION: logic, argumentative supposition, and the oldest sense all keep the literal groundwork.
branches.cn: 地基：逻辑前提、论证中的假定与最古老的义项，都保留了字面上的“垫在下面”。

branches.en: GUESS AND TOOL: daily conjecture has no test attached, while a working hypothesis is laid down so that work can start today.
branches.cn: 猜想与工具：日常猜测后面没有检验，而工作假设被铺下是为了今天就能开工。

branches.en: STATISTICS: the null hypothesis is the plain foundation that the whole test is built to demolish.
branches.cn: 统计学：原假设是最朴素的地基，整套检验却是为了拆掉它而建。

branches.en: RIVALS: several hypotheses stand side by side, and the evidence must choose which slab to stand on.
branches.cn: 竞争者：多个假说并排而立，证据必须选择站上哪一块石板。

intro.en: Hypothesis is a Greek compound borrowed whole: hypo- 'under' plus thesis 'a placing'. English adds -ical, -ly, and -ize, and the same two Greek pieces build a large family.
intro.cn: hypothesis 是整体借入的希腊语复合词：hypo-“在下”加 thesis“放置”。英语加上 -ical、-ly、-ize，同样两个希腊成分还构成一大群词。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin took the Greek word unchanged as hypothesis, and Latin thesis came from the same Greek noun. Medieval Latin suppositio was used to translate hypothesis, which is why supposition still feels like its twin.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语原样吸收了希腊词 hypothesis，拉丁语 thesis 也来自同一个希腊名词。中世纪拉丁语用 suppositio 翻译 hypothesis，所以 supposition 至今像是它的双胞胎。

items.meaning: a proposition placed under an argument; a testable explanation
items.meaningCN: 垫在论证下面的命题；可检验的解释（hypo- 在下 + thesis 放置）
items.example: The hypothesis was rejected after the second trial.
items.exampleCN: 第二次试验之后，这个假说被否定了。

items.meaningCN: 两个或更多假说（希腊语式复数 -es）
items.example: Both hypotheses assume the same starting temperature.
items.exampleCN: 两个假说都假定相同的初始温度。

items.meaning: based on a hypothesis; imagined for argument
items.meaningCN: 假设的；为论证而假想的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: Consider a hypothetical case in which no one answers.
items.exampleCN: 设想一个无人应答的假想情形。

items.meaning: in an assumed or imagined situation
items.meaningCN: 在假设或假想的情况下（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Hypothetically, the plan could work if costs fell.
items.exampleCN: 假定成本下降，这个计划理论上可行。

items.meaningCN: 提出假说（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: Researchers hypothesize that the sound guides the fish home.
items.exampleCN: 研究者假设这种声音能引导鱼回到出生地。

items.meaning: under the skin, as an injection
items.meaningCN: 皮下的（如皮下注射；hypo- 在下 + derma 皮肤）
items.example: The nurse prepared a hypodermic needle.
items.exampleCN: 护士准备好了一支皮下注射针。

items.meaning: a body temperature dangerously below normal
items.meaningCN: 低体温；体温过低（hypo- 在下 + therme 热）
items.example: The climbers were treated for hypothermia.
items.exampleCN: 登山者接受了低体温治疗。

items.meaning: a proposition to be defended; a long research essay
items.meaningCN: 待辩护的命题；长篇研究论文（希腊语“放置、命题”）
items.example: Her thesis argues that the two reforms were one process.
items.exampleCN: 她的论文主张这两场改革其实是一个过程。

items.meaning: the direct opposite of a proposition
items.meaningCN: 对立命题；正相反的说法（anti- 反对 + thesis 放置）
items.example: His calm manner is the antithesis of her urgency.
items.exampleCN: 他的从容正是她那种急切的对照。

items.meaning: a putting together of parts into a whole
items.meaningCN: 综合；合成（syn- 一起 + thesis 放置）
items.example: The book is a synthesis of history and economics.
items.exampleCN: 这本书是历史学与经济学的综合。

items.meaning: a phrase placed beside the main sentence; a bracket
items.meaningCN: 插入语；圆括号（para- 旁 + en- 内 + thesis 放置）
items.example: The date appears in parentheses at the end.
items.exampleCN: 日期放在末尾的圆括号里。

latinEntries.meaning: base, groundwork; basis of an argument
latinEntries.meaningCN: 地基、基础；论证的依据（晚期拉丁语原样借入）

latinEntries.structure: Greek thesis, from PIE *dhe- 'to set, put'

latinEntries.meaning: a putting under; assumption, used to translate Greek hypothesis
latinEntries.meaningCN: 放在下面；假定（中世纪拉丁语用来翻译希腊语 hypothesis）

definition_zh: 先于；居先；在前发生
definition_en: to go or come before something in time, order, or rank
core_image: 一个人走在队伍最前面，后面的人还没迈步
scene: 长队排到门口，领队的人已经推门走了进去。 The opening speech antecedes the award ceremony by half an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 antecede 是「先于、居先」（第 1 个义项：在时间或顺序上走在前面）；句意为开场致辞比颁奖典礼早半小时进行。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ent 名词后缀构成，义为「前情；先例；先行词」
由本词加 -ence 构成，义为「居先；先例」
同族词，义为「早于；把日期填早」

senses.title: To go before in time or order
senses.definition: to happen, exist, or come earlier than something else in time or sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在时间或顺序上比另一事物更早发生、存在或出现
senses.example: The unrest anteceded the official announcement by several months.
senses.exampleCN: 骚动比官方公告早了几个月出现。
senses.why: The Latin prefix ante- means 'before' and cedere means 'to go', so the word literally pictures one thing walking ahead of another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁前缀 ante- 表示「在前」，cedere 表示「走」，所以这个词的字面画面就是一物走在另一物前面。

senses.title: To precede in rank or position
senses.definition: to rank or be placed before someone else in order of importance or position
senses.definitionCN: 在重要程度或位次上排在他人之前
senses.example: The vice president antecedes all other officers in the procession.
senses.exampleCN: 游行队伍中副总裁的位次排在其他官员之前。
senses.why: Walking ahead of someone in a line became the image of standing higher in rank, since leaders lead the column.
senses.whyCN: 在队伍里走在别人前面，被引申为地位更高，因为领头的人总是走在最前面。

intro.en: Antecede is built from Latin ante 'before' and cedere 'to go', a combination Latin itself used in antecedere.
intro.cn: antecede 由拉丁语 ante「在前」与 cedere「走」构成，拉丁语本身就有 antecedere 这个组合。

items.en: The root *ked- meant 'to go, yield', and it also produced the English word cede.
items.cn: 词根 *ked- 意为「走、让步」，它同时生出了英语的 cede。

items.en: The preposition ante meant 'before, in front of', both in space and in time.
items.cn: 介词 ante 意为「在……之前」，既指空间也指时间。

items.en: Latin combined the two parts into antecedere, 'to go before, precede in time or rank'.
items.cn: 拉丁语把两个成分合成 antecedere，意为「走在前面，在时间或级别上居先」。

items.en: English borrowed the verb from Latin in the sixteenth century, largely in formal and scholarly writing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪从拉丁语借入这个动词，主要用于正式与学术文字。

items.en: Today antecede is rare; its noun and adjective relatives antecedent and antecedence carry most of the load.
items.cn: 如今 antecede 已较少见；它派生的名词与形容词 antecedent 和 antecedence 承担了大部分用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the close family of the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of coming first.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干的近亲；近义组收各种「走在前面」的动词。

entries.definition: A noun or adjective for something that comes before, especially a cause or the word a pronoun refers to.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「先前的；前情；先行词」，指在先的事物或代词所指的对象。

entries.definition: The fact of going before; priority in time or order.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「居先；先例」，指在时间或顺序上的领先。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to be earlier than something, or to put an earlier date on a document.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「早于；把日期填早」，与 antecede 同根但更常用。

entries.definition: The common verb for coming before something in time, order, or position.
entries.definitionCN: 常用动词，义为「先于；在……之前」，覆盖时间、顺序与位置。

entries.definition: To be a sign of something before it happens.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「预示；是……的先兆」，强调提前给出信号。

entries.definition: A formal word meaning to go before, often confused with forgo 'to do without'.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用词，义为「走在前面」，常与拼形相近的 forgo「放弃」混淆。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two Latin halves and the family of antecedent words that carry the same stem.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用两个拉丁语成分，以及共享同一词干的 antecedent 词族。

normal.en: ante plus cede: going before, exactly like precede with a different prefix.
normal.cn: ante 加 cede：走在前面，和 precede 只是前缀不同。

normal.en: The cede root also gives concede, recede, and proceed, all about going.
normal.cn: cede 词根还生出 concede、recede、proceed，都与「走」有关。

normal.en: Ante- marks 'before' in antechamber, ante meridiem, and ante bellum.
normal.cn: ante- 在 antechamber、ante meridiem、ante bellum 中都表示「在前」。

normal.en: The noun antecedent is far more common than the verb itself.
normal.cn: 名词 antecedent 远比动词本身常用。

normal.en: Grammar uses antecedent for the noun a pronoun points back to.
normal.cn: 语法里 antecedent 指代词回指的那个名词。

abstract.en: Picture a scout walking ten steps ahead of the column on a narrow path.
abstract.cn: 想象侦察兵在窄路上走在队伍前十步。

abstract.en: Picture yesterday's footprints already on the sand before anyone arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象沙滩上早已留好、先于来人的脚印。

abstract.en: Picture the opening credits rolling before the first scene.
abstract.cn: 想象正片第一幕之前先滚出的片头字幕。

examples.en: Folk tales about the flood antecede the first written records.
examples.cn: 关于洪水的民间传说早于最早的文字记载。

examples.en: Years of tension anteceded the formal breakup of the alliance.
examples.cn: 多年的紧张关系先于联盟的正式解体。

examples.en: The mayor's speech antecedes the ribbon cutting.
examples.cn: 市长讲话之后才剪彩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安梯细的」——他安了梯子先细细走在前面，后面的人跟着上，就是「先于」

root: 拉丁语 ante（在前）+ cedere（走）→ antecedere（走在前面）；进入英语后保留「先于、居先」之义，同根词 precede、recede、concede 都围绕「走」的核心意象。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses grow from one image of going ahead: arriving earlier in time, and standing ahead in rank.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项由「走在前面」这一意象长出：时间上先到，位次上居前。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one thing walking ahead of another on the same road
core.cn: 核心意象：在同一道路上，一物走在另一物之前

branches.en: The temporal line: one event walks ahead of another on the calendar.
branches.cn: 时间线：一个事件在日历上走在另一个之前。

branches.en: The rank line: walking ahead of the column becomes standing above it.
branches.cn: 位次线：走在队伍前面变成站在队伍之上。

branches.en: The cause line: what antecedes is often read as what causes.
branches.cn: 因果线：先发生的事常被解读为原因。

branches.en: Both senses share the front position, whether in time or in line.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享「前排位置」，无论在时间上还是在队伍里。

branches.en: The prehistory line: customs anteceding records point to an unrecorded past.
branches.cn: 史前线：早于记载的习俗指向无文字的过去。

intro.en: The word is a clean Latin compound: the prefix ante- on the verb stem cede-, with regular English endings.
intro.cn: 这个词是干净的拉丁复合词：前缀 ante- 加在动词词干 cede- 上，再带规则的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is the cedere group, one of the most productive verb families in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词族是 cedere 一族，它是英语里最高产的动词家族之一。

items.example: It supplies the 'before' in antecede.
items.exampleCN: 它为 antecede 提供「在前」的意思。

items.example: It supplies the 'go' in antecede.
items.exampleCN: 它为 antecede 提供「走」的意思。

items.meaningCN: 来自拉丁 -ere 的动词词尾
items.example: It forms antecede itself.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 antecede 本身。

items.example: It forms anteceded.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 anteceded。

items.example: It forms anteceding.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 anteceding。

items.meaning: one that, or being in a state
items.example: It forms antecedent.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 antecedent。

items.example: It forms antecedence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 antecedence。

items.example: It forms precede, the common synonym.
items.exampleCN: 它构成常用近义词 precede。

items.example: It forms recede, to go back.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 recede，即后退。

latinEntries.example: It is the stem of antecedere.
It is the direct source of antecede.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 antecede 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: It stands behind the English antecedent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是英语 antecedent 的来源。

definition_zh: 单项胜任力；技能项；能力标准
definition_en: a single named skill or behaviour standard that a role or course requires, treated as one item in a list
core_image: 一张能力清单钉在墙上，每一项后面都留着一格待勾的方框
scene: 招聘主管把岗位拆成若干可教可查的能力项，逐条写进面试评分表。 The hiring panel scored each competency separately.
sceneCN: 招聘主管把岗位拆成可教可查的能力项写进评分表；句中的 competency 指「清单中的单项能力标准」（第 1 个义项：可单独培训与检验的技能项）。图中可辨识物件：能力清单、勾选框、面试评分表、笔。

pos.zh: 单项胜任力；技能项；能力标准

senses.title: A named skill in a list
senses.definition: one skill or behaviour, written down so that it can be taught and checked
senses.definitionCN: 一项可写下、可教、可查的技能或行为
senses.example: The hiring panel scored each competency separately.
senses.exampleCN: 招聘小组对每一项能力分别评分。
senses.why: competency is the countable form: competence is the general fitness, while one competency is a single item that can be named.
senses.whyCN: competency 是可数形式：competence 指整体的胜任，competency 指一项可以命名的条目。

senses.title: An item in a human-resources framework
senses.titleCN: 人力资源框架中的一项
senses.definition: a standard entry in a framework used for hiring, review and promotion
senses.definitionCN: 用于招聘、评议与晋升的框架中的标准条目
senses.example: The new competency framework lists twelve items for managers.
senses.exampleCN: 新的能力框架为管理者列出十二项。
senses.why: human resources turned the word into an inventory item, because a framework needs countable pieces rather than a vague quality.
senses.whyCN: 人力资源把这个词变成库存条目，因为框架需要可数的部件，而非一种模糊的品质。

senses.title: A core competency of a firm
senses.definition: one capability a company treats as central to its strategy
senses.definitionCN: 企业视为战略核心的一项能力
senses.example: Designing quiet engines is the firm's core competency.
senses.exampleCN: 设计安静的发动机是这家公司的核心能力。
senses.why: strategy borrowed the countable form because a firm must choose a few capabilities to be known for.
senses.whyCN: 战略领域借用这个可数形式，因为企业必须选定少数几项能力来立身。

senses.title: Legal capacity, in variant spelling
senses.titleCN: 法律上的资格（异体拼写）
senses.definition: the legal power to act, in the older spelling that still appears in some jurisdictions
senses.definitionCN: 行动的法律权力，这一较旧拼写仍见于部分司法辖区
senses.example: The document uses competency for the court's power to act.
senses.exampleCN: 这份文件用 competency 指法院的行动权力。
senses.why: the two spellings overlap here, so a legal text may use the countable-looking form for the uncountable idea.
senses.whyCN: 两种拼写在此时重叠，因此法律文本可能用看似可数的形式表达不可数的概念。

senses.title: Demonstrated skill in assessment
senses.definition: a skill shown to an assessor through a task, not merely claimed on a form
senses.definitionCN: 通过任务向评估者证明的技能，而非仅在表格上宣称
senses.example: Candidates must demonstrate each competency in a simulated shift.
senses.exampleCN: 候选人须在模拟班次中证明每一项能力。
senses.why: assessment joins the word to proof: a competency is not possessed until it has been shown doing something.
senses.whyCN: 评估把词与证据接上：一项能力在被做出来之前不算拥有。

senses.title: A teaching or clinical requirement
senses.titleCN: 教学或临床的能力要求
senses.definition: a skill that a training programme requires before a learner may progress
senses.definitionCN: 培训项目要求学习者在进阶前必须掌握的一项技能
senses.example: The nursing course certifies competency in wound care.
senses.exampleCN: 护理课程对伤口护理的能力予以认证。
senses.why: training programmes need milestones, so each competency becomes a gate a learner must pass.
senses.whyCN: 培训项目需要里程碑，于是每项能力都成为学习者必须通过的一道门。

senses.title: A behavioural model item
senses.definition: a described pattern of behaviour, such as listening or giving feedback
senses.definitionCN: 被描述出来的一类行为模式，如倾听或给出反馈
senses.example: The leadership model includes the competency of giving clear feedback.
senses.exampleCN: 领导力模型包含「给出清晰反馈」这一能力项。
senses.why: when the item is behavioural, the standard describes what a person does, not only what a person knows.
senses.whyCN: 当条目属于行为时，标准描述的是人做什么，而不只是人知道什么。

senses.title: A minimum standard for a stage
senses.definition: the threshold skill a pupil must reach before moving on
senses.definitionCN: 学生进阶前必须达到的门槛技能
senses.example: The district set a minimum competency in reading for each grade.
senses.exampleCN: 该学区为每个年级设定了阅读的最低能力标准。
senses.why: education uses the countable form for a floor: a competency is something a learner either has or lacks at a given stage.
senses.whyCN: 教育领域用可数形式表示地板：一项能力在学习者的某一阶段，要么具备，要么不具备。

intro.en: Competency is the countable branch of competence, built the same way from Latin competere 'to meet, be suitable', through the participle competens and the English suffix -ency. Its modern list sense grew in management and education. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: competency 是 competence 的可数分支，同样来自拉丁 competere「相遇、适合」，经分词 competens 与英语中的名词后缀构成。其现代「清单条目」义在管理学与教育领域发展出来。年代为约数。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus petere 'to seek' gave competere 'to meet, be suitable, be sufficient'.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 petere「寻求」给出 competere「相遇、适合、足够」。

items.en: The noun competentia named a meeting or a correspondence, the fit between two things.
items.cn: 名词 competentia 指相遇或对应，即两物之间的相合。

items.en: English competence appeared in the sixteenth century for ability and authority, an uncountable quality.
items.cn: 英语 competence 于十六世纪出现，指能力与权限，是不可数的品质。

items.en: The spelling competency developed as a parallel form; from the nineteenth century it increasingly named a specific capacity that could be listed.
items.cn: competency 这一拼写作为并行形式发展；从十九世纪起，它越来越多地指可被列出的一项具体能力。

items.en: In the twentieth century human resources and competency-based education made the word countable in earnest, so each skill became one item on a framework.
items.cn: 二十世纪，人力资源与「基于能力的教育」让这个词真正可数，每项技能成为框架中的一条。

items.en: The reason the -ency spelling became the countable one is not fully documented; the split is conventional rather than logical. The deeper origin of petere remains uncertain, and forms offered for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 为何是这一拼写承担可数义，缺乏完整记录；这一分工属约定俗成而非逻辑必然。petere 的更早来源仍不确定，为其给出的形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the two spellings that are often confused and the adjective behind them; group two holds words for skills and proof, each with a different unit.
note.cn: 第一组是常被混淆的两种拼写及其背后的形容词；第二组是技能与证明类词，计量单位各不相同。

entries.definition: The general ability or legal authority; it does not normally name one item in a list.
entries.definitionCN: 指整体能力或法定权限；通常不指清单中的某一项。

entries.definition: Describes a person who meets the standard; competency is the item being measured.
entries.definitionCN: 描述达到标准的人；competency 是被测量的条目。

entries.definition: A contest for one prize, from the same verb but with no sense of a skill item.
entries.definitionCN: 指争一奖的竞赛，同出该动词，却毫无「技能项」之意。

entries.definition: The lack of general ability, an uncountable judgement rather than a listed item.
entries.definitionCN: 指缺乏整体能力，是不可数的判断而非清单条目。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a learned ability; a competency is a skill written as an assessable standard.
entries.definitionCN: 指学成的能力，是日常词；competency 是被写成可评估标准的技能。

entries.definition: Often a broader capacity of a person or system, not necessarily certified.
entries.definitionCN: 常指人或系统更宽的容量，未必经认证。

entries.definition: The certificate or training that proves suitability; a competency is the ability itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指证明适合的证书或训练；competency 是能力本身。

entries.definition: A required level of quality; a competency is one such standard tied to a skill.
entries.definitionCN: 指要求的质量水平；competency 是与某项技能绑定的这样一条标准。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the real countable split, the real management use and the real education use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自真实的可数分工、真实的管理用法与真实的教育用法。

normal.en: competence is the whole; one competency is one item on the list.
normal.cn: competence 是整体；一项 competency 是清单上的一条。

normal.en: com- 'together' plus petere 'seek': a person and a task meeting.
normal.cn: com-「共同」加 petere「寻求」：人与任务相遇。

normal.en: Human resources made it countable: a framework of named items.
normal.cn: 人力资源让它可数：一份由具名条目组成的框架。

normal.en: Education made it a gate: a minimum competency per stage.
normal.cn: 教育把它变成一道门：每个阶段的最低能力。

normal.en: The adjective stays competent; only the noun splits.
normal.cn: 形容词仍是 competent；只有名词发生分工。

abstract.en: Picture a wall chart of boxes, every box waiting for a tick.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上挂着一张方格表，每格都等着打勾。

abstract.en: Picture a job interview reduced to twelve lines and a score beside each.
abstract.cn: 想象一场面试被压缩成十二行，每行旁边一个分数。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder with a name written at every rung.
abstract.cn: 想象一把梯子，每一级都写着名字。

examples.en: The competency framework is reviewed every three years.
examples.cn: 这套能力框架每三年复审一次。

examples.en: Each competency must be demonstrated in a real setting.
examples.cn: 每项能力都须在真实场景中证明。

examples.en: Innovation is treated as a core competency of the group.
examples.cn: 创新被视为该集团的核心能力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「competent（能胜任的）+ cy」——把「能胜任」拆成一条条可勾选的项 → 技能项、能力标准

root: 拉丁 com-「共同」+ petere「寻求」→ competere「相遇、适合」→ competentia／competens → 英语 competence；其可数分支写作 competency，十九世纪后渐指可列出的单项能力。petere 的更早来源不确定，相关形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe one list: a general fitness is cut into named items, and each item is then used for hiring, for a framework, for strategy, for legal capacity, for proof in assessment, for a training gate, for a behaviour model and for a minimum stage standard.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述的是一张清单：整体胜任力被切成具名条目，每条随后用于招聘、框架、战略、法律资格、评估证明、培训门坎、行为模型与阶段最低标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall chart of named boxes, each waiting for a tick, each tickable only after it has been shown.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上挂着一张具名方格表，每格都等着打勾，而每一勾都只能在证明之后落下。

branches.en: THE ITEM: ability becomes countable, and the count becomes a human-resources framework.
branches.cn: 条目：能力变得可数，计数又变成人力资源框架。

branches.en: STRATEGY: a firm chooses a few items to be known for.
branches.cn: 战略：企业选定少数几条来立身。

branches.en: LAW: the older spelling survives in legal texts for power to act.
branches.cn: 法律：较旧的拼写留存于法律文本，指行动权力。

branches.en: PROOF AND TRAINING: an item counts only when shown, and training makes each item a gate.
branches.cn: 证明与培训：条目只有被做出才作数，培训又把每条变成一道门。

branches.en: BEHAVIOUR AND FLOOR: items can describe what a person does, and can set the minimum for a stage.
branches.cn: 行为与地板：条目可以描述人做什么，也可以设定阶段的下限。

intro.en: The noun is the countable branch of a Latin verb family, and its pieces still read clearly: a prefix, a root and a state suffix.
intro.cn: 这个名词是一个拉丁动词词族的可数分支，其部件至今读得清楚：一个前缀、一个词根与一个表状态的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Com- and petere build competere; competens gives the adjective, and the -ency suffix gives the countable noun.
latinIntro.cn: com- 与 petere 构成 competere；competens 给出形容词，名词后缀给出可数名词。

items.example: The prefix joins the two sides.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀连接两方。

items.example: Petere is the shared root.
items.exampleCN: petere 是共享词根。

items.example: Competere is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: competere 是基础动词。

items.example: Competens gives the adjective.
items.exampleCN: competens 给出形容词。

items.example: Competence is the uncountable form.
items.exampleCN: competence 是不可数形式。

items.example: Competency is the countable branch.
items.exampleCN: competency 是可数分支。

items.example: The list has twelve competencies.
items.exampleCN: 清单上有十二项能力。

items.example: The adjective serves both nouns.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词服务两个名词。

items.example: He acted competently.
items.exampleCN: 他行事称职。

definition_zh: 气质；性情；易激动的脾性；气质类型说；平均律（音乐）
definition_en: the usual temper of a person or animal, or the tuning of an instrument to a settled system
core_image: 四种不同温度的水倒进同一只杯子，杯子不变，杯里的冷热却决定了它适合装什么
scene: 同一个班里，一个孩子跌倒后自己爬起来继续跑，另一个要人抱很久才肯下地，老师记住了这两个名字。 Thirty years later the teacher still described them by temperament rather than by grades.
sceneCN: 这里 temperament 指「一个人天生而稳定的性情倾向」（第 1 个义项：稳定的人格气质）；句意是三十年后老师仍按性情、而不是按成绩来描述这两个人。图中可辨识物件：操场、自己爬起的孩子、被抱着的孩子。

derivatives.zh: 气质的；喜怒无常的；性能不稳定的

senses.title: A settled natural disposition
senses.definition: the usual balance of a person's nature, especially as it shows in how they react
senses.definitionCN: 一个人天性的通常配比，尤其体现在反应方式上
senses.example: The teacher described them by temperament rather than by grades.
senses.exampleCN: 老师按性情而不是按成绩来描述他们。
senses.why: the word began as a word for a due mixture, so it names a ratio inside a person that stays roughly the same across situations.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指「恰当的混合」，因此命名的是人体内一个在各种情境下大致不变的配比。

senses.title: A tendency to flare up
senses.definition: the part of a disposition that decides how quickly anger or excitement rises
senses.definitionCN: 决定愤怒或兴奋升起多快的那部分性情
senses.example: He has the temperament of a kettle that whistles early.
senses.exampleCN: 他的脾性像一只早早叫起来的水壶。
senses.why: heat is one of the oldest images in this word, which is why it so often appears with fiery or calm.
senses.whyCN: 「热」是这个词最古老的意象之一，因此它常与「火爆」或「沉静」连用。

senses.title: One of the four old types
senses.titleCN: 旧说中的四种类型之一
senses.definition: a category in the ancient theory that divided people by the balance of bodily humours
senses.definitionCN: 古代按体液配比给人分类的那套理论中的一个类别
senses.example: The four temperaments were once taught as medical fact.
senses.exampleCN: 四种气质类型曾被当作医学事实讲授。
senses.why: classical medicine explained character by the mixture of fluids in the body, and the word still carries that taxonomy.
senses.whyCN: 古典医学用体内液体的混合来解释性格，这个词至今带着那套分类。

senses.title: A system of tuning
senses.definition: a way of tuning instruments so that the notes stay in usable relations across keys
senses.definitionCN: 一种调音方式，使各音在各调之间保持可用的关系
senses.example: Equal temperament made the piano a flexible instrument.
senses.exampleCN: 十二平均律让钢琴成为一件灵活的乐器。
senses.why: in music the word keeps its literal sense of adjusting a mixture until it balances, applied here to intervals.
senses.whyCN: 在音乐里，这个词保留了「把混合调到平衡」的字面义，只是把对象换成了音程。

senses.title: An animal's handling
senses.titleCN: 动物的性子与好不好带
senses.definition: the disposition of an animal, especially as it affects how easily it can be worked with
senses.definitionCN: 动物的性情，尤其影响它好不好驾驭
senses.example: The breed is chosen for a steady temperament around children.
senses.exampleCN: 选这个品种，是因为它在孩子身边性子稳。
senses.why: the word applies wherever a creature has a fixed setting, which is why breeders use it like a specification.
senses.whyCN: 凡是有固定「设定」的生物都适用这个词，因此育种者拿它当规格来用。

senses.title: The temper of an age
senses.definition: the prevailing character of a period or a group, spoken of as if it were a person
senses.definitionCN: 某个时期或群体的主导性格，被当作一个人来说
senses.example: Historians speak of the temperament of the decade.
senses.exampleCN: 史学家会谈那十年的时代脾气。
senses.why: the metaphor of a body with balanced fluids transfers easily to a collective, which is how whole eras get a temper.
senses.whyCN: 「体内液体平衡」这一比喻很容易搬到集体上，整个时代于是有了脾气。

senses.title: The fit between parts
senses.definition: the working balance among mixed elements, as in a blend or an arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 混合成分之间起作用的配比，如调配或布局
senses.example: The garden's temperament comes from the ratio of stone to green.
senses.exampleCN: 这座园子的脾性来自石头与绿意的配比。
senses.why: this sense reaches back to the original meaning of a measured mixture and keeps the word's earliest image alive.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项回到「按量混合」的本义，让这个词最早的意象继续活着。

senses.title: A temperamental machine
senses.definition: the use of the derived adjective for equipment that works only when it feels like it
senses.definitionCN: 用其派生形容词指只在它高兴时才肯工作的设备
senses.example: The old press is temperamental in cold weather.
senses.exampleCN: 那台老印刷机天冷时脾气很坏。
senses.why: machines are described with this family because they are treated as having a disposition, which is the joke the usage rests on.
senses.whyCN: 机器被用这一词族来描述，是因为它们被当作有性情，这个用法正建立在这个玩笑上。

intro.en: Temperament comes from Latin temperamentum 'a due mixture', from temperare 'to mix in proportion, to moderate'. Classical medicine used it for the balance of bodily humours, and music borrowed it for the tuning of intervals. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: temperament 来自拉丁 temperamentum「恰当的混合」，出自 temperare「按比例调配、节制」。古典医学用它指体液配比，音乐则借它指音程的调校。年代均为约数。

items.en: Temperare meant 'to divide or mix in due proportion, to moderate'. A suggested link to tempus 'time' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: temperare 意为「按适当比例调和、节制」。有人认为它与意为「时间」的词有关，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: The noun named the resulting balance, first of climate and of bodily fluids, later of any mixture.
items.cn: 这个名词指混合后的平衡，先是气候与体液，后来是任何混合。

items.en: Greek and then Latin medicine explained health and character by four fluids, so temperament became a medical word for a person's constitutional balance.
items.cn: 希腊继而拉丁医学用四种液体解释健康与性格，于是 temperament 成为指个人体质配比的医学词。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth century for a person's habitual disposition, and the older medical theory faded while the word stayed.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入这个词，指一个人惯常的性情；旧医学理论衰落，词却留了下来。

items.en: From the seventeenth century musicians used it for the tuning of intervals, where a tempered system is one deliberately adjusted to balance.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起，音乐家用它指音程的调校，所谓「调律体系」就是刻意调整以求平衡的系统。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of temperare is a reconstruction, and the exact date of the musical use is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：temperare 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式，音乐义的确切年代也未定。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin verb of mixing, which differ sharply in meaning; group two holds the words for character that psychologists keep apart.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「调配」动词、意义却相差很远的词；第二组是心理学家刻意区分的性格词。

entries.definition: From the same Latin verb through a noun for a tempered state: it measures heat, not character, and the resemblance is purely historical.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个拉丁动词，经一个表调匀状态的名词而来：它量的是热度，不是性格，相似纯属历史同源。

entries.definition: The shorter relative: as a noun it means a tendency to anger, as a verb to soften or moderate something.
entries.definitionCN: 较短的亲属词：作名词指易怒的倾向，作动词指使变软或使缓和。

entries.definition: The adjective of restraint, used of climate, habits and speech; it describes moderation rather than an inborn balance.
entries.definitionCN: 指有节制的形容词，用于气候、习惯与言谈；它描述的是节制，而不是天生的配比。

entries.definition: Built on this noun: it can mean 'of temperament' but is used far more often for people or machines that change behaviour abruptly.
entries.definitionCN: 由本名词构成：可指「性情的」，但更常用于形容人或机器行为突然多变。

entries.definition: The total pattern of traits and behaviour built over a life; temperament is the part thought to be inborn and stable.
entries.definitionCN: 一生中形成的特质与行为的总格局；temperament 是其中被认为天生而稳定的那一部分。

entries.definition: A settled readiness to behave in a certain way; it is less biological in tone than temperament.
entries.definitionCN: 按某种方式行事的固定倾向；在语气上不如 temperament 那样带生理色彩。

entries.definition: The moral shape of a person, judged as strong or weak; temperament says nothing about virtue.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的道德形状，可评为坚强或软弱；temperament 与德行无关。

entries.definition: The everyday word for what someone is like by birth; it is broader and carries no theory of humours.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个人天生怎样的日常词；更宽，也不带任何体液理论。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin verb behind it means 'to mix in due proportion', so a temperament is a recipe that came out balanced.
normal.cn: 背后的拉丁动词意为「按比例调配」，因此气质就是一份调得刚好的配方。

normal.en: The family runs temperament, temperamental, temperamentally, temper, temperate, temperature.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 temperament、temperamental、temperamentally、temper、temperate、temperature。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: a calm temperament, by temperament, an artistic temperament.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：沉静的气质、就性情而言、艺术家的脾性。

normal.en: Equal temperament is the musical sense, where intervals are adjusted to balance.
normal.cn: 十二平均律是音乐义，那里音程被调校以求平衡。

normal.en: The four temperaments come from the old medicine of bodily humours.
normal.cn: 四种气质类型来自旧的体液医学。

abstract.en: Picture four cups of water at different temperatures poured into one glass.
abstract.cn: 想象四杯不同温度的水倒进同一只杯子。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle whose whistle comes at different moments for different owners.
abstract.cn: 想象一只水壶，对不同主人有不同的鸣叫时刻。

abstract.en: Picture a piano tuned so that every key agrees to compromise.
abstract.cn: 想象一架钢琴被调成每个键都同意让步。

examples.en: By temperament she is patient, though the work tests her daily.
examples.cn: 就性情而言她很有耐心，尽管这份工作每天在考验她。

examples.en: The two brothers share a temperament but not a vocabulary.
examples.cn: 两兄弟性情相同，说话方式却完全不同。

examples.en: Equal temperament allows a keyboard instrument to play in every key.
examples.cn: 十二平均律让键盘乐器能在所有调上演奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: temper（调和）+ ament（东西）——把身体里的冷热调成一配方 → 气质、性情

root: 拉丁 temperamentum「恰当的混合」，出自 temperare「按比例调配、节制」；古典医学用它指体液配比，音乐借它指调律。与表「时间」的词是否有联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a mixture is brought into balance, and that balance is then read as a person's settled nature, as heat, as one of four types, as a tuning system, as an animal's setting, as the temper of an age, as a ratio among parts and finally as a machine's whims.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：混合物被调到平衡，这个平衡依次被读作一个人稳定的天性、热度、四种类型之一、一套调律、动物的设定、一个时代的脾气、各部分之间的配比，最后是机器的任性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four waters at different temperatures poured into one glass, so the glass decides what it can hold.
core.cn: 核心意象：四杯不同温度的水倒进同一只杯子，杯子于是决定了它能装什么。

branches.en: THE RATIO AND ITS HEAT: the settled mixture first, then the question of how quickly it boils.
branches.cn: 配比与热度：先是定下来的混合，再是它多快沸腾。

branches.en: THE OLD TAXONOMY: the mixture turned into named types by classical medicine.
branches.cn: 旧的分类：古典医学把这种混合变成几个有名字的类型。

branches.en: BALANCE APPLIED TO SOUND: music adjusts intervals by the same logic of compromise.
branches.cn: 平衡用于声音：音乐用同一套让步的逻辑来调音程。

branches.en: SETTINGS EVERYWHERE: an animal's handling and a garden's ratio are the same idea read on other objects.
branches.cn: 各处的设定：动物的性子与园子的配比，是同一观念读在别的对象上。

branches.en: FROM AN AGE TO A MACHINE: collectives and equipment get a temper, and the metaphor stretches until it becomes a joke.
branches.cn: 从时代到机器：集体与设备都得到了脾气，比喻一路拉伸，直到成了玩笑。

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin verb of mixing plus a Latin noun-forming element, and the same pieces recur across a large family.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁「调配」动词加一个拉丁名词构词成分搭成，同样的成分反复出现在一大族词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin temperare gives temper, temperament, temperate and temperature, all through the idea of bringing something to a due measure.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 temperare 衍生 temper、temperament、temperate、temperature，全部经由「把某物调到适当的度」这一观念。

items.example: The verb supplies the idea of a measured mixture.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「按量混合」的意思。

items.meaning: means or result of an action
items.example: It turns the verb into the name of a resulting balance.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个动词变成调好之后的平衡的名称。

items.meaning: a due mixture, a balanced state
items.example: The noun first described climate and body fluids.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词最初描述气候与体液。

items.example: He has a calm temperament.
items.exampleCN: 他性情沉静。

items.example: The press is temperamental in winter.
items.exampleCN: 那台印刷机天冷时脾气很坏。

items.example: They are temperamentally unsuited.
items.exampleCN: 他们在性情上并不合适。

items.meaning: a tendency to anger; to moderate
items.example: He lost his temper at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 他在门口发了脾气。

items.example: The same root measures heat elsewhere.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词根在别处用来量热度。

items.example: A temperate climate suits the crop.
items.exampleCN: 温和的气候适合这种作物。

latinEntries.meaning: to mix in due proportion, moderate
a tempering, due mixture; later, heat level
latinEntries.meaningCN: 调和；适当混合；后指热度

definition_zh: 微生物学；研究微生物及其活动的学科
definition_en: the science that studies microorganisms, their structure, growth, and effects
core_image: 实验台上成排的培养皿与显微镜，标签上写满菌种编号，一张记录表逐项填写
scene: 这里指「微生物学」。 Clinical microbiology identified the strain before the second dose was given.
sceneCN: 这里 microbiology 是「微生物学」（第 3 个义项：临床微生物学这一分支）；句意：临床微生物学在给予第二剂之前就鉴定了菌株。图中可辨识物件：培养皿、显微镜、菌种鉴定报告。

pos.zh: 微生物学（不可数名词）；指学科时通常不加冠词，指某一分支时可加限定语

derivatives.zh: 微生物学的；微生物学方法的
生物技术（与微生物学交叉的现代领域）

senses.title: The Science of Microbes
senses.titleCN: 微生物学：研究微生物的科学
senses.definition: the branch of biology that studies microorganisms
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中研究微生物的分支
senses.example: Microbiology asks how a single cell can live, grow and cause disease.
senses.exampleCN: 微生物学追问一个细胞如何生存、生长并致病。
senses.why: The word joins micro-, 'small', biology, 'study of life', and -logy, 'science of'. The core is a discipline, not an organism: it names the organised knowledge about small life.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 micro-「小」、biology「生命研究」与 -logy「……学」构成；核心是一门学科，而不是某种生物：它命名的是关于微小生命的系统知识。

senses.title: A Discipline and a Department
senses.titleCN: 学科与院系：作为建制单位
senses.definition: the academic field or the institutional unit that teaches and researches it
senses.definitionCN: 教授与研究该领域的学术建制或单位
senses.example: She joined the microbiology department as a lecturer.
senses.exampleCN: 她以讲师身份加入了微生物学系。
senses.why: A science becomes an institution: it has chairs, degrees, journals and laboratories. The uncountable name can therefore stand for the department that houses the field.
senses.whyCN: 一门科学会变成一种建制：它拥有教席、学位、期刊与实验室；因此这个不可数名词可以代指容纳该领域的院系。

senses.title: Clinical Microbiology
senses.titleCN: 临床微生物学：为诊断服务
senses.definition: the branch that identifies microbes causing human disease
senses.definitionCN: 鉴定引起人类疾病的微生物的分支
senses.example: Clinical microbiology reports the species and its drug sensitivity.
senses.exampleCN: 临床微生物学报告菌种及其药物敏感性。
senses.why: In hospital use the science is narrowed to diagnosis. The adjective clinical marks the setting, and the work is to name the agent and guide treatment.
senses.whyCN: 在医院语境中，这门科学被收窄为诊断用途；形容词 clinical 标出场景，工作内容是命名病原并指导治疗。

senses.title: Food and Industrial Microbiology
senses.titleCN: 食品与工业微生物学：发酵与保质
senses.definition: the branch concerned with fermentation, preservation and industrial use
senses.definitionCN: 研究发酵、防腐与工业应用的微生物学分支
senses.example: Food microbiology keeps cheese cultures pure and spoilage out.
senses.exampleCN: 食品微生物学保持奶酪菌种纯净，并防止腐败。
senses.why: Here the discipline serves production: it manages useful microbes and excludes harmful ones. The same science that studies disease also runs a factory.
senses.whyCN: 这里这门学科为生产服务：管理有益微生物、排除有害微生物；研究疾病的同一门科学，也在经营工厂。

senses.title: Environmental Microbiology
senses.titleCN: 环境微生物学：生境中的微生物
senses.definition: the branch that studies microbes in soil, water and air
senses.definitionCN: 研究土壤、水体与空气中微生物的分支
senses.example: Environmental microbiology traced the oil spill's cleanup to local bacteria.
senses.exampleCN: 环境微生物学把漏油的清理归功于本地细菌。
senses.why: The setting shifts from the clinic to the ecosystem. The discipline asks how microbial communities cycle elements and degrade pollutants.
senses.whyCN: 场景从诊室转向生态系统；这门学科研究微生物群落如何循环元素、降解污染物。

senses.title: Laboratory Methods
senses.titleCN: 实验室方法：培养、染色与鉴定
senses.definition: the practical methods of culturing, staining and identifying microbes
senses.definitionCN: 培养、染色与鉴定微生物的实用方法
senses.example: The course begins with the microbiology of streaking a plate.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课从平板划线这一微生物学基本操作开始。
senses.why: A science is also a set of hands-on techniques. The name can denote the method side, which is why a laboratory course and a research field share the word.
senses.whyCN: 一门科学也是一套动手技术；这个名称可以指方法层面，因此实验室课程与研究领域共用同一个词。

senses.title: A Course or a Textbook
senses.titleCN: 课程与教材：作为教学科目
senses.definition: a course or textbook that teaches the subject
senses.definitionCN: 教授该科目的课程或教材
senses.example: Microbiology is a second-year course in most biology programmes.
senses.exampleCN: 在多数生物专业中，微生物学是二年级课程。
senses.why: The name of a science can metonymically name its teaching. Students say they are taking microbiology, meaning the course rather than the whole field.
senses.whyCN: 学科名可以通过转喻指它的教学；学生说自己在上微生物学，指的是课程，而不是整个领域。

senses.title: The Microbes of a Sample
senses.titleCN: 样本的微生物组成：转喻用法
senses.definition: the microbial content or profile of a sample or a body site
senses.definitionCN: 某样本或身体部位的微生物组成或图谱
senses.example: The microbiology of the gut changed after the treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗之后，肠道的微生物组成发生了变化。
senses.why: Professional shorthand says the microbiology of a site when it means the microbes found there. The discipline name stands for its object, a familiar kind of metonymy.
senses.whyCN: 专业简称会说某部位的「微生物学」，实际指的是该处检出的微生物；学科名代替了它的研究对象，这是常见的转喻。

intro.en: Microbiology was coined in English in 1880 by joining the Greek prefix micro- to biology, a word itself only sixty years older. Its history shows how a new instrument, the microscope, created a new science.
intro.cn: microbiology 于 1880 年在英语中由希腊前缀 micro- 与 biology 组合而成，而 biology 本身只比它早六十年。它的历史显示，一件新工具——显微镜——如何创造出一门新科学。

items.en: Greek mikros, Attic smikros, meant 'small'. The Latinized prefix micro- entered scientific English as the standard marker of the very small. Beekes suspects a Pre-Greek origin, so the deeper etymology is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 mikros（阿提卡形式 smikros）意为「小」；拉丁化前缀 micro- 作为「极小」的标准标记进入科学英语。Beekes 怀疑它源自前希腊语底层，因此更深词源不确定。

items.en: Biology was suggested in 1802 by Treviranus and introduced in French by Lamarck, entering English by 1819. It joins Greek bios 'life' and -logia 'study, discourse'.
items.cn: biology 由特雷维拉努斯于 1802 年提出，并由拉马克以法语引入，1819 年进入英语；它由希腊 bios「生命」与 -logia「研究、论述」构成。

items.en: Greek -logia came from -log-, the combining form of legein 'to speak, tell', itself from a root meaning 'to gather, pick out'. Hence -logy names a disciplined way of speaking about a subject.
items.cn: 希腊 -logia 来自 -log-，即 legein「说、讲述」的组合形式，其词根意为「收集、拣选」；因此 -logy 命名的是关于某主题的一套有纪律的论述方式。

items.en: Microbiology is recorded from 1880, coined in English from micro- and biology. The same period produced microbiologist (1882) and the adjective microbiological.
items.cn: microbiology 记录于 1880 年，在英语中由 micro- 与 biology 构成；同一时期还产生了 microbiologist（1882）与形容词 microbiological。

items.en: Pasteur's and Koch's work in the 1870s and 1880s gave the new science its first great successes: sterilisation, pure culture and the identification of specific pathogens.
items.cn: 巴斯德与科赫在十九世纪七十至八十年代的工作，给这门新科学带来最初的重大成功：灭菌、纯培养与特定病原的鉴定。

items.en: The older name bacteriology covered only bacteria. Microbiology became the wider term once protists, fungi and later viruses were studied with the same methods. The shift is a widening of the object, not a change of root.
items.cn: 较早的 bacteriology 只涵盖细菌；当原生生物、真菌以及后来的病毒用同样方法研究之后，microbiology 成为更宽的名称。这一变化是研究对象的扩展，而不是词根的更换。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same stem that occupy other grammatical or professional slots. The second group holds neighbouring disciplines, each with a narrower object.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干上占据其他语法或职业位置的词；第二组是相邻学科，各自的研究对象更窄。

entries.definition: A person who practises microbiology. The ending -ist marks the practitioner, not the field.
entries.definitionCN: 从事微生物学的人；词尾 -ist 标记从业者，而不是学科。

entries.definition: Relating to microbiology or its methods, as in microbiological safety. It describes the discipline's procedures rather than the organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 与微生物学或其方法有关的，如微生物学安全；描述的是学科程序，而不是生物体。

entries.definition: Of microbes themselves. It is the object-level adjective, while microbiological is the discipline-level one.
entries.definitionCN: 指微生物本身的形容词；它是对象层面的形容词，而 microbiological 是学科层面的。

entries.definition: The study of bacteria only. It is a subset of microbiology and was the older name for much of the same work.
entries.definitionCN: 只研究细菌的学科；它是微生物学的子集，也曾是大部分同类工作的旧名称。

entries.definition: The study of viruses, which are not cells and are often excluded from microorganisms. It is a separate discipline with separate methods.
entries.definitionCN: 研究病毒的学科；病毒不是细胞，常被排除在微生物之外，因此它是一门有独立方法的独立学科。

entries.definition: The study of fungi, including yeasts and moulds. Many fungi are microorganisms, but the discipline is defined by the group, not the size.
entries.definitionCN: 研究真菌（包括酵母与霉菌）的学科；许多真菌是微生物，但这门学科按类群而非大小定义。

entries.definition: The industrial use of living systems, microbes among them. It is an application of microbiology rather than a branch of it.
entries.definitionCN: 对生命系统（包括微生物）的工业利用；它是微生物学的应用，而不是其分支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: micro- 'small' + biology 'study of life' + -logy 'science of': the science of small life.
normal.cn: micro-「小」+ biology「生命研究」+ -logy「……学」：研究微小生命的科学。

normal.en: The word was coined in 1880, one year after microbial and two after microbe.
normal.cn: 这个词于 1880 年创制，比 microbial 晚一年，比 microbe 晚两年。

normal.en: The family runs microbiology, microbiologist, microbiological, microbiologically, microbe, microbial and microbiome.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 microbiology、microbiologist、microbiological、microbiologically、microbe、microbial、microbiome。

normal.en: Prefixes mark the branch: clinical, food, environmental, molecular and industrial microbiology.
normal.cn: 限定语标出分支：临床、食品、环境、分子与工业微生物学。

normal.en: Microbiology is wider than bacteriology because its object is defined by size, not by kingdom.
normal.cn: microbiology 比 bacteriology 宽，因为它的对象按大小定义，而不是按生物界定义。

abstract.en: Picture a science that began the day a lens made a hidden world visible.
abstract.cn: 想象一门科学，始于镜片让隐藏世界变得可见的那一天。

abstract.en: Picture a department where every shelf holds a dish of invisible citizens.
abstract.cn: 想象一个院系，每个架子上都放着一盘看不见的居民。

abstract.en: Picture a single cell asked to explain both a disease and a loaf of bread.
abstract.cn: 想象要求一个细胞同时解释一场疾病和一条面包。

examples.en: Microbiology turned the unknown outbreak into a named species.
examples.cn: 微生物学把不明疫情变成了一个有名字的物种。

examples.en: She studied microbiology before moving into public health.
examples.cn: 她在转入公共卫生之前学习过微生物学。

examples.en: Industrial microbiology keeps the fermentation tanks free of spoilage.
examples.cn: 工业微生物学让发酵罐免于腐败。

dict_mnemonic.text: micro-（微小）+ biology（生物学）→ 研究微小生物的学科 → microbiology 微生物学

root: 希腊 mikros「小」→ 拉丁化 micro-；希腊 bios「生命」+ -logia「研究、论述」→ biology（1819 年入英语）→ 1880 年英语合成 micro- + biology = microbiology。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the science itself to its institutional, clinical, industrial, environmental, practical, teaching and metonymic uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从这门科学本身，走向它的建制、临床、工业、环境、实践、教学与转喻用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of labelled dishes on a bench, a microscope and a report being filled in.
core.cn: 核心意象：实验台上一排贴标签的培养皿、显微镜，以及正在填写的报告。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE: the organised study of small life is the root sense from which the others radiate.
branches.cn: 知识：关于微小生命的系统研究是根义，其他义项都由它辐射而出。

branches.en: INSTITUTION AND TEACHING: a science can be a department or a course, because people organise and teach it.
branches.cn: 建制与教学：一门科学可以是一个院系或一门课，因为人们会组织它、教授它。

branches.en: APPLIED SETTINGS: the clinic names pathogens, the factory manages cultures.
branches.cn: 应用场景：诊所命名病原，工厂管理菌种。

branches.en: ENVIRONMENT: the same methods move outdoors to soil, water and air.
branches.cn: 环境：同样的方法移到户外，用于土壤、水体与空气。

branches.en: HANDS AND OBJECT: techniques are the hands of the science, and 'the microbiology of a site' is its object standing in for it.
branches.cn: 双手与对象：技术是这门科学的双手，而「某处的微生物学」是它的研究对象代它出场。

intro.en: Microbiology stacks three Greek elements: a prefix of smallness, a root of life, and a suffix of disciplined study.
intro.cn: microbiology 叠合了三个希腊成分：表示「微小」的前缀、表示「生命」的词根，以及表示「系统研究」的后缀。

latinIntro.en: The elements reached English through Latinized scientific forms: micro- from Greek mikros, biology from New Latin biologia, and -logy from Latin -logia. No single classical Latin word lies behind the compound.
latinIntro.cn: 这些成分经拉丁化的科学形式进入英语：micro- 来自希腊 mikros，biology 来自新拉丁 biologia，-logy 来自拉丁 -logia。这个复合词背后并没有单一的古典拉丁词。

items.example: Microbiology has its own methods.
items.exampleCN: 微生物学有自己的方法。

items.meaningCN: 从事这门科学的从业者
items.example: The microbiologist read the plate.
items.exampleCN: 微生物学家判读了培养皿。

items.example: Microbiological safety was checked.
items.exampleCN: 检查了微生物学安全。

items.meaning: from a microbiological point of view
items.example: The sample was microbiologically clean.
items.exampleCN: 该样本在微生物学上是洁净的。

items.example: Biology split into many branches.
items.exampleCN: 生物学分成许多分支。

items.example: The microbe was cultured in agar.
items.exampleCN: 这种微生物在琼脂中培养。

items.example: Microbial mats cover the pool.
items.exampleCN: 微生物席覆盖着水塘。

items.example: The microbiome project sampled many sites.
items.exampleCN: 微生物组计划在许多地点取样。

items.example: Bacteriology predates microbiology.
items.exampleCN: 细菌学早于微生物学。

definition_zh: 社会制度；社会机构（家庭、学校、宗教、法庭等由社会共同承认并长期沿用的组织或规则体系）
definition_en: an established organization or body of rules through which a society meets a basic need, such as the family, a school or a court
core_image: 广场四周并排立着教堂、学校与议事厅，台阶上有人在等待，每扇门上方都刻着同一枚旧纹章
scene: 小镇广场的四边围着教堂、学校和议事厅，人们从各自的门口进出。 The village school became a social institution long before the state paid for it.
sceneCN: 这里指「社会共同承认并长期沿用的组织或规则体系」（第 1 个义项：为满足基本社会需要而设立的组织）；句意为这所村校早在国家出资之前就已成为一项社会制度。可辨识物件：广场、教堂、学校、议事厅、旧纹章。

pos.zh: 社会制度；社会机构（可数）

collocations.phrase: the family as a social institution

senses.title: An organization meeting a basic social need
senses.titleCN: 为满足基本社会需要而设的组织
senses.definition: an established organization that a society relies on to meet a basic need
senses.definitionCN: 社会为满足某项基本需要而依赖的常设组织
senses.example: The library is a social institution that serves everyone in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆是一项服务全镇所有人的社会机构。
senses.why: the phrase joins a word for companionship with a word for something set up, so it names a standing arrangement people share.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把表「相伴」的词与表「设立」的词合在一起，指人们共同拥有的常设安排。

senses.title: The family as a foundational institution
senses.definition: the household as the first and most basic arrangement through which a society raises its young
senses.definitionCN: 社会抚养下一代所依靠的第一项、最基础的安排，即家庭
senses.example: Sociologists treat the family as the oldest social institution.
senses.exampleCN: 社会学家把家庭视为最古老的社会制度。
senses.why: the family is the clearest case where an everyday arrangement is also a recognized structure.
senses.whyCN: 家庭最能说明：日常安排同时也可以是被承认的结构。

senses.title: The school system
senses.definition: the organized system of schools and teaching that a society maintains
senses.definitionCN: 社会维持的学校与教学组织体系
senses.example: Compulsory schooling turned education into a national social institution.
senses.exampleCN: 义务教育使教育成为一项全国性的社会制度。
senses.why: schooling became a state duty, so the network that delivers it took the name of an institution.
senses.whyCN: 学校教育成为国家义务，承担它的网络因此获得了「制度」之名。

senses.title: An established religion
senses.definition: an organized religious body with recognized buildings, offices and rules
senses.definitionCN: 拥有被承认的场所、职位与规章的宗教组织
senses.example: The old temple remains a social institution as well as a place of worship.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古庙既是礼拜场所，也是一项社会制度。
senses.why: a faith with buildings and offices is an institution in the everyday sense as well as the sociological one.
senses.whyCN: 拥有场所与职位的信仰团体，在日常意义与社会学意义上都是制度。

senses.title: Courts and representative bodies
senses.definition: the legal and political bodies that settle disputes and make binding decisions
senses.definitionCN: 解决争端并作出有约束力决定的法律与政治机构
senses.example: A functioning court is a social institution in the strict sense.
senses.exampleCN: 运转正常的法庭是严格意义上的社会制度。
senses.why: courts settle disputes by recognized rules, which is the defining work of an institution.
senses.whyCN: 法庭依被承认的规则解决争端，而这正是制度的定义性工作。

senses.title: The market and property rules
senses.definition: the accepted rules of exchange, contract and ownership that make economic life predictable
senses.definitionCN: 使经济生活可预期的交换、契约与所有权规则
senses.example: Currency and contract are social institutions before they are economic tools.
senses.exampleCN: 货币与契约在成为经济工具之前，先已是社会制度。
senses.why: exchange needs stable expectations more than it needs buildings, so rules count as the institution.
senses.whyCN: 交换更需要稳定的预期而非建筑，因此规则本身就构成制度。

senses.title: A pattern of norms rather than a building
senses.titleCN: 作为规范格局而非实体建筑
senses.definition: a settled pattern of shared expectations that exists even without a single building
senses.definitionCN: 即使没有某座建筑也依然存在的共同期待格局
senses.example: Greeting customs are a social institution with no headquarters at all.
senses.exampleCN: 问候习俗是一项根本没有总部的社会制度。
senses.why: the sociological reading drops the building and keeps only the settled expectations.
senses.whyCN: 社会学的读法去掉建筑，只留下沉淀下来的共同期待。

senses.title: A body that shapes public opinion
senses.definition: an established press or broadcaster whose routines shape what a society considers news
senses.definitionCN: 其日常运作塑造社会「何为新闻」的既有报刊或广播机构
senses.example: The national broadcaster acts as a social institution during elections.
senses.exampleCN: 选举期间，这家全国广播机构起着社会制度的作用。
senses.why: a broadcaster's routines decide what counts as news, which is a basic need in a public.
senses.whyCN: 广播机构的日常运作决定什么算新闻，而这是公众的一项基本需要。

intro.en: Social institution joins social, from Latin socialis 'of companionship', and institution, from Latin instituere 'to set up'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词由表「社会的」与表「机构」的两个名词组合而成：前者出自拉丁 socialis「相伴的」，后者出自拉丁 instituere「设立」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally, partner'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link sometimes proposed with a root meaning 'to follow' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友、合伙人」。其更深来源不确定；有人提出它与一个表「跟随」的词根有关，那属于重构形式。

items.en: The ending -alis built relational adjectives, so socialis meant 'of companions, of alliance' before English widened it to all of society.
items.cn: 表关系的拉丁形容词词尾构成这类形容词，因此 socialis 先指「同伴的、结盟的」，后来英语才把它扩展到整个社会。

items.en: In- plus statuere 'to set, cause to stand' produced instituere 'to set up, establish'.
items.cn: 前缀表「在内」加 statuere「放置、使站立」，构成 instituere「设立、建立」。

items.en: English formed institution in the fifteenth century from the Latin action noun, at first for an ordinance or an established body.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪由拉丁动作名词构成「机构」一词，最初指条例或已设立的机构。

items.en: Nineteenth-century sociology paired the two words to name the standing arrangements that outlast individuals.
items.cn: 十九世纪社会学把这两个词配对，用来指比个人活得更久的常设安排。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of socius is not established, so any older form quoted for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：socius 在拉丁语之前的来源未获证明，凡为其引用的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike phrases and forms built from the same two stems; group two holds near neighbours that name organized life.
note.cn: 第一组是由同两个词干构成的形近短语与词形；第二组是描述组织化生活的近义词。

entries.definition: The arrangement of groups and ranks in a society; it is the shape institutions sit inside.
entries.definitionCN: 指社会中群体与层级的排列，是制度所嵌入的形态。

entries.definition: The condition in which rules are obeyed and life is predictable, rather than a named body.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则被遵守、生活可预期的状态，而非某个具名机构。

entries.definition: Used alone it may mean any organization, including a bank; the full phrase restricts it to society's basic arrangements.
entries.definitionCN: 单用时泛指任何机构，包括银行；完整短语把它限定为社会的基本安排。

entries.definition: The process by which people learn a society's norms; it is what institutions do to newcomers.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们习得社会规范的过程，是制度对新成员所做的事。

entries.definition: A structured group with a purpose; it lacks the phrase's implication of a basic social need.
entries.definitionCN: 指有目的的结构化团体，缺少该短语「满足基本社会需要」的含义。

entries.definition: Often names the existing holders of power, with a critical tone; it is narrower and more political.
entries.definitionCN: 常指在位的权力集团，带批评语气，范围更窄也更政治化。

entries.definition: A habitual practice handed down; it can be an institution's content but not the body itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指代代相传的习惯做法，可成为制度的内容，却不是机构本身。

entries.definition: A supporting structure of rules; it emphasizes design rather than social acceptance.
entries.definitionCN: 指支撑性的规则结构，强调设计，而非社会承认。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective means 'of companions', which is exactly what a shared institution is.
normal.cn: 那个形容词意为「同伴的」，而共同制度正是同伴之间的事物。

normal.en: The second word means 'something set up', so the phrase is literally a standing arrangement.
normal.cn: 第二个词意为「被设立之物」，因此整个短语字面上就是一项常设安排。

normal.en: Fixed phrases pair it with family, school, religion and the market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它与家庭、学校、宗教、市场配对。

normal.en: The family runs society, social, socially, socialize, socialization, institution.
normal.cn: 同族包括「社会」「社会的」「在社会层面」「使社会化」「社会化」「机构」。

normal.en: Sociology contrasts institution with structure: the body versus the arrangement.
normal.cn: 社会学把「制度」与「结构」对照：前者是实体，后者是排列。

abstract.en: Picture four doors around one square, each opening onto the same old seal.
abstract.cn: 想象广场四周有四扇门，每扇都开向同一枚旧印章。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that people obey even when no official is watching.
abstract.cn: 想象一条即使没有官员看着、人们仍遵守的规则。

abstract.en: Picture a chair worn smooth by generations sitting in the same place.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子被一代代人坐在同一处，磨得发亮。

examples.en: The family is the social institution on which most others depend.
examples.cn: 家庭是大多数其他社会制度所依赖的那一项。

examples.en: A court that no one trusts has stopped working as a social institution.
examples.cn: 一个无人信任的法庭，已不再作为社会制度运转。

examples.en: Social institutions change more slowly than the people inside them.
examples.cn: 社会制度的变化比其中的人慢得多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「搜受」加「因斯提图深」——大家一起搜罗并承受的那套深植的安排，就是社会制度。

root: social 出自拉丁 socialis「同伴的」，其词干 socius「同伴」的更深来源不确定；institution 出自拉丁 instituere「设立」，由 in- 与 statuere「放置、使站立」构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move outward from one idea: a basic need is met by an arrangement stable enough to be recognized, whether that arrangement is a family, a school, a faith, a court, a market, a custom or a broadcaster.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个观念向外展开：某项基本需要由一种稳定到足以被承认的安排来满足，无论那是家庭、学校、信仰、法庭、市场、习俗还是广播机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four doors around one square, each opening onto the same worn seal.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场四周的四扇门，每扇都通向同一枚磨旧的印章。

branches.en: THE DEFINITION: any established body that carries a basic need counts.
branches.cn: 定义本身：凡承担基本需要的常设组织都算。

branches.en: FIRST ARRANGEMENT: the household is the oldest and smallest case.
branches.cn: 最早的安排：家庭是最古老也最小的例子。

branches.en: TEACHING AND TELLING: schools form the young, broadcasters form what the public calls news.
branches.cn: 教导与告知：学校塑造年轻人，广播机构塑造公众所称的新闻。

branches.en: FAITH: a religious body is an institution in both the everyday and the strict sense.

definition_zh: 优化；最优化；最佳化；调优
definition_en: the process of making something as good or as effective as possible, often within stated limits
core_image: 一条曲线上有一个最低点，一支笔沿着线移动，最后停在那一点上。
scene: 工程团队反复调整参数，让同一台发动机在油耗与动力之间找到折中。 Years of optimization brought fuel use and power into balance.
sceneCN: 这里 optimization 是“在约束下把效果调到最好”（第 2 个义项）；句意：多年的优化让油耗与动力达到平衡。

pos.zh: 优化；最优化；最佳化；调优

senses.title: Making it as good as it can be
senses.definition: the process of improving something toward its best possible state
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物朝其最佳可能状态改进的过程
senses.example: The optimization of the design took months of small changes.
senses.exampleCN: 这项设计的优化花了数月时间做小改动。
senses.why: The word is comparative in secret: it assumes a scale of better and worse, then moves an object along that scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个词暗含比较：它预设了一条“更好—更差”的尺度，然后把对象沿这条尺度推动。

senses.title: Best under constraints
senses.titleCN: 最优化：在限制里找最好的那点
senses.definition: the mathematical process of finding the best solution to a problem within given limits
senses.definitionCN: 在给定限制内为问题寻找最佳解的数学过程
senses.example: The optimization problem asked for the shortest route under a fixed budget.
senses.exampleCN: 这个最优化问题要求在固定预算下找出最短路线。
senses.why: Mathematics adds constraints: without limits almost anything could be improved, and with them a best point may exist.
senses.whyCN: 数学加上了约束：没有限制，几乎任何东西都能再改进；有了限制，才可能存在一个最优点。

senses.title: A procedure that searches
senses.titleCN: 优化算法：一步步试出更好的解
senses.definition: an algorithm or method that searches for a better solution by repeated adjustment
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复调整搜索更优解的算法或方法
senses.example: The optimization converged after forty iterations.
senses.exampleCN: 该优化过程在四十次迭代后收敛。
senses.why: When the best point cannot be calculated directly, the work becomes a search: adjust, measure, keep what improves, repeat.
senses.whyCN: 当最优点无法直接算出时，工作就变成搜索：调整、测量、保留改进、重复。

senses.title: Spending less for the same result
senses.titleCN: 成本优化：同样的效果，更少的钱
senses.definition: the reduction of costs while maintaining an acceptable level of output or quality
senses.definitionCN: 在维持可接受产出或质量水平的同时降低成本
senses.example: Cost optimization cut the packaging budget without changing the product.
senses.exampleCN: 成本优化削减了包装预算，产品本身没有变化。
senses.why: In business the scale is money: the same output is held fixed while the input is pushed down, which is optimization in one direction.
senses.whyCN: 在商业中，尺度是钱：产出保持不变，投入被压低，这是单向的优化。

senses.title: Being found by search engines
senses.titleCN: 搜索引擎优化：让页面更容易被找到
senses.definition: the practice of improving a web page so that search engines rank it more highly
senses.definitionCN: 改进网页以使其在搜索引擎中获得更高排名的做法
senses.example: Search engine optimization raised the shop's traffic without any advertising.
senses.exampleCN: 搜索引擎优化在没有投放广告的情况下提高了店铺流量。
senses.why: Here the 'best state' is defined by an external ranking system, so optimization means fitting the page to someone else's scoring rule.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“最佳状态”由外部排名系统定义，因此优化意味着让页面迎合别人的评分规则。

senses.title: Getting more from what you have
senses.titleCN: 资源优化：同一批人、同一批料，做出更多
senses.definition: the arrangement of people, materials, or time so that available resources produce the most value
senses.definitionCN: 安排人力、物料或时间，使现有资源产出最大价值
senses.example: Resource optimization moved two nurses to the night shift and cut waiting times.
senses.exampleCN: 资源优化把两名护士调去夜班，缩短了等待时间。
senses.why: When resources are fixed, improvement can only come from arrangement: the same pieces are ordered differently.
senses.whyCN: 当资源固定时，改进只能来自安排：同样的零件被重新排序。

senses.title: Making software run faster
senses.titleCN: 性能优化：让程序少等、少算
senses.definition: the process of making software use less time, memory, or power for the same task
senses.definitionCN: 使软件完成同一任务时消耗更少时间、内存或电力的过程
senses.example: Performance optimization reduced the page load from four seconds to one.
senses.exampleCN: 性能优化把页面加载时间从四秒降到一秒。
senses.why: Computing gives optimization a measurable target: the same output must be produced with fewer machine cycles.
senses.whyCN: 计算领域给优化一个可测量的目标：同样的输出必须用更少的机器周期完成。

senses.title: Rewriting code before it runs
senses.titleCN: 编译器优化：运行前先替代码省力
senses.definition: the rewriting of code by a compiler to make the resulting program faster or smaller
senses.definitionCN: 由编译器改写代码，使生成的程序更快或更小
senses.example: Compiler optimization removed a loop that always ran zero times.
senses.exampleCN: 编译器优化删掉了一个永远执行零次的循环。
senses.why: The compiler optimizes on the programmer's behalf, using facts proved at compile time to drop work the program would otherwise do.
senses.whyCN: 编译器替程序员做优化，利用编译期已证明的事实删去程序本会执行的工作。

intro.en: Optimization comes from optimize, formed from Latin optimum, 'the best', plus -ize and -ation. Optimum is the neuter of optimus, the superlative of bonus, good.
intro.cn: optimization 来自 optimize，由拉丁语 optimum“最好的”加 -ize 与 -ation 构成。optimum 是 optimus 的中性形式，而 optimus 是 bonus“好”的最高级。

items.en: Bonus meant good. Its comparative melior and superlative optimus supplied the whole scale of better and best.
items.cn: bonus 意为好。其比较级 melior 与最高级 optimus 提供了“更好—最好”的整条尺度。

items.en: Optimus meant best. The neuter optimum named the best thing or the best condition, and entered English as a noun and adjective.
items.cn: optimus 意为最好的。其中性形式 optimum 指最好的事物或最佳条件，作为名词与形容词进入英语。

items.en: English optimum first appeared in scientific writing for the best condition, such as the temperature at which an enzyme works best.
items.cn: 英语 optimum 最初出现在科学写作中，指最佳条件，例如酶活性最高的温度。

items.en: Optimize was formed in the 19th century on optimum plus -ize, meaning to make the best of a situation.
items.cn: optimize 于 19 世纪由 optimum 加 -ize 构成，意为“充分利用条件、使达到最好”。

items.en: The suffix -ation, from -atio, turns the verb into the name of the process. Optimization is therefore the process of making optimal.
items.cn: 后缀 -ation（源自 -atio）把动词变成过程之名。因此 optimization 就是“使之最优”的过程。

items.en: Mathematics and computing gave the word its technical sense: a search for a best point under constraints, and the rewriting of code for speed.
items.cn: 数学与计算赋予该词技术含义：在约束下搜索最优点，以及为提速而改写代码。

note.en: The first group is the optimum family; the second compares words for improvement, each with a different standard of 'better'.
note.cn: 第一组是 optimum 词族；第二组比较表示“改进”的词，各自对“更好”的标准不同。

entries.definition: to make something as effective as possible. It names the action.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物尽可能有效；命名的是动作。

entries.definition: best or most favourable among the options available.
entries.definitionCN: 在可选方案中最好的或最有利的。

entries.definition: the best possible condition or level.
entries.definitionCN: 最佳的可能条件或水平。

entries.definition: a change that makes something better. It does not imply that a best point has been reached.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变好的改变；不暗示已到达最优点。

entries.definition: a small change that makes something more precise or elegant. It is improvement by polishing.
entries.definitionCN: 使事物更精确或更精致的小改动；靠打磨实现的改进。

entries.definition: output divided by input. Optimization often raises it, but the two are not the same.
entries.definitionCN: 产出与投入之比；优化常提高效率，但二者并不相同。

entries.definition: making something as large as possible. Optimization can target a maximum or a minimum.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物尽可能大；优化既可以求最大，也可以求最小。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: optimum, the best, plus -ize and -ation. Optimization is the process of moving something toward the best available point.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：optimum“最好的”，加 -ize 与 -ation。optimization 就是把事物推向最佳可用点的过程。

normal.en: Optimum is the best point on the curve; optimization is the walk toward it.
normal.cn: optimum 是曲线上的最优点；optimization 是走向它的那段路。

normal.en: No constraints, no optimum: the limits are what make a best point exist.
normal.cn: 没有约束就没有最优：正是限制让“最优点”得以存在。

normal.en: Cost optimization keeps the output and squeezes the input.
normal.cn: 成本优化固定产出，挤压投入。

normal.en: Search engine optimization is fitting a page to someone else's scoring rule.
normal.cn: 搜索引擎优化就是让页面迎合别人的评分规则。

normal.en: Compiler optimization does the tidying before the program ever runs.
normal.cn: 编译器优化在程序运行之前就替它收拾干净。

abstract.en: Every optimization chooses a measure, and the measure quietly decides what counts as good.
abstract.cn: 每次优化都要选一个度量，而度量悄悄决定了什么算“好”。

abstract.en: What is optimal for one part of a system is often costly for another; the whole is rarely optimized at once.
abstract.cn: 对系统某部分最优的事，往往对另一部分代价高昂；整体很少能一次同时达到最优。

abstract.en: The word sounds final, but an optimum is only the best among the options someone thought to consider.
abstract.cn: 这个词听起来像终点，但最优点只是“在某人想到要考虑的选项里”最好的那个。

examples.en: The optimization of the timetable saved eight buses without lengthening any trip.
examples.cn: 时刻表的优化省下了八辆车，却没有延长任何一趟行程。

examples.en: The algorithm's optimization step is where most of the computing time goes.
examples.cn: 算法中耗去大部分计算时间的正是优化那一步。

examples.en: She studied cost optimization in hospitals and found that supplies, not staff, drove the waste.
examples.cn: 她研究医院成本优化，发现造成浪费的是耗材，而不是人力。

dict_mnemonic.text: optim（最好）+ ization（化）——朝“最好”去的过程，就是优化、最优化。

root: 源自拉丁语 optimum（最好的，为 optimus 的中性形式，optimus 又是 bonus“好”的最高级），加 -ize 与 -ation 构成，本义为“使之达到最佳状态的过程”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of optimization, all built on one shape: a curve with a best point and a search toward it. The curve may be mathematical, financial, operational, computational, or a search engine's ranking rule.
sensesIntro.cn: optimization 的八个义项都建立在同一个形状上：一条带有最优点的曲线，以及朝它进行的搜索。这条曲线可以是数学的、财务的、运营的、计算的，或搜索引擎的排名规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curve with a lowest point, and a pen moving along it until it stops there.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条带最低点的曲线，一支笔沿线移动，最后停在那一点。

branches.en: THE GENERAL MOVE AND THE MATHEMATICAL ONE: improving toward a best state, and finding a best point under constraints.

branches.en: MACHINE SPEED: fewer cycles at run time, and code rewritten before run time.
branches.cn: 机器速度：运行时减少周期，以及运行前改写代码。

intro.en: Optimization is optimize plus -ation. Optimize is optimum plus -ize, and optimum is the Latin superlative 'best'. The family also gives optimal, optimally, and optimist.

items.example: The crop grows best near the optimum temperature.
items.exampleCN: 这种作物在最佳温度附近长得最好。

items.meaning: the process of reaching the best available state

items.example: The optimization reduced fuel use by a fifth.
