items.example: The engine runs optimally at this speed.
items.exampleCN: 发动机在这个转速下运转最佳。

items.meaning: the view that things are or will be good; hopefulness

items.example: Her optimism carried the team through the delay.
items.exampleCN: 她的乐观让团队熬过了延误。

items.meaning: the opposite of optimism, built on the Latin superlative for worst

definition_zh: 膜；薄膜；细胞膜；隔膜
definition_en: a thin layer of tissue or material that separates two regions or covers a surface
core_image: 一层薄而柔韧的皮，把两边隔开又允许某些东西通过
scene: 这里指「膜」。 The membrane around the cell controls what enters and leaves.
sceneCN: 这里 membrane 指「细胞膜」（第 2 个义项：包围细胞的薄膜）；句意：细胞周围的膜控制物质的进出。

pos.zh: 膜；薄膜；细胞膜；隔膜；（鼓、扬声器的）振动膜

senses.title: Thin separating layer
senses.definition: a thin sheet of material that separates two spaces or covers a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把两个空间隔开或覆盖表面的薄片
senses.example: A membrane kept the salt water from mixing with the fresh water.
senses.exampleCN: 一层膜阻止盐水与淡水混合。
senses.why: The Latin word named a thin skin, and the core sense remains any thin layer that divides one region from another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词本指一层薄皮，核心义仍是把两个区域隔开的任何薄层。

senses.title: Cell membrane
senses.definition: the thin layer that surrounds a cell and controls what passes through
senses.definitionCN: 包围细胞并控制物质通过的薄膜
senses.example: The cell membrane is a double layer of lipids.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜是脂质的双层结构。
senses.why: Every cell is separated from its surroundings by a skin, so biology uses the word for the boundary of life itself.
senses.whyCN: 每个细胞都靠一层皮与外界隔开，因此生物学用这个词指生命本身的边界。

senses.title: Mucous membrane
senses.definition: the moist lining of body cavities such as the mouth and nose
senses.definitionCN: 口腔、鼻腔等体腔的湿润内衬
senses.example: The virus enters through the mucous membrane of the nose.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒经由鼻腔的黏膜进入。
senses.why: Anatomy names the lining of a cavity by its thin membranous character, and the fixed phrase mucous membrane marks the wet ones.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学按薄而似膜的特征命名体腔内衬，固定说法 mucous membrane 标出其中湿润的那类。

senses.title: Synthetic membrane
senses.definition: a manufactured film used to filter or separate substances
senses.definitionCN: 用于过滤或分离物质的人造薄膜
senses.example: The plant uses a membrane to remove salt from seawater.
senses.exampleCN: 该厂用一层膜从海水中除盐。
senses.why: Engineers copy the biological boundary with synthetic films, and the same word follows the function rather than the material.
senses.whyCN: 工程师用人工薄膜复制生物边界，同一个词跟随的是功能而不是材料。

senses.title: Eardrum
senses.definition: the thin membrane in the ear that vibrates with sound
senses.definitionCN: 耳中随声音振动的薄膜
senses.example: A loud noise can rupture the tympanic membrane.
senses.exampleCN: 巨大的噪声可能震破鼓膜。
senses.why: The eardrum is literally a small stretched membrane, so anatomy borrows the general word without metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 鼓膜字面上就是一张绷紧的小膜，因此解剖学直接借用这个通用词，并不构成比喻。

senses.title: Membrane proteins
senses.definition: the proteins and lipids that make up a biological membrane
senses.definitionCN: 构成生物膜的蛋白质与脂质
senses.example: Membrane proteins pump ions across the bilayer.
senses.exampleCN: 膜蛋白把离子泵过双分子层。
senses.why: Once the membrane is an object, its components need names, and compounds such as membrane protein locate them in that layer.
senses.whyCN: 一旦膜成为对象，它的组成部分就需要名字，membrane protein 这类复合词就把它们定位在这层结构中。

senses.title: Membrane potential
senses.definition: the voltage difference across a biological membrane
senses.definitionCN: 生物膜两侧的电压差
senses.example: The membrane potential changes when an ion channel opens.
senses.exampleCN: 离子通道打开时膜电位会改变。
senses.why: Because a membrane separates two compartments, a difference in charge can build across it, giving the word a physical role.
senses.whyCN: 由于膜把两个隔间分开，电荷差会在它两侧积累，于是这个词有了物理学角色。

senses.title: Tensile structure
senses.definition: a thin fabric or sheet stretched to carry loads in architecture
senses.definitionCN: 建筑中绷紧以承载的薄织物或薄片
senses.example: The stadium roof is a membrane supported by cables.
senses.exampleCN: 体育场的屋顶是由钢索支撑的张拉膜。
senses.why: Architecture uses the word for a surface that works by tension, the same idea of a thin skin doing a structural job.
senses.whyCN: 建筑用这个词指靠张力工作的表面，仍是「一层薄皮承担结构任务」的同一想法。

senses.title: Vibrating diaphragm
senses.definition: the stretched sheet in a drum, speaker or microphone that produces or senses sound
senses.definitionCN: 鼓、扬声器或麦克风中产生或感知声音的绷紧薄片
senses.example: The microphone's membrane moves with the slightest sound.
senses.exampleCN: 麦克风的振动膜会随极轻微的声音移动。
senses.why: A thin sheet stretched over a frame is the physical shape of every drumhead, so the word covers that everyday object too.
senses.whyCN: 绷在框架上的薄片正是每个鼓面的物理形态，因此这个词也涵盖这种日常物件。

intro.en: Membrane is Latin for a thin skin; its link to the word for a limb is plausible but not certain.
intro.cn: membrane 在拉丁语里指一层薄皮；它与表示「肢体」的词的联系看似合理，但并不确定。

items.en: Latin membrana meant a thin skin, parchment or the surface of a body part. English borrowed it in the 15th century for anatomical coverings.
items.cn: 拉丁语 membrana 指薄皮、羊皮纸或身体某部分的表面。英语在 15 世纪借入，用于解剖上的覆盖层。

items.en: Many dictionaries connect membrana with membrum, 'limb, member of the body'. The connection is plausible but not proven, so it is uncertain.
items.cn: 许多词典把 membrana 与 membrum「肢体、身体的一部分」联系起来。这一联系看似合理但未被证实，属于来源不确定。

items.en: As microscopy revealed thin boundaries in plants and animals, membrane became the general word for any such layer. Hooke and his contemporaries described membranes in cork and in tissue.
items.cn: 显微镜揭示动植物中的薄边界之后，membrane 成为指这类薄层的通用词。Hooke 及其同代描述了软木与组织中的膜。

items.en: Cell theory gave the cell membrane its modern role as the boundary of the cell. The phrase cell membrane is 19th century or later.
items.cn: 细胞学说赋予细胞膜「细胞边界」的现代角色。cell membrane 这一说法出现于 19 世纪或更晚。

items.en: In the 20th century the lipid bilayer, membrane proteins and membrane potential became standard terms in biophysics.
items.cn: 20 世纪，脂质双分子层、膜蛋白与膜电位成为生物物理学的标准术语。

note.en: The first group separates membrane from words for its material and from the specific cell boundary; the second separates it from other thin layers and coverings.
note.cn: 第一组把 membrane 与指其材料的词以及专指细胞边界的词分开；第二组把它与其它薄层和覆盖物分开。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of membrane' or 'membrane-like'; membrane is the countable noun.
entries.definitionCN: 是形容词，意为「膜的」或「膜状的」；membrane 是可数名词。

entries.definition: A person in a group or a limb; it may share a Latin source with membrane, but its meaning is unrelated to thin layers.
entries.definitionCN: 指群体中的成员或肢体；它可能与 membrane 共享拉丁来源，但词义与薄层无关。

entries.definition: A small membrane-like structure in a cell, used in specialist biology; it is not a general synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞中膜状的小结构，属于专业生物学术语，不是通用同义词。

entries.definition: A thin layer of any material, often on a surface; a membrane usually separates two spaces and has a function.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何材料的薄层，常附在表面；membrane 通常分隔两个空间并具有功能。

entries.definition: A layer covering the inside of something; a mucous membrane is a lining, but not every lining is a membrane.
entries.definitionCN: 指覆盖在内部的一层；黏膜是一种内衬，但不是所有内衬都是膜。

entries.definition: Anything that blocks movement; a membrane can act as a barrier but may also let selected substances through.
entries.definitionCN: 指阻挡运动的东西；膜可以起屏障作用，但也可能让特定物质通过。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin membrana 'thin skin': a sheet that separates two spaces.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 membrana「薄皮」：把两个空间隔开的一层薄片。

normal.en: The family runs membranous, membranal, membranelle, membrane-bound and bilayer.
normal.cn: 同族词有 membranous、membranal、membranelle、membrane-bound、bilayer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: cell membrane, mucous membrane, tympanic membrane, semipermeable membrane.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：细胞膜、黏膜、鼓膜、半透膜。

normal.en: The same word covers a soap bubble film, an eardrum and a stadium roof.
normal.cn: 同一个词涵盖肥皂泡的薄膜、鼓膜与体育场屋顶。

normal.en: A membrane is defined by being thin and by separating something.
normal.cn: 膜的定义特征就是薄，并且把某物隔开。

abstract.en: A membrane is a border checkpoint: it does not just block, it chooses.
abstract.cn: 膜像一个边境检查站：它不只是阻挡，还会选择。

abstract.en: Think of a drum: a stretched skin turns a hit into a sound, and a cell membrane turns a signal into a response.
abstract.cn: 想象一面鼓：绷紧的皮把敲击变成声音，细胞膜则把信号变成反应。

abstract.en: A stadium roof is a membrane holding up the sky, the same thin sheet doing a structural job.
abstract.cn: 体育场屋顶像一层托住天空的膜，同样是薄片承担结构任务。

examples.en: The cell membrane controls which ions enter the cell.
examples.cn: 细胞膜控制哪些离子进入细胞。

examples.en: A semipermeable membrane lets water through but holds salt back.
examples.cn: 半透膜让水通过，却把盐挡住。

examples.en: The mucous membrane of the nose traps dust and viruses.
examples.cn: 鼻腔黏膜会截留灰尘与病毒。

root: 拉丁语 membrana「薄皮、羊皮纸」→ 英语 membrane；与 membrum「肢体」的联系看似合理但未证实。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all describe a thin layer with a job: separating, covering, filtering, vibrating, or carrying a voltage. The cell membrane, mucous lining, filter, eardrum, roof and drumhead are all the same shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都描述一层有任务的薄层：分隔、覆盖、过滤、振动或承载电压。细胞膜、黏膜、滤膜、鼓膜、屋顶与鼓面都是同一种形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin flexible skin that separates two sides and lets some things through.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层薄而有弹性的皮，把两边隔开，允许某些东西通过。

branches.en: THE GENERAL LAYER: any thin sheet that divides two regions.
branches.cn: 一般薄层：任何把两个区域分开的薄片。

branches.en: THE CELL BOUNDARY: the membrane itself, its proteins, and the voltage across it.
branches.cn: 细胞边界：膜本身、它的蛋白，以及跨膜的电压。

branches.en: ANATOMICAL LINING: the wet membrane covering a body cavity.
branches.cn: 解剖内衬：覆盖体腔的湿润薄膜。

branches.en: FUNCTIONAL SHEETS: synthetic filters and the eardrum.
branches.cn: 功能性薄片：人工滤膜与鼓膜。

branches.en: ENGINEERED AND VIBRATING: tensile roofs and the stretched diaphragm of instruments.
branches.cn: 工程与振动：张拉屋顶与乐器、麦克风的绷紧膜片。

intro.en: Membrane is a Latin noun with no prefix; its family is built with -ous, -al and the diminutive -elle.

latinIntro.en: Latin membrana supplies the root; the adjective ending -ous comes from Latin -osus, and -elle is a French/Latin diminutive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 membrana 提供词根；形容词词尾 -ous 来自拉丁语 -osus，-elle 是法语与拉丁语的指小成分。

definition_zh: 地形；地势；一片土地的自然特征
definition_en: the physical features and surface of a tract of land, especially as they affect movement or use
core_image: 越野车在碎石坡上颠簸前行，车轮下是坑洼与松石
scene: 越野车驶上碎石坡，车身随坑洼剧烈起伏，司机不断换挡： The jeep struggled over rough terrain full of loose stones.
sceneCN: 这里 terrain 指「一片土地的地形与地表状况」（第 1 个义项：土地的自然起伏与表面特征）；句意为越野车在遍布松石的崎岖地形中艰难前行。

pos.zh: 地形；地势；地带（可数或不可数，复数为 terrains）

senses.title: The physical features of land
senses.titleCN: 土地的自然起伏与表面特征
senses.definition: the shape, slope, and surface of a piece of land, including hills, rocks, and gullies
senses.definitionCN: 一片土地的形状、坡度与表面，包括山丘、岩石与冲沟
senses.example: The jeep struggled over rough terrain full of loose stones.
senses.exampleCN: 越野车在遍布松石的崎岖地形中艰难前行。
senses.why: Terrain comes from Latin terra 'earth', so it names the earth as something you must cross rather than something you own.
senses.whyCN: terrain 来自拉丁语 terra「土地」，因此它把土地命名为需要穿越的东西，而非拥有的东西。

senses.title: A tract of land for a purpose
senses.titleCN: 供某种用途的一片土地
senses.definition: an area of land considered as a unit for building, farming, or military use
senses.definitionCN: 作为建设、耕作或军事用途单位来考虑的一片土地
senses.example: The engineers surveyed the terrain before laying the foundation.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在打地基前勘测了这片土地。
senses.why: A tract becomes terrain when its physical character matters to what you plan to do on it.
senses.whyCN: 当一片土地的自然特征影响你打算做的事时，它就成为 terrain。

senses.title: Ground that affects movement
senses.definition: the surface conditions that help or hinder travel, especially for vehicles and troops
senses.definitionCN: 帮助或阻碍通行、尤其影响车辆与部队行动的地面状况
senses.example: The tanks slowed in the soft terrain near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 坦克在河边的松软地形中减速。
senses.why: Military usage made terrain a technical term: what the ground does to movement, not how it looks in a picture.
senses.whyCN: 军事用法使 terrain 成为技术术语：地面如何影响行动，而非照片上好不好看。

senses.title: Rough and difficult country
senses.definition: land that is broken, steep, or obstructed enough to make travel slow and dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 破碎、陡峭或受阻到使行进缓慢危险的土地
senses.example: Rescuers carried the injured climber across difficult terrain.
senses.exampleCN: 救援者抬着受伤的攀登者穿越难行地形。
senses.why: The word often carries an adjective of difficulty because terrain is defined by resistance to movement.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常与「困难」类形容词连用，因为 terrain 的定义就与对移动的阻力有关。

senses.title: Land represented in a model
senses.definition: a digital or physical representation of the land surface used in planning, games, or simulation
senses.definitionCN: 用于规划、游戏或仿真的地表数字或实体再现
senses.example: The game renders terrain down to individual boulders.
senses.exampleCN: 游戏把地形渲染到每一块巨石。
senses.why: Once land is data, terrain means the surface mesh: elevation, slope, and texture stored in a file.
senses.whyCN: 当土地变成数据，terrain 就指表面网格：存于文件中的高程、坡度与纹理。

senses.title: Habitat defined by ground features
senses.titleCN: 由地面特征定义的栖息地
senses.definition: the physical ground conditions that determine which species can live in an area
senses.definitionCN: 决定哪些物种能在某地生存的地面物理条件
senses.example: The lizard prefers rocky terrain with deep crevices.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蜥蜴偏好有深裂缝的岩石地形。
senses.why: For a small animal, slope and rock size are not scenery but shelter, so terrain becomes habitat.
senses.whyCN: 对小动物而言，坡度与石块大小不是风景，而是庇护所，因此地形成为栖息地。

senses.title: Abstract: an unfamiliar field
senses.definition: a field of knowledge or activity, pictured as ground to be crossed
senses.definitionCN: 被想象成需要穿越的地面的知识或活动领域
senses.example: The book leads readers through uncharted terrain in philosophy.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书带读者穿越哲学中未标注的领域。
senses.why: The metaphor treats knowledge as landscape: some parts are mapped, others are rough and unknown.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把知识当作地貌：有些部分已测绘，另一些则崎岖未知。

senses.title: Ski and outdoor park terrain
senses.definition: constructed or natural ground features used for skiing, biking, or off-road recreation
senses.definitionCN: 用于滑雪、骑行或越野休闲的人工或天然地面特征
senses.example: The resort opened a new terrain park for beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 度假村为初学者新开了一座地形公园。
senses.why: Recreation borrows the word for shaped ground: jumps, rails, and slopes are terrain made on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 休闲领域借这个词指被塑形的地面：跳台、栏杆与坡面都是刻意造出的地形。

intro.en: Terrain comes from French, from Latin terrenum 'earth, ground', built on terra. The Latin root is well attested. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: terrain 经法语来自拉丁语 terrenum「土地、地面」，由 terra 构成。拉丁词根书证充分。年代均为约数。

items.en: Terra meant 'earth, land, ground'. It goes back to a reconstructed root for dry land, seen also in territory and terrestrial.
items.cn: terra 意为「土地、陆地、地面」。它可上溯到一个表示干地的重构词根，亦见于 territory 与 terrestrial。

items.en: Terrenum meant 'earthly ground, land', the neuter form of terrenus 'of earth'.
items.cn: terrenum 意为「地上的土地」，是 terrenus「土地的」的中性形式。

items.en: French terrain carried the sense of ground considered for its surface and quality, especially in hunting and military writing.
items.cn: 法语 terrain 带有「就表面与性质而言的地面」之义，尤其见于狩猎与军事文献。

items.en: English borrowed terrain in the eighteenth century, chiefly in military and surveying contexts.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪借入 terrain，主要用于军事与测量语境。

items.en: Modeling, gaming, and recreation added new senses in the twentieth century; their first dates are not precisely recorded.
items.cn: 建模、游戏与休闲在 20 世纪增添新义，其最早年代没有精确记载。

note.en: Group one holds land-description words that are easily confused with terrain; group two holds words for land as property, surface, or setting.
note.cn: 第一组是易与 terrain 混淆的土地描述词；第二组是把土地视为财产、表面或环境的词。

entries.definition: An area under a state's control; it stresses ownership and boundaries rather than surface shape.
entries.definitionCN: 受国家控制的区域；强调所有权与边界，而非地表形状。

entries.definition: Relating to the earth or to land as opposed to water; it describes a realm, not a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 与地球或陆地（相对于水）有关；它描述领域，而非地表。

entries.definition: The Latin word for earth, used in scientific compounds such as terra incognita.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语「土地」一词，用于 terra incognita 等学术短语。

entries.definition: The systematic description of surface features and elevations; terrain is the ground as experienced, topography as measured.
entries.definitionCN: 对地表特征与高程的系统描述；terrain 是体验到的地面，topography 是测量出的地形。

entries.definition: The visible appearance of an area, including vegetation and human features; it is what you see, not what you cross.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地区的可见外观，包括植被与人工要素；它是你看到的，而非你穿越的。

entries.definition: The surface you stand on; it is neutral and lacks terrain's implication of difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 你站立其上的表面；它是中性的，不含 terrain 那种困难意味。

entries.definition: The difference in height across an area; it is one measurable property of terrain.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地区内的高度差；它是地形的一项可测属性。

definition_zh: 动机；内在动力；积极性；动因；激励；目的；学习动机；动机陈述
definition_en: the reason or reasons why a person acts in a certain way, or the inner drive and enthusiasm that keeps a person acting
core_image: 一个人看着山顶的小旗，脚下一级一级往上踩，没有人在背后推他
scene: 这里指「动机」。 No one pushes him; he keeps climbing toward a small flag on the summit because the flag is his own: that inner push is motivation.
sceneCN: 这里 motivation 是「动机」（第 1 个义项：内在动力）；句意：没有人推他，他仍一级一级朝山顶的小旗往上走，因为那面旗是他自己的，这股内在的推力就是动机。图中可辨识物件：登山者、石阶、山顶小旗、远处的云、没有第二个人。

derivatives.zh: 有积极性的；有明确动机的

senses.title: The inner drive: wanting to act
senses.definition: the inner drive or desire that makes a person want to act or keep acting
senses.definitionCN: 使人愿意开始行动、并持续行动的内在推力或愿望
senses.example: Her motivation came from curiosity rather than from money.
senses.exampleCN: 她的动力来自好奇，而不是金钱。
senses.why: Latin motivus means 'moving', from movere 'to move'. Motivation is therefore the moving force inside a person: what sets an action going when nobody pushes from outside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 motivus 意为「使动的」，出自 movere「移动」。因此 motivation 就是人内部的推动力：在无人从外面推时让行动启动的东西。

senses.title: Enthusiasm and drive that keep going
senses.titleCN: 积极性、干劲：还能继续做下去
senses.definition: the enthusiasm, energy or willingness that sustains effort over time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内维持努力的干劲、精力或意愿
senses.example: The team lost motivation after the third delay.
senses.exampleCN: 第三次延期之后，团队失去了干劲。
senses.why: A single reason starts an action; sustained enthusiasm keeps it running. English uses motivation for both the spark and the fuel, which is why one can lose motivation without having lost a reason.
senses.whyCN: 单个理由能启动行动，持续的干劲则让它继续运转。英语用 motivation 兼指火花与燃料，所以人可能并未失去理由，却失去了动力。

senses.title: A reason or cause for behaviour
senses.definition: the reason or reasons behind a particular action, often examined by others
senses.definitionCN: 某一具体行为背后的理由，常由他人加以审视
senses.example: Investigators questioned the motivation behind the payment.
senses.exampleCN: 调查人员质疑这笔付款背后的动机。
senses.why: From 'the mover' the word shifts to 'the reason moved'. When others ask about motivation, they are asking what cause could produce such an act.
senses.whyCN: 从「推动者」转为「被推动的理由」。当他人追问 motivation 时，问的是什么样的原因会产生这样的行为。

senses.title: Drive in psychology: a directed force
senses.titleCN: 心理学中的驱力：有方向的力量
senses.definition: in psychology, the internal state that directs behaviour toward a goal, studied as a measurable construct
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指引导行为指向目标的内在状态，被当作可测量的构念来研究
senses.example: The experiment manipulated motivation by varying the reward.
senses.exampleCN: 实验通过改变奖励来操纵动机水平。
senses.why: Psychology turned the everyday word into a variable. Here motivation is not a compliment but something that can be raised, lowered and measured across groups.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把这个日常词变成了一个变量。这里的 motivation 不是称赞，而是可以升高、降低并在组间测量比较的东西。

senses.title: Incentive in management: getting people to perform
senses.titleCN: 管理中的激励：让人愿意干
senses.definition: the practice of encouraging employees or members to work harder, as in employee motivation
senses.definitionCN: 鼓励员工或成员更努力工作的做法，如「员工激励」
senses.example: The bonus scheme was designed to improve motivation.
senses.exampleCN: 奖金方案的设计目的是提升积极性。
senses.why: Management speaks of motivation as something an organisation can supply or damage. The inner drive is treated as a resource that leadership can influence.
senses.whyCN: 管理学把 motivation 说成组织可以提供或损害的东西。内在动力被当作一种领导层能够影响的资源。

senses.title: Purpose: the aim behind an act
senses.definition: the purpose or goal that an action is intended to serve
senses.definitionCN: 某一行为意图服务的目的或目标
senses.example: The motivation for the reform was to cut waiting times.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革的目的是缩短等候时间。
senses.why: A motive can be a future state that pulls rather than a past cause that pushes. English lets motivation cover both, which is why it can mean 'reason' and 'goal' at once.
senses.whyCN: 动机既可以是向前拉的未来状态，也可以是向后推的过去原因。英语让 motivation 两者都覆盖，所以它同时能指「理由」与「目的」。

senses.title: Learning motivation: why students engage
senses.titleCN: 学习动机：学生为何投入
senses.definition: in education, the willingness of a learner to engage with and persist at learning tasks
senses.definitionCN: 教育中指学习者愿意投入学习任务并坚持下去的意愿
senses.example: Task choice strongly affects learning motivation.
senses.exampleCN: 任务的选择对学习动机影响很大。
senses.why: Education studies motivation because engagement cannot be commanded. The word names the learner's own side of the bargain, which the teacher can only influence.
senses.whyCN: 教育学之所以研究动机，因为投入无法被命令。这个词命名的是学习者自己那一半的交易，教师只能施加影响。

senses.title: A motivation letter: the statement of intent
senses.titleCN: 动机陈述：写下来的「我为何而来」
senses.definition: a written statement explaining why one is applying for a course, job or grant, often called a motivation letter
senses.definitionCN: 说明为何申请某项课程、职位或资助的书面陈述，常称动机信
senses.example: Her motivation letter explained the gap in her studies.
senses.exampleCN: 她的动机信解释了她学业上的那段空白。
senses.why: Institutions cannot see inner drive, so they ask for it in writing. The word then names a document, and the abstract noun becomes a page in an application.
senses.whyCN: 机构看不见内在动力，于是要求把它写出来。这个词于是指一份文件，抽象名词变成申请表里的一页。

intro.en: Motivation is motive plus -ation. Motive comes from Latin motivus 'serving to move', from movere 'to move' with its participle motus. English uses motive from the 15th century for a reason for acting, and motivation is a 19th-century noun that psychology made technical in the 20th. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: motivation 是 motive 加 -ation。motive 出自拉丁语 motivus「使动的」，源自 movere「移动」，其分词为 motus。英语自 15 世纪用 motive 指行为的理由，motivation 则是 19 世纪的名词，20 世纪被心理学专业化。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Motivation becomes a technical term in psychology and management, and intrinsic and extrinsic are fixed as its two poles.
items.cn: motivation 在心理学与管理学中成为技术术语，intrinsic（内在的）与 extrinsic（外在的）被固定为它的两极。

items.en: English motivation is recorded, naming the act of providing a motive or the state of having one.
items.cn: 英语 motivation 见于记载，指提供动机的行为或具有动机的状态。

items.en: Motive enters English from Old French, meaning a reason that prompts an action.
items.cn: motive 经古法语进入英语，指促使行动的理由。

items.en: motivus is 'serving to move', built on movere 'to move', whose participle motus also gives motion and emotion.
items.cn: motivus 意为「使动的」，建立在 movere「移动」上，其分词 motus 还给出 motion 与 emotion。

items.en: movere goes back to a reconstructed root *meue- 'to push away', which also underlies move and remove.
items.cn: movere 可追溯到重构词根 *meue-「推开」，该词根也支撑 move 与 remove。

note.en: The first group separates real relatives from a look-alike; the second compares words that each name part of what motivation covers.
note.cn: 第一组把真正的同族词与一个形近词分开；第二组比较分别覆盖 motivation 一部分的近义词。

entries.definition: a reason for acting, often in a criminal or hidden sense. It is the concrete reason, while motivation can also mean the general drive.
entries.definitionCN: 行为的理由，常带犯罪或隐秘色彩。它指具体理由，而 motivation 也可指总体动力。

entries.definition: the act of moving, or a formal proposal. It shares motus with motivation but names physical movement or a parliamentary step.
entries.definitionCN: 移动的动作，或正式提案。它与 motivation 共享 motus，但指物理移动或议会程序。

entries.definition: a partial change. It comes from modus 'measure', not movere 'move', and shares only the -ification shape of the ending.
entries.definitionCN: 局部改动。它出自 modus「尺度」，而非 movere「移动」，只在词尾形状上相似。

entries.definition: something offered to make people act, such as a bonus. It is the external object, while motivation can be internal.
entries.definitionCN: 为促使人们行动而提供的东西，如奖金。它是外部之物，而 motivation 可以是内部的。

entries.definition: a strong inner urge to act or achieve. It is close to motivation but stresses force and energy rather than reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 行动或成就的强烈内在冲动。它接近 motivation，但强调力量与能量，而非理由。

entries.definition: strong liking and eagerness. It describes the feeling, while motivation also covers the reason behind the feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的喜爱与热切。它描述感觉，而 motivation 还包含感觉背后的理由。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: movere 'to move' gives motive, motion, emotion, promote and remove: all involve setting something in motion.
normal.cn: movere「移动」给出 motive、motion、emotion、promote、remove，全都涉及让某物动起来。

normal.en: -ation makes an action noun, so motivation is the business of having or giving a motive.
normal.cn: -ation 构成动作名词，因此 motivation 就是「有动机或给动机」这件事。

normal.en: intrinsic motivation is the motive inside the task; extrinsic motivation is the motive outside it.
normal.cn: intrinsic motivation（内在动机）是任务内部的动机；extrinsic motivation（外在动机）是任务外部的动机。

normal.en: A motive is usually the specific reason; motivation can be that reason or the general drive.
normal.cn: motive 通常是具体理由；motivation 既可以是那个理由，也可以是总体动力。

normal.en: A motivation letter writes down what an institution cannot see.
normal.cn: 动机信写下的，正是机构看不见的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a climber with no one behind him, only a flag ahead that he chose himself.
abstract.cn: 想象一名登山者，身后无人，前方只有他自己选定的那面旗。

abstract.en: Motivation is both the push and the pull: a cause already past, and a goal still ahead.
abstract.cn: 动机既是推也是拉：既是已经过去的原因，也是尚在前方的目标。

abstract.en: The word always asks why anyone bothered, and whether they will bother again tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 这个词总在问：为什么有人愿意费这个劲，以及明天还愿不愿意。

examples.en: Curiosity was the strongest motivation behind her research.
examples.cn: 好奇心是她研究背后最强的动机。

examples.en: Poor pay can destroy motivation faster than long hours.
examples.cn: 低薪比长时间工作更快地摧毁积极性。

examples.en: The course asks for a short motivation letter in English.
examples.cn: 这门课程要求提交一份简短的英文动机信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩托为神」——心里有台摩托在推，人自己就往前冲 → motivation 动机、动力

root: 拉丁语 movere「移动」→ motivus「使动的」→ 古法语 motif → 英语 motive；加 -ation → motivation。核心是「让人动起来的那股力」，既可以是背后的理由，也可以是前方的目标。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: an inner push that starts and sustains action. What changes is the frame — a personal drive, lasting enthusiasm, a reason others investigate, a psychological variable, a management task, a goal, a learner's engagement, or a written statement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：一股启动并维持行动的内在推力。变化的只是框架——个人动力、持久干劲、他人追查的理由、心理学变量、管理任务、一个目标、学习者的投入，还是一份书面陈述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a climber ascending toward a flag he chose, with nobody pushing.
core.cn: 核心意象：登山者朝他选定的旗子往上走，背后没有人推。

branches.en: THE INNER PUSH: movere supplies the force, which both starts an action and keeps it running.
branches.cn: 内在推力：movere 提供力量，既启动行动，也维持行动。

branches.en: REASON AND PURPOSE: the mover can be a past cause or a future goal, and others may examine either.
branches.cn: 理由与目的：推动者可以是过去的原因，也可以是未来的目标，他人都可能审视其中之一。

branches.en: THE VARIABLE: psychology treats the inner push as something that can be raised, lowered and measured.
branches.cn: 变量：心理学把内在推力当作可升高、可降低、可测量的东西。

branches.en: THE MANAGED AND THE TAUGHT: organisations try to supply it, and education studies how learners bring their own.
branches.cn: 被管理与被教导的：组织试图提供它，教育则研究学习者如何自带它。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT: when inner drive must be shown, it is written down as a motivation letter.
branches.cn: 文件：当内在动力需要被展示时，它被写成一份动机信。

intro.en: Motivation is motive plus -ation. The ending -ation names an action or state; motive is Latin motivus, from movere 'to move'.
intro.cn: motivation 是 motive 加 -ation。词尾 -ation 表示动作或状态；motive 是拉丁语 motivus，出自 movere「移动」。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb is movere 'to move', with participle motus and adjective motivus. The same verb gives motion, emotion, promote, remote and remove.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词是 movere「移动」，分词 motus，形容词 motivus。同一个动词还给出 motion、emotion、promote、remote、remove。

items.meaning: the drive or reason for acting
items.example: Her motivation was to help her village.
items.exampleCN: 她的动机是帮助自己的村子。

items.meaning: to give someone a reason to act
items.example: Good teachers motivate students.
items.exampleCN: 好老师能激励学生。

items.meaning: having a reason or drive to act
items.meaningCN: 有积极性的；动机明确的
items.example: The team was highly motivated.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队积极性很高。

items.meaning: relating to motivation, or able to inspire it
items.example: He gave a short motivational talk.
items.exampleCN: 他做了一段简短的激励讲话。

items.example: Praise is a weak motivator over time.
items.exampleCN: 长期来看，表扬是很弱的激励因素。

items.structure: Latin motivus through Old French motif
items.example: The police looked for a motive.
items.exampleCN: 警方在寻找动机。

items.example: The motion was carried by a vote.
items.exampleCN: 这项动议经表决通过。

items.meaning: a feeling that moves a person outward
items.meaningCN: 情绪（字面「把人向外推动的东西」）
items.example: The speech stirred strong emotion.
items.exampleCN: 这番讲话激起了强烈的情绪。

items.meaning: to move someone or something forward
items.meaningCN: 促进；提升；推广（pro- 表示向前）
items.example: The campaign promoted healthy eating.
items.exampleCN: 这项运动推广健康饮食。

items.example: They removed the damaged beam.
items.exampleCN: 他们拆掉了受损的横梁。

latinEntries.meaning: to move, to set in motion
forms a noun of action or state

definition_zh: 作为对……的回应；为回应……；针对……（作出反应）
definition_en: as an answer or reaction to something said, done or experienced
core_image: 服务台收到一封投诉信，主管当天就拟好回复
scene: 服务台收到一封投诉信，主管当天就拟好回复。 The company changed its policy in response to customer complaints.
sceneCN: 这里取「回应投诉」（第 3 个义项：针对批评或投诉作出反应）；句意为公司因客户投诉而改变了政策。

pos.zh: 介词短语：作为对……的回应；针对……

senses.title: Answering a question or request
senses.definition: used to say that something is said or done as an answer
senses.definitionCN: 表示某话或某动作是作为回答而作出
senses.example: The note was written in response to a direct question.
senses.exampleCN: 这张便条是针对一个直接提问写的。
senses.why: The phrase points backward to a stimulus and forward to the answer, so it naturally follows verbs of replying.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语向后指向刺激、向前指向回答，因此天然跟在答复类动词之后。

senses.title: Reacting to an event
senses.definition: used to describe a reaction to something that has happened rather than a verbal answer
senses.definitionCN: 描述对已发生之事的反应，而非口头回答
senses.example: Prices fell in response to the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 价格因这项公告而下跌。
senses.why: Here the answer is not words but a change in behaviour, which widens the phrase beyond conversation.
senses.whyCN: 此处的回应不是言语，而是行为变化，于是短语超出会话范围。

senses.title: Answering criticism or complaints
senses.definition: used when an organization reacts to complaints or public criticism
senses.definitionCN: 在机构对投诉或公众批评作出反应时使用
senses.example: The company changed its policy in response to customer complaints.
senses.exampleCN: 公司因客户投诉而改变了政策。
senses.why: Institutional writing uses the phrase to show that a change was forced by outside pressure, not chosen freely.
senses.whyCN: 机构文字借此显示改变由外部压力促成，而非自由选择。

senses.title: Reacting to medical treatment
senses.definition: used in clinical writing to describe how a body or illness reacts to treatment
senses.definitionCN: 在临床写作中，描述身体或疾病对治疗的反应
senses.example: The tumour shrank in response to the new drug.
senses.exampleCN: 肿瘤对这种新药产生了反应而缩小。
senses.why: Clinical prose needs a neutral way to describe improvement or failure without naming a cause with certainty.
senses.whyCN: 临床文字需要一个中性说法，不确定地描述好转或无效。

senses.title: Policy reaction to pressure or prices
senses.titleCN: 市场与政策：应对压力、价格
senses.definition: used to describe a policy move taken because of market or political pressure
senses.definitionCN: 描述因市场或政治压力而采取的政策动作
senses.example: Interest rates were raised in response to rising prices.
senses.exampleCN: 为应对物价上涨，利率被提高。
senses.why: Policy writing uses the phrase to tie a measure to a pressure without claiming that the pressure was the only cause.
senses.whyCN: 政策文字借此把措施与压力挂钩，又不宣称压力是唯一原因。

senses.title: The news-style opening
senses.definition: placed at the start of a report to name the trigger before the action
senses.definitionCN: 置于报道开头，先点名触发因素，再说行动
senses.example: In response to the outbreak, the city closed its schools.
senses.exampleCN: 针对疫情暴发，这座城市关闭了学校。
senses.why: News prose front-loads the trigger so the action reads as a consequence, which is why the phrase often opens a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 新闻文字把触发因素前置，使行动读起来像结果，因此这个短语常开句。

senses.title: Replying to a letter or request in official style
senses.definition: used at the start of official correspondence to name the letter being answered
senses.definitionCN: 在公函开头点出所答复的来信
senses.example: In response to your letter of the fifth, we enclose the file.
senses.exampleCN: 针对你方五日来函，随信附上档案。
senses.why: Official letters need a formula that names the incoming document without repeating its contents.
senses.whyCN: 公函需要一个套语，点出来文而不重复其内容。

senses.title: A bodily reaction to a stimulus
senses.definition: used in science to describe a living system's reaction to a stimulus
senses.definitionCN: 在科学文字中，描述生命系统对刺激的反应
senses.example: The pupil narrows in response to bright light.
senses.exampleCN: 瞳孔对强光作出反应而收缩。
senses.why: Scientific writing uses the phrase for automatic reactions that need no intention behind them.
senses.whyCN: 科学文字借此描述无需意图的自动反应。

intro.en: Response comes from Latin responsum, from respondere, to answer, itself re-, back, and spondere, to pledge. The Latin line is clear; the English phrase is modern.
intro.cn: response 来自拉丁语 responsum，词根 respondere 意为「回答」，由 re-「回」与 spondere「承诺」构成。拉丁语线索清楚，英语短语属近代。

items.en: Spondere meant to pledge or promise, and survives in sponsor and spouse.
items.cn: spondere 意为许诺、承诺，仍见于 sponsor 与 spouse。

items.en: Respondere meant to answer, literally to pledge back.
items.cn: respondere 意为回答，字面是「回以承诺」。

items.en: The noun named the answer given, and Old French response carried it to English.
items.cn: 这个名词指给出的回答，古法语 response 把它带入英语。

items.en: English response appears in the Middle English period; the date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 response 见于中古英语，年代为约数。

items.en: The phrase with this preposition and to settles in modern official and scientific writing.
items.cn: 带这个介词与 to 的短语在近代官方与科学文字中定型。

note.en: The first group also points to a trigger but stresses connection, cause or rejection; the second group holds plainer phrases of reaction.
note.cn: 第一组同样指向触发因素，但侧重关联、原因或拒斥；第二组是更朴素的反应说法。

entries.definition: It stresses a response to a stimulus, often immediate and emotional.
entries.definitionCN: 它强调对刺激的反应，常是即时且情绪化的。

entries.definition: It is used for words in return, especially in letters.
entries.definitionCN: 它只用于回话，尤见于书信。

entries.definition: It is a formal way to name the question being answered.
entries.definitionCN: 正式点出所回答的问题。

entries.definition: It links two matters without any answering.
entries.definitionCN: 它只连接两件事，不含回答。

entries.definition: It describes a response without naming the trigger as a prepositional object.
entries.definitionCN: 描述反应，但不把触发因素作介词宾语。

entries.definition: It turns the response into an action in progress.
entries.definitionCN: 把回应写成正在进行的动作。

entries.definition: It gives a cause and has no answering sense.
entries.definitionCN: 它给出原因，没有回答之意。

entries.definition: It explains why something happened rather than what it answers.
entries.definitionCN: 解释事情为何发生，而非回应什么。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pledge root, the real trigger types and the real register.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实「承诺」词根、真实触发类型与真实语域。

normal.en: To respond is to pledge back, so the word carries an answer returned to a source.
normal.cn: 回应就是回以承诺，因此这个词带着一个还回源头的答复。

normal.en: It takes a noun, never a clause.
normal.cn: 它接名词，从不接从句。

normal.en: The trigger may be a question, a complaint, a price, a drug or a light.
normal.cn: 触发因素可以是提问、投诉、价格、药物或光。

normal.en: It is neutral about cause: the phrase ties a reaction to a trigger without proving it.
normal.cn: 它对因果保持中性：把反应与触发因素挂钩，却不证明因果。

normal.en: News and official prose front it so the action reads as a consequence.
normal.cn: 新闻与公文常把它前置，使行动读作结果。

abstract.en: Like a letter arriving and an answer leaving the same desk on the same day.
abstract.cn: 像一封信送到，当天同一张桌上就有回信发出。

abstract.en: Like a thermostat switching on because the room turned cold.
abstract.cn: 像恒温器因屋子变冷而启动。

abstract.en: Like an echo that returns only to the wall it came from.
abstract.cn: 像只朝来处返回的回声。

examples.en: The firm issued a statement in response to the rumours.
examples.cn: 公司针对谣言发表了一份声明。

examples.en: In response to the drought, the city limited water use.
examples.cn: 为应对旱情，城市限制了用水。

examples.en: The patient improved in response to the second course of treatment.
examples.cn: 病人在第二个疗程后有所好转。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因 瑞斯庞斯 图」——信一到，回信当天就走：作为回应

root: response 来自拉丁语 responsum，词根 respondere「回答」由 re-「回」与 spondere「承诺」构成，经古法语进入英语；短语 in response to 在近代官方与科学文字中定型，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split by the trigger and the kind of answer: a question, an event, a complaint, a treatment, a market pressure, a news opening, an official letter, and a bodily stimulus.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按触发因素与回应方式区分：提问、事件、投诉、治疗、市场压力、新闻开头、公函来文、生理刺激。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a complaint letter arriving and a reply leaving the same desk the same day.
core.cn: 核心意象：投诉信送到，当天同一张桌上发出回信。

branches.en: THE ANSWER: questions and official letters receive a direct reply.
branches.cn: 回答：提问与公函得到直接答复。

branches.en: THE EVENT: an action is tied to what set it off.
branches.cn: 事件：行动被绑到引发它的事情上。

branches.en: THE PRESSURE: complaints and market moves force a policy change.
branches.cn: 压力：投诉与市场变动迫使政策改变。

branches.en: THE BODY: treatment and stimuli produce reactions without intention.
branches.cn: 身体：治疗与刺激产生无意图的反应。

branches.en: THE FRAME: fronting makes the action read as a consequence.
branches.cn: 框架：前置使行动读作结果。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin noun of answering with an English preposition; the Latin core is clear.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语「回答」名词与英语介词结合；拉丁核心清楚。

latinIntro.en: The Latin etyma are respondere, to answer, and spondere, to pledge.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词源是 respondere「回答」与 spondere「承诺」。

items.example: The verb also underlies sponsor and spouse.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也是另外两个英语词的基础。

items.example: The prefix sends the pledge back to its source.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把承诺送回源头。

items.example: The noun names the reply itself.
items.exampleCN: 名词直接指答复。

items.example: English widened the noun to include reactions.
items.exampleCN: 英语把名词扩展到反应。

items.example: The verb is the everyday base.
items.exampleCN: 动词是日常基词。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把名词变成性质。

items.example: The suffix names the person answering.
items.exampleCN: 后缀指作出回答的人。

items.example: The phrase is standard in official and scientific prose.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语在官方与科学文字中是标准用法。

definition_zh: 心理表征；心理意象；概念结构；记忆痕迹；语义表征
definition_en: an internal stand-in in the mind for something outside it, such as an object, a scene or a meaning
core_image: 头脑里挂着一张透明地图，用不同形状的标记代替真实街道，却仍能指路。
scene: 闭眼之后，那个人仍能在脑中看见自家厨房的布置，连碗柜把手的位置都清楚。 Even with eyes closed, she can inspect her kitchen through a mental representation built from years of use.
sceneCN: 这里 mental representation 指「头脑中替代外部事物的内部表征」（第 1 个义项：在心中为外部对象建立的替代性结构）；句意为她闭着眼也能凭多年使用形成的心理表征查看厨房。可辨识物件：闭眼的人、厨房轮廓、碗柜、把手标记。

pos.zh: 心理表征；心理意象；概念结构；记忆痕迹

collocations.zh: 对某一物体的心理表征

forms.label: 形容词（表征的；代表性的）

senses.title: An internal stand-in for something
senses.titleCN: 替代外部事物的内部结构
senses.definition: a structure in the mind that stands for an object, scene or state of affairs and allows it to be thought about
senses.definitionCN: 头脑中替代某一物体、场景或事态的结构，使人能够思考该对象
senses.example: Even with eyes closed, she can inspect her kitchen through a mental representation built from years of use.
senses.exampleCN: 即使闭着眼，她也能凭多年使用形成的心理表征查看厨房。
senses.why: The phrase says exactly what it does: a representation is something that stands in for another thing, and mental locates the stand-in inside the mind.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语字面就说清了它的作用：表征是替另一事物站出来的东西，而「心理的」限定这个替身位于头脑之内。

senses.title: A picture-like image in the mind
senses.titleCN: 头脑中类似图画的意象
senses.definition: a representation that has a visual or spatial form, as when someone turns a described room into an imagined picture
senses.definitionCN: 具有视觉或空间形式的表征，例如把人描述的房间变成想象中的画面
senses.example: She formed a mental representation of the room from his description.
senses.exampleCN: 她根据他的描述在脑中形成了那个房间的意象。
senses.why: The word image and the word representation overlap here: the mind keeps the shape of what it has seen or heard described.
senses.whyCN: 「意象」与「表征」在这里重叠：心智保留了所见或所听描述的形状。

senses.title: A structured concept
senses.definition: a representation made of linked features or rules rather than a picture, such as the concept of a bird
senses.definitionCN: 由相互关联的特征或规则构成、而非图画的表征，例如「鸟」这一概念
senses.example: The concept of a bird is a mental representation with feathers, wings and eggs linked inside it.
senses.exampleCN: 「鸟」这一概念是一种心理表征，内部把羽毛、翅膀与蛋联系起来。
senses.why: Thinking needs more than pictures: a concept holds relations, so the same phrase covers an abstract structure.
senses.whyCN: 思考不能只靠图画：概念要保存关系，因此同一个短语也涵盖抽象结构。

senses.title: A trace kept in memory
senses.definition: a stored representation that lets a past experience be recalled after the original event is gone
senses.definitionCN: 被储存起来的表征，使过去经验在原初事件消失后仍能被回忆
senses.example: The smell of chalk revived a mental representation of her first classroom.
senses.exampleCN: 粉笔的气味唤醒了她对第一间教室的心理表征。
senses.why: Memory is the keeping of a stand-in after the thing itself has left, which is precisely what a representation is.
senses.whyCN: 记忆就是在事物本身离开后仍保留一个替身，而这正是表征所做的事。

senses.title: The meaning side of language
senses.definition: the representation of meaning that a speaker attaches to a word or sentence
senses.definitionCN: 说话者赋予词或句子的意义表征
senses.example: Listeners build a mental representation of the sentence as the words arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 听众随着词语到来而逐步构建句子的心理表征。
senses.why: A sentence is not the meaning itself; the mind must construct a stand-in for what the words describe.
senses.whyCN: 句子并不等于意义本身；心智必须为词语所描述的内容构造一个替身。

senses.title: What the senses deliver
senses.definition: a representation formed from seeing, hearing or touching, before any name is attached
senses.definitionCN: 由看、听或触而形成、尚未附带名称的表征
senses.example: The visual mental representation of the face stayed with him longer than the name.
senses.exampleCN: 那张脸的视觉心理表征比名字在他脑中留得更久。
senses.why: Perception already selects and organizes input, so what arrives is a representation rather than the object itself.
senses.whyCN: 知觉已经在筛选与组织输入，因此到达心智的是表征，而非物体本身。

senses.title: A schema or working model
senses.definition: an organized representation that supplies expectations about how a familiar situation usually works
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的表征，为熟悉情境的通常运作方式提供预期
senses.example: Her mental representation of a restaurant told her to wait for a host.
senses.exampleCN: 她对餐馆的心理表征告诉她要先等领位员。
senses.why: A schema is a large representation with slots, so the phrase covers the model a person carries into a familiar scene.
senses.whyCN: 图式是一种带空位的大型表征，因此这个短语也涵盖人带进熟悉场景的心理模型。

senses.title: The content of a belief or desire
senses.definition: the proposition-like content that a belief, hope or fear is directed at
senses.definitionCN: 信念、希望或恐惧所指向的命题式内容
senses.example: Her hope rested on a mental representation of a house she had never seen.
senses.exampleCN: 她的希望寄托在对一栋从未见过的房子的心理表征上。
senses.why: Beliefs are about things even when those things are absent, and the phrase names what the mind is directed at.
senses.whyCN: 即使对象不在场，信念也总关于某物，而这个短语指的就是心智所指向的内容。

intro.en: The phrase joins mental, from Latin mens, mind, to representation, from Latin repraesentare, to bring before the eyes. It became a fixed term in philosophy and later in cognitive science.
intro.cn: 这个短语把来自拉丁 mens「心智」的 mental 与来自拉丁 repraesentare「呈现在眼前」的 representation 连在一起，先成为哲学术语，后成为认知科学术语。

items.en: Mens, with the stem ment-, meant mind, thought or intention. Its deeper origin is generally considered to belong to a reconstructed Indo-European root, but the exact pre-Latin form is not settled.
items.cn: mens（词干 ment-）意为心智、思想或意图。其更早来源一般认为是某个印欧语词根，但拉丁语之前的确切形态尚无定论。

items.en: The verb combined a prefix meaning again or back with praesentare, to present, itself from praesens, being before the eyes. It meant to bring something before someone, or to act in its place.
items.cn: 这个动词由表示「再次、向后」的前缀与 praesentare「呈现」构成，后者又来自 praesens「在眼前」，意为把某物带到某人面前，或代替它行动。

items.en: Mental entered English in the fifteenth century from Late Latin mentalis, and for a long time it named matters of the mind in general rather than images in particular.
items.cn: mental 在十五世纪经晚期拉丁 mentalis 进入英语，很长时间里泛指与心智有关的事，而非专指心中图像。

items.en: Representation came through French and named both the act of showing and the thing shown; the second sense made it useful for what stands in for an object.
items.cn: representation 经法语进入英语，既指展示的动作，也指被展示之物；后一义使它适合用来指替代某物的东西。

items.en: The full phrase became standard in philosophy of mind and in cognitive psychology in the twentieth century, when mental states were routinely described as representations of something.
items.cn: 整个短语在二十世纪的心智哲学与认知心理学中成为标准说法，当时人们习惯把心理状态描述为对某物的表征。

items.en: Source uncertain (first fixed use of the phrase): no single first citation is established for the exact collocation, and the deeper origin of mens is a reconstructed form rather than a demonstrated one.
items.cn: 来源不确定（该短语首次固定使用的时间）：这一确切搭配没有公认的最早书证；mens 的更早来源属重构形式，而非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same two Latin families that are easy to confuse; group two holds other names for what the mind carries.
note.cn: 第一组是两个拉丁词族中容易混淆的词；第二组是心智所携带之物的其他名称。

entries.definition: Anything that stands for something else, from a picture to a legal claim; it needs mental only when the stand-in is in a mind.
entries.definitionCN: 任何替另一物站出来的东西，从图画到法律主张；只有替身位于头脑中时才需要加 mental。

entries.definition: Someone or something chosen to speak or stand for a larger group; it is a role, not a mental structure.
entries.definitionCN: 被选出来为更大群体发言或代表其的人或物；它指角色，不是心理结构。

entries.definition: Relating to the mind; it says where something happens, while the full phrase says what kind of structure is there.
entries.definitionCN: 与心智有关的；它说明事情发生在哪里，而整个短语说明那里存在何种结构。

entries.definition: A way of thinking characteristic of a person or group; it is a style of thought, not a stand-in for an object.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或群体特有的思维方式；它是思想风格，不是某物的替身。

entries.definition: A visual picture in the mind; it is one kind of mental representation, the kind that has spatial form.
entries.definitionCN: 头脑中的视觉画面；它是心理表征的一种，即具有空间形式的那一种。

entries.definition: A general idea built from shared features; a concept is a mental representation with a largely verbal structure.
entries.definitionCN: 由共有特征构成的一般观念；概念是一种以语词结构为主的心理表征。

entries.definition: A large mental frame with slots for the parts of a familiar situation; it is a schema, hence a kind of representation.
entries.definitionCN: 为熟悉情境的各部分留有位置的大型心理框架；它是图式，因而是表征的一种。

entries.definition: A simplified copy used to predict or explain; a mental model is a representation used for reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 用于预测或解释的简化副本；心理模型是用于推理的表征。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin sources, the cognitive science setting and the everyday act of picturing a room.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁来源、认知科学的语境，以及日常在脑中描绘房间的动作。

normal.en: Mental comes from the Latin word for mind; representation comes from a verb meaning to bring before the eyes.
normal.cn: mental 来自拉丁语中表示「心智」的词；representation 来自意为「带到眼前」的动词。

normal.en: A representation is a stand-in: it is not the thing, but it can be inspected in the thing's absence.
normal.cn: 表征是一个替身：它不是事物本身，却能在事物缺席时被查看。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: form a mental representation, a shared mental representation, a visual mental representation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：形成心理表征、共享的心理表征、视觉心理表征。

normal.en: The same noun appears in political representation and in representational art, where the stand-in is public rather than private.
normal.cn: 同一个名词也出现在政治代表与具象艺术中，那里的替身是公开的而非私人的。

normal.en: Cognitive science uses the phrase for concepts, memories and the meanings listeners build from sentences.
normal.cn: 认知科学用这个短语指概念、记忆以及听者从句子中构建的意义。

abstract.en: Picture a transparent map folded inside a pocket, useful only while it stays folded.
abstract.cn: 想象一张透明地图折在口袋里，只有折着的时候才有用。

abstract.en: Picture a theatre model of a city, complete enough to walk through with a finger.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市舞台模型，完整得可以用手指走一遍。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow that keeps the shape of a person after the person has left.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人离开后，影子仍保留他的形状。

examples.en: Two people can hold different mental representations of the same agreement.
examples.cn: 两个人可能对同一份协议持有不同的心理表征。

examples.en: The therapy aims to change the patient's mental representation of failure.
examples.cn: 这种治疗旨在改变患者对失败的心理表征。

examples.en: A map is public, but the route a driver follows is a mental representation.
examples.cn: 地图是公开的，而司机所循的路线是一种心理表征。

dict_mnemonic.text: 在心里给外部世界做一个小替身，替身不在场时也能拿出来看 → 心理表征

root: 拉丁 mens「心智」（词干 ment-）+ 拉丁 repraesentare「带到眼前」= 表示「再次」的前缀 + praesentare「呈现」（来自 praesens「在眼前」）；英语 mental representation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: something stands in for something else inside the mind, and that stand-in can be a picture, a concept, a memory, a meaning, a percept, a schema or the content of a belief.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个观念展开：某物在头脑内部替另一物站出来，而这个替身可以是画面、概念、记忆、意义、知觉、图式或信念的内容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded map carried in a pocket, standing for a city that is far away.
core.cn: 核心意象：口袋里一张折起的地图，替一座远方的城市站出来。

branches.en: THE STAND-IN: the base relation is replacement, not resemblance.
branches.cn: 替身：基础关系是替代，而不是相似。

branches.en: THE SENSES: what is seen or heard arrives already shaped as a picture.
branches.cn: 感官：所见所闻到达心智时已被塑成画面。

branches.en: THE FRAME: features and slots hold relations that a picture cannot.
branches.cn: 框架：特征与空位保存了图画无法保存的关系。

branches.en: THE TRACE: the stand-in outlives the event that produced it.
branches.cn: 痕迹：替身比产生它的事件活得更久。

branches.en: THE MEANING: words and beliefs point at content the mind must supply.
branches.cn: 意义：词语与信念指向心智必须提供的内容。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two Latin adjectives and nouns that also form large English families, one for the mind and one for standing in place of something.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁形容词与名词构成，它们各自形成庞大的英语词族，一个关于心智，一个关于代替某物。

latinIntro.en: Latin mens gives mental, mentality and mention-like words; repraesentare gives represent, representation and representative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mens 衍生 mental、mentality 等词；repraesentare 衍生 represent、representation 与 representative。

items.example: Mental effort can exhaust a person faster than physical work.
items.exampleCN: 脑力消耗有时比体力劳动更快让人疲惫。

items.example: The team's mentality changed after the first win.
items.exampleCN: 首场胜利之后，团队的心态变了。

items.example: The dots represent cities on the map.
items.exampleCN: 图上的点代表城市。

items.meaning: the act or result of standing for something
items.meaningCN: 代表或描绘的动作与结果
items.example: The painting is a representation of a harbour.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画是港口的表现。

items.example: The gallery shows representational art, not pure abstraction.
items.exampleCN: 这家画廊展出具象艺术，而非纯抽象。

items.meaning: serving as a typical example or delegate
items.meaningCN: 有代表性的；作为代表的
items.example: The sample is representative of the whole shipment.
items.exampleCN: 这份样本能代表整批货物。

items.meaning: to show or give; also being here now
items.example: She presented the findings to the board.
items.exampleCN: 她向董事会呈现了研究结果。

items.example: His presence quieted the room.
items.exampleCN: 他的在场让房间安静下来。

items.example: The advertisement misrepresents the size of the room.
items.exampleCN: 这则广告歪曲了房间的大小。

derivatives.meaning: the view that the mind works through representations
derivatives.meaningCN: 认为心智通过表征运作的主张

latinEntries.meaning: to bring before the eyes, represent

definition_zh: 毁灭；歼灭；湮灭；彻底失败
definition_en: the act of destroying something completely, or total destruction itself
core_image: 归零的瞬间：一切存在被抹为无
scene: 战报送到指挥部，地图上一支箭头消失了。 The general's gamble ended in the annihilation of his entire army.
sceneCN: 这里 annihilation 是「歼灭、彻底毁灭」（第 1 个义项：完全摧毁的行为或结果）；句意为：将军的豪赌以全军覆没告终。

derivatives.zh: annihilation 的动词形式，义为「歼灭；彻底摧毁」

senses.title: Complete destruction in war
senses.definition: the total destruction of an army, city, or people in conflict
senses.definitionCN: 战争中军队、城市或族群被彻底摧毁
senses.example: The campaign ended in the annihilation of the invading force.
senses.exampleCN: 这场战役以入侵部队全军覆没告终。
senses.why: The Latin root means to reduce to nothing, and war provides the most literal reduction.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根义为「化为无」，战争提供了最字面意义上的归零。

senses.title: Utter defeat in competition
senses.definition: an overwhelming defeat in a game or contest
senses.definitionCN: 比赛或竞争中一边倒的惨败
senses.example: Fans still talk about the annihilation of the visitors in the final.
senses.exampleCN: 球迷仍在谈论决赛中客队的一败涂地。
senses.why: A defeat so total that the loser vanishes from the scoreboard borrows the language of ruin.
senses.whyCN: 败得从记分牌上「消失」的失利，借用了毁灭的语言。

senses.title: Particle-antiparticle annihilation in physics
senses.definition: the process in which a particle and its antiparticle convert into energy
senses.definitionCN: 粒子与反粒子相互转化并释放能量的物理过程
senses.example: Electron-positron annihilation produces two gamma photons.
senses.exampleCN: 正负电子湮灭产生两个伽马光子。
senses.why: Physics makes the metaphor exact: mass truly becomes nothing but energy.
senses.whyCN: 物理学使比喻成为精确事实：质量真的只化为能量，别无余留。

senses.title: Threat to the existence of a state or group
senses.definition: destruction so complete that a nation or group ceases to exist
senses.definitionCN: 使国家或族群不复存在的彻底毁灭
senses.example: Nuclear weapons raised the specter of mutual annihilation.
senses.exampleCN: 核武器带来了相互毁灭的幽灵。
senses.why: When destruction extends past armies to whole societies, the stakes become existence itself.
senses.whyCN: 当毁灭的范围越过军队扩及整个社会，赌注便成为存在本身。

senses.title: Annihilation of hope, morale, or arguments
senses.definition: the complete destruction of intangible things such as hopes or theories
senses.definitionCN: 希望、理论等无形之物的彻底破灭
senses.example: The scandal meant the annihilation of his political hopes.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻意味着他政治希望的彻底破灭。
senses.why: Anything that can be built can be reduced to nothing, including what has no atoms.
senses.whyCN: 凡能建立之物皆可归于无，包括没有原子的东西。

senses.title: Annihilation of distance or barriers
senses.definition: the complete removal of separation or hindrance
senses.definitionCN: 阻隔或障碍的彻底消除
senses.example: Air travel brought the annihilation of distance between continents.
senses.exampleCN: 航空旅行消除了大陆之间的距离阻隔。
senses.why: What no longer hinders at all may be said to have been annihilated.
senses.whyCN: 完全不再构成阻碍之物，可视为已被「消灭」。

senses.title: Self-annihilation in religion or mysticism
senses.definition: the mystical extinction of the individual self before the divine
senses.definitionCN: 在神圣面前个体自我的消解
senses.example: Sufi poetry describes annihilation of the self in divine love.
senses.exampleCN: 苏菲诗歌描述在神圣之爱中消融自我。
senses.why: Becoming nothing is here not a loss but the highest union.
senses.whyCN: 化为无在此并非损失，而是最高的合一。

senses.title: Annihilation in ecology or history
senses.definition: the wiping out of species, cultures, or ways of life
senses.definitionCN: 物种、文化或生活方式的消灭
senses.example: The annihilation of the buffalo herds changed the plains forever.
senses.exampleCN: 野牛群的灭绝永远改变了这片平原。
senses.why: Whole living worlds can be reduced to nothing by human hands.
senses.whyCN: 整个人类世界可能因人之手而化为无。

intro.en: Annihilation is the noun of annihilate, keeping the Latin recipe of making into nothing on its label.
intro.cn: annihilation 是 annihilate 的名词形式，标签上仍写着拉丁配方「化为无」。

items.en: The negative root *neh₂- (not) lies behind Latin nihil, nothing.
items.cn: 否定词根 *neh₂-（不）是拉丁语 nihil（无）的来源，属一般认为的重构。

items.en: Nihil or nihilum meant nothing; the verb annihilare meant to bring a thing to nothing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nihil 或 nihilum 意为「无」；动词 annihilare 意为「使物化为无」。

items.en: Annihilatio named the completed act of reducing to nothing.
items.cn: 后拉丁语 annihilatio 指已完成的「化为无」行为。

items.en: The noun entered English with annihilate, first in theological talk of the soul's annihilation.
items.cn: 名词与动词一同进入英语，最初用于神学中「灵魂归于无」的讨论。

items.en: War, physics, sport, and ecology have each claimed the word, all keeping its core of totality.
items.cn: 战争、物理、体育与生态学各自使用该词，而「彻底」的核心义不变。

note.en: Grouped by shared nihil roots and by words nearby in the field of total destruction.
note.cn: 按共享 nihil 词根与「彻底毁灭」义场的近义词分组。

entries.definition: the verb form, to destroy utterly
entries.definitionCN: 动词形式，义为「彻底摧毁」，与 annihilation 同根

entries.definition: the doctrine that values are groundless
entries.definitionCN: 虚无主义，共享 nihil（无）词根

entries.definition: converting figures to a yearly rate
entries.definitionCN: 年化（计算），与 annihilation 开头拼写相近但词根为 annus（年），无关

entries.definition: the erasing of all traces
entries.definitionCN: 抹除；消迹，强调痕迹全无

entries.definition: the killing of a whole group
entries.definitionCN: 灭绝，多指族群或害虫

entries.definition: complete removal, as of disease
entries.definitionCN: 根除，多用于疾病或弊病

normalIntro.en: These hooks rest on the real nihil root and the standard word family.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子基于真实的 nihil 词根及标准词族。

normal.en: annihilation = the noun of annihilate, the state of being reduced to nothing.
normal.cn: annihilation 是 annihilate 的名词，指「归于无」的状态或行为。

normal.en: Physics class keeps the word alive: electron-positron annihilation.
normal.cn: 物理课让这个词保持活力：正负电子湮灭。

normal.en: The phrase mutual annihilation names the nuclear standoff.
normal.cn: 短语 mutual annihilation 指核僵局。

normal.en: Same nihil family: nihilism, nil, nihil obstat.
normal.cn: 同属 nihil 词族：nihilism、nil、nihil obstat。

normal.en: Sports pages use annihilation for lopsided finals.
normal.cn: 体育版用 annihilation 描述悬殊的决赛。

abstract.en: Picture a galaxy of sand grains blown flat, the desert smooth again.
abstract.cn: 想象一把细沙被吹平，沙漠恢复平整。

abstract.en: See two photons leave where a particle used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象粒子消失之处射出两枚光子。

abstract.en: Feel a name being crossed off every list it ever appeared on.
abstract.cn: 感受一个名字从所有名单上被划去。

examples.en: The city never recovered from the annihilation of 1945.
examples.cn: 这座城市从未从 1945 年的毁灭中恢复。

examples.en: Scientists observed annihilation between the particle beams.
examples.cn: 科学家观测到粒子束之间的湮灭。

examples.en: The final was an annihilation, six goals to none.
examples.cn: 那场决赛是一场碾压，六比零。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺乃一灭神」——俺乃灭世之神，专司毁灭，正是 annihilation（毁灭、湮灭）。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ nihil（无，源自一般认为的印欧否定词根 *neh₂-「不」）+ -atio（名词后缀）→ annihilatio「化为无（之行为）」→ 英语 annihilation（15 世纪，随 annihilate 一同借入）。

sensesIntro.en: From the act of reducing to nothing, the noun covers battlefields, physics labs, scoreboards, and the extinction of species and selves.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「化为无」的行为出发，名词覆盖战场、物理实验室、记分牌，以及物种与自我的消亡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the completed return to zero
core.cn: 核心意象：彻底归零的完成态

branches.en: destruction of armies and states
branches.cn: 军队与国家层面的毁灭

branches.en: utter defeat, of teams or hopes
branches.cn: 队伍或希望的一败涂地

branches.en: matter becoming pure energy
branches.cn: 物质化为纯粹能量

branches.en: barriers made as if never there
branches.cn: 障碍仿佛从未存在

branches.en: selves and species passing into nothing
branches.cn: 自我与物种的消亡

intro.en: The word carries its Latin parts openly: prefix, root, and noun suffix, with nothing hidden.
intro.cn: 这个词的拉丁部件一目了然：前缀、词根、名词后缀，毫无隐藏。

latinIntro.en: Latin nihil anchors the family, and the suffix -io turned the verb into a completed noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nihil 是词族的锚点，后缀 -io 将动词变为完成态名词。

items.example: Annihilate and advance both open with this prefix.
items.exampleCN: annihilate 与 advance 都以该前缀开头。

items.example: Nihil is the Latin word for zero.
items.exampleCN: nihil 是拉丁语的「零、无」。

items.example: Creation and fixation share this ending.
items.exampleCN: creation 与 fixation 共用此词尾。

items.example: Annihilative destruction is destruction that annihilates.
items.exampleCN: annihilative destruction 即具有毁灭性的破坏。

items.example: The score was three nil.
items.exampleCN: 比分是三比零。

items.example: Nihilism denies objective meaning.
items.exampleCN: 虚无主义否认客观意义。

items.example: The bombing meant the obliteration of the old quarter.
items.exampleCN: 轰炸意味着旧城区被彻底抹除。

items.example: The contract fell into the void.
items.exampleCN: 合同归于无效。

definition_zh: 触发；引发；激起；扳机；触发器；诱因
definition_en: to cause something to start suddenly, and the small lever or device that sets a mechanism going
core_image: 靶场上，一根手指搭在扳机上，只要一个很小的动作，整支枪的力量就会释放
scene: 靶场上，一根手指搭在扳机上，只要一个很小的动作，整支枪的力量就会释放。 A single spark was enough to trigger the alarm.
sceneCN: 这里指引发、触发（第 1 个义项：使某事突然开始）；句意为一个火花就足以触发警报。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词的现在分词转成的名词或形容词，义为「触发；引发性的」
由该动词的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「被触发的；受激的」
由该名词与表示「热衷」的形容词合成为复合形容词，义为「动辄开枪的；莽撞行事的」
由该动词加表示可能性的形容词尾构成，义为「可被触发的」

senses.title: Cause an event to begin suddenly
senses.definition: to set off an event or a chain of events that would not have started by itself
senses.definitionCN: 使一个本不会自行开始的事件或连锁事件开始
senses.example: A small error can trigger a chain of failures.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小错误就可能引发一连串故障。
senses.why: The word began as the small lever that releases a gun, and the idea of a little act releasing a large force is the heart of every sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指释放枪械力量的小杠杆，而「一个小动作释放巨大力量」正是每个义项的核心。

senses.title: Provoke a strong feeling
senses.definition: to cause anger, fear or excitement in a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 引起个人或群体的愤怒、恐惧或激动
senses.example: The news triggered an angry response from the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 那条消息激起人群的愤怒回应。
senses.why: A feeling that was quiet suddenly fires, and the word pictures it as a mechanism released by a small event.
senses.whyCN: 原本安静的情绪突然开火，这个词把它画成被小事释放的机械。

senses.title: Set a device into operation
senses.definition: to make a sensor, circuit or machine begin working, often automatically
senses.definitionCN: 使传感器、电路或机器开始工作，常为自动进行
senses.example: The sensor triggers the lamp when someone walks past.
senses.exampleCN: 有人走过时，传感器就会触发那盏灯。
senses.why: This is the most literal modern sense: a small signal releases a larger action.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的现代义：一个小信号释放一个更大的动作。

senses.title: Induce an illness or symptom
senses.definition: in medicine, to cause a disease, attack or symptom to begin
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指引起疾病、发作或症状开始
senses.example: The virus can trigger a high fever.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病毒能引发高烧。
senses.why: A body already carrying a condition may need only one small provocation, and the word names that provocation.
senses.whyCN: 身体本就带着病因，也许只差一个很小的刺激，而这个词命名的正是那个刺激。

senses.title: The lever on a firearm
senses.definition: the small lever a finger pulls to fire a gun
senses.definitionCN: 手指扣动以使枪械击发的小杠杆
senses.example: He kept his finger off the trigger until the order came.
senses.exampleCN: 在命令下达之前，他的手指一直没有放在扳机上。
senses.why: This is the sense from which every other sense borrows its shape: the smallest part controls the largest release.
senses.whyCN: 这是其他所有义项借取形状的源头义：最小的部件控制最大的释放。

senses.title: An electronic pulse that starts an action
senses.titleCN: 电子触发器或触发脉冲
senses.definition: a signal in a circuit that tells another part to begin its cycle
senses.definitionCN: 电路中通知另一部件开始运行周期的信号
senses.example: The circuit sends a trigger to the camera every two seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 电路每隔两秒向相机发送一个触发信号。
senses.why: Electronics kept the gun image and made the lever invisible: a pulse instead of a finger.
senses.whyCN: 电子学保留了枪的意象，却把杠杆变得看不见：用脉冲代替手指。

senses.title: The cause or occasion of an event
senses.definition: the event or remark that was the immediate occasion for something larger
senses.definitionCN: 成为更大事件的直接起因的事件或言论
senses.example: The report was the trigger for a wider debate.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告成了更广泛争论的诱因。
senses.why: In this noun sense the lever becomes the occasion itself, the point at which the mechanism was released.
senses.whyCN: 在这个名词义项里，杠杆变成了事件本身，即机械被释放的那一刻。

senses.title: Bring a memory back
senses.definition: to cause a scene, smell or sound to bring an old memory into the mind
senses.definitionCN: 使景象、气味或声音把旧日记忆带回心中
senses.example: The smell of bread triggered a memory of his grandmother's kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 面包的气味唤起了他对祖母厨房的记忆。
senses.why: A memory sits loaded like a spring, and one small sensory cue can release it whole.
senses.whyCN: 记忆像上了弦的弹簧，一个小小的感官线索就能把它整个释放。

senses.title: Set off a biological response
senses.definition: to start an allergic, immune or inflammatory reaction in a living body
senses.definitionCN: 在生物体内引起过敏、免疫或炎症反应
senses.example: The pollen may trigger an allergic reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 花粉可能引发过敏反应。
senses.why: The body is the machine here, and the allergen is the finger on the lever.
senses.whyCN: 这里的机器是身体，而过敏原就是搭在杠杆上的那根手指。

intro.en: Trigger is a Dutch loan. It comes from trekker, a puller, from trekken, to pull, and it entered English first as a name for the lever of a firearm.
intro.cn: 这个词借自荷兰语，来自 trekker「拉者」，而 trekker 出自 trekken「拉」；它进入英语时最先指枪械上的杠杆。

items.en: Trekken meant to pull or draw, and it is also the source of the English word trek, a long journey drawn out by oxen.
items.cn: trekken 意为拉、拖，它也是英语 trek「长途跋涉」的来源，那正是牛车拉出来的路。

items.en: The noun meant one that pulls, and it could name a person, a rope or a part of a machine.
items.cn: 这个名词意为「拉的东西」，可以指人、指绳，也可以指机器部件。

items.en: The earliest English form was tricker, recorded in the sixteenth century for the lever of a gun; the spelling was not yet fixed.
items.cn: 最早的英语形式是 tricker，十六世纪时用来指枪的杠杆；当时拼写尚未固定。

items.en: The modern spelling settled in the seventeenth century, still tied to firearms before it moved to any small releasing part.
items.cn: 现代拼写在十七世纪固定下来，仍先与枪械绑定，之后才转向任何小的释放部件。

items.en: Machines and then circuits borrowed the word for any small part that starts a larger motion.
items.cn: 机器、随后是电路，都借这个词来指任何启动更大运动的细小部件。

items.en: Psychology and medicine extended it to memories, emotions and symptoms, where a small cue releases a large response.
items.cn: 心理学与医学把它扩展到记忆、情绪与症状，那里一个小小的线索就释放出很大的反应。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like trigger; the second group names neighbouring ways of starting something.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 trigger 相近；第二组是与「引发、启动」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The act of setting something off, or the quality of doing so.
entries.definitionCN: 指触发的行为，或指具有引发作用的性质。

entries.definition: Set off or activated by something else.
entries.definitionCN: 指被某物触发或激活的。

entries.definition: Too ready to shoot or to act rashly.
entries.definitionCN: 指动辄开枪或鲁莽行事的。

entries.definition: A large striped cat; it looks close in spelling but has no shared history.
entries.definitionCN: 指一种大型条纹猫科动物；拼写相近，但没有共同来源。

entries.definition: To flow in a thin stream; it sounds close but comes from a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指细细地流；读音相近，但来自另一个动词。

entries.definition: To make something happen; neutral about size and speed, and the broadest word here.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某事发生；不涉及大小与速度，是这里最宽泛的词。

entries.definition: To stir a feeling or a reaction, often deliberately; it stresses the irritation.
entries.definitionCN: 指激起情绪或反应，常含故意；强调被激起的恼怒。

entries.definition: To start something large from a very small beginning, with the image of a spark and dry grass.
entries.definitionCN: 指由极小的开端引发大事，意象是火星与干草。

entries.definition: To start a device, alarm or chain of events; plainer and more physical than trigger.
entries.definitionCN: 指启动装置、警报或一连串事件；比本词更朴素、更物理。

entries.definition: To begin something formally or deliberately, without the idea of a small lever.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式或有意地开始某事，不含「小杠杆」的意思。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the pulling root, the gun lever and the small-cause-large-effect pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想利用「拉」的词根、枪的杠杆，以及「小原因、大效果」的模式。

normal.en: The Dutch root means pull, so the trigger is the part you pull to release everything else.
normal.cn: 荷兰语词根意为拉，所以扳机就是你拉一下、其余一切随之释放的那个部件。

normal.en: A finger moves a few millimetres and the whole gun answers; that is the shape of the word.
normal.cn: 手指移动几毫米，整支枪都作出回应；这就是这个词的形状。

normal.en: A smoke detector is a trigger made electronic: a little smoke, a loud alarm.
normal.cn: 烟雾报警器就是电子化的扳机：一点烟，一阵大响。

normal.en: A smell that brings back a kitchen is the same mechanism working on memory.
normal.cn: 让厨房重现的气味，是同一套机械在记忆上工作。

normal.en: The stock phrase pull the trigger keeps the original object visible inside the modern verb.
normal.cn: 固定说法「扣动扳机」让原本的物件在现代动词里仍然可见。

abstract.en: A trigger is defined by the ratio between the small input and the large release.
abstract.cn: 扳机的本质，在于小输入与大释放之间的比例。

abstract.en: The same event can be a trigger for one person and a trifle for another, because the mechanism is inside.
abstract.cn: 同一件事对一个人是扳机，对另一个人却无关紧要，因为机械装在内部。

abstract.en: Naming a trigger is already a way of taking some power back from it.
abstract.cn: 说出一个触发点，本身已经是从它手里收回一部分权力。

examples.en: The ruling triggered protests across the country.
examples.cn: 那项裁决引发了全国范围的抗议。

examples.en: A loud noise can trigger a panic attack.
examples.cn: 巨大的声响可能引发惊恐发作。

examples.en: The alarm was triggered by a broken wire.
examples.cn: 警报是被一根断线触发的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「吹格」——手指一「吹」，扳机一「格」响，整支枪就响了：扳机、触发

root: 荷兰语 trekken「拉」→ trekker「拉者、拉动的部件」→ 英语早期形式 tricker（十六世纪指枪的杠杆）→ trigger「扳机」→ 动词「触发、引发」；核心是「一个很小的拉动释放很大的力量」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all follow one pattern, a small act releasing a large response: events, feelings, devices, illness, the gun lever itself, circuits, occasions, memories and allergic reactions.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都遵循同一个模式——小动作释放大反应：事件、情绪、装置、疾病、枪的杠杆本身、电路、诱因、记忆与过敏反应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one finger on a small lever, and the whole weapon answers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指搭在小杠杆上，整件武器随之响应。

branches.en: THE RELEASE BRANCH: one error starts a chain, and one allergen starts a reaction.
branches.cn: 释放分支：一个错误引发连锁，一个过敏原引发反应。

branches.en: THE INNER BRANCH: a piece of news fires anger, and a smell fires a memory.
branches.cn: 内部分支：一条消息点燃愤怒，一种气味点燃记忆。

branches.en: THE MACHINE BRANCH: a sensor starts a lamp, and a pulse starts a camera.
branches.cn: 机械分支：传感器启动灯，脉冲启动相机。

branches.en: THE ILLNESS BRANCH: a virus provokes a fever in a body already carrying it.
branches.cn: 疾病分支：病毒在本已带病的身体里诱发高烧。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN BRANCH: the gun lever itself, and the occasion that releases a debate.
branches.cn: 源头分支：枪的杠杆本身，以及释放一场争论的诱因。

intro.en: Trigger is not a Latin word at all: it is a Dutch loan whose parts are a verb of pulling and an agent ending.
intro.cn: 这个词根本不是拉丁词，而是一个荷兰语借词，其部件是一个表示「拉」的动词和一个施动词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin etymon behind this word. Its family is Germanic, and the Latin entries are therefore left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁语词源，它属于日耳曼语族，因此拉丁语条目留空。

items.example: The pulling action is the physical core of the word.
items.exampleCN: 「拉」这个动作是这个词的物理核心。

items.example: It turns the verb into a noun for the thing that pulls.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成指「拉动之物」的名词。

items.example: The Dutch noun named the part that sets a mechanism going.
items.exampleCN: 这个荷兰语名词命名启动机械的那个部件。

items.example: English took the Dutch noun and narrowed it to the gun part.
items.exampleCN: 英语借入这个荷兰语名词，并把意义收窄到枪的部件。

items.structure: English conversion from noun to verb
items.example: English turned the part into an action without adding an ending.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个部件直接变成动作，没有加任何词尾。

items.example: The compound keeps the gun sense alive in ordinary speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词让枪的义项在日常说法里继续存活。

items.example: It forms triggered, the past and participle of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 triggered，即该动词的过去式与过去分词。

items.meaning: ongoing action, or the act itself
items.meaningCN: 正在进行的动作，或行为本身
items.example: It forms triggering, both participle and verbal noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 triggering，既是分词也是动名词。
