definition_zh: 吹嘘；自夸；夸口说
definition_en: to talk too proudly about oneself or one's achievements
core_image: 一个人挺着胸脯拍自己的胸口，唾沫横飞地向四周宣布自己的丰功伟绩
scene: 酒馆里有人又开始高谈阔论自己的棋艺。 He would brag about beating the town champion, though no one had seen the game.
sceneCN: 这里 brag 是「自夸」（第 1 个义项：言语上夸耀自己）；句意是他总爱吹嘘击败过镇上冠军，尽管没人见过那盘棋。

pos.zh: 首屈一指的（brag 一词在古义中表「卓越的」）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「吹嘘行为」
由动词加表人后缀构成，义为「吹牛者」
由同根加表人后缀构成，义为「自夸的人」
由同根加拟意大利后缀构成，义为「大话；自夸」
由表人名词加副词后缀构成，义为「吹牛地」

senses.title: To talk proudly about oneself
senses.definition: to speak with too much pride about what one has done or owns
senses.definitionCN: 以过度的骄傲谈论自己的所作所为或所有之物
senses.example: He bragged about his new car for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 他连续几个星期吹嘘自己的新车。
senses.why: The core image is the swollen voice: pride forcing itself out of the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是膨胀的声音：骄傲从嘴里挤出来。

senses.title: To boast before proving
senses.definition: to claim victory or ability in advance of the result
senses.definitionCN: 在结果出来之前宣称必胜或自称有能
senses.example: They bragged they would finish the job by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们夸口周五之前就能完工。
senses.why: Swollen talk runs ahead of swollen deeds, so claiming comes before doing.
senses.whyCN: 嘴上的膨胀跑在行动前面，宣称便先于做成。

senses.title: To speak boastfully on someone's behalf
senses.definition: to praise another, often one's own family, in a boastful way
senses.definitionCN: 以夸口的口吻称赞他人，常指家人
senses.example: Grandmother brags of her grandchildren endlessly.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母没完没了地夸自己的孙辈。
senses.why: One's own pride extends naturally to what belongs to one's own circle.
senses.whyCN: 对自身的骄傲自然延伸到自己圈内的人和物。

senses.title: A boastful statement
senses.definition: an instance of boasting; a thing said with too much pride
senses.definitionCN: 一次吹嘘；说得过头的话
senses.example: That was no brag; he really did it.
senses.exampleCN: 那不是大话；他真的做到了。
senses.why: The act names its product, as talk leaves words behind.
senses.whyCN: 行为命名其产物，正如言谈留下话语。

senses.title: A proud claim worth making
senses.definition: something to be proud of, as in bragging rights
senses.definitionCN: 足以自豪之事，如 bragging rights（夸耀的资本）
senses.example: Winning the league gave them bragging rights for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 赢得联赛让他们有一年的夸耀资本。
senses.why: Since boasting implies grounds, the grounds themselves take the word's name.
senses.whyCN: 吹嘘必有凭据，凭据便借用了这个词的名字。

senses.title: First-rate, of the best kind
senses.definition: outstanding or first-rate, in older or dialect use
senses.definitionCN: 卓越的、一流的，见于旧用法或方言
senses.example: In old use, a brag horse meant the finest horse.
senses.exampleCN: 旧用法中 brag horse 指最好的马。
senses.why: Boastful excess shades into superlative praise of the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 夸口的过分反转为对事物本身的最高级称赞。

senses.title: A card game of bluffing
senses.definition: a British card game in which bluffing is central, ancestor of poker
senses.definitionCN: 一种以虚张声势为核心的英国纸牌游戏，扑克的祖先
senses.example: The sailors passed the night playing brag.
senses.exampleCN: 水手们打了一夜的吹牛纸牌。
senses.why: The game is named for its chief move: talking up a weak hand.
senses.whyCN: 该游戏因其核心动作得名：把弱牌吹成强牌。

senses.title: A loud or startling sound or thing
senses.definition: in older use, a thunderous noise or a striking thing
senses.definitionCN: 旧义指雷鸣般的响声或令人吃惊的事物
senses.example: Early texts used brag for a burst of thunder.
senses.exampleCN: 早期文本用 brag 指一声炸雷。
senses.why: The swollen voice began as swollen sound before it became swollen words.
senses.whyCN: 膨胀之声先于膨胀之词，词义由响声起家。

intro.en: Brag arose in Middle English, probably imitative of loud talk, with possible Norse connections; its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: brag 产生于中古英语，一般认为是对大声说话的拟声，或与诺斯语有关；更深的来源不确定。

items.en: Old Norse braka meant to creak or crack; a link is generally suggested but not proven.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 braka 意为吱嘎作响、爆裂；一般认为有关联但未获证实。

items.en: Brag first meant to make a loud noise, then to talk loudly and proudly.
items.cn: 十四世纪 brag 先指发出巨响，后指大声而骄傲地说话。

items.en: The adjective brag meant spirited or first-rate, as in brag lines of verse.
items.cn: 形容词 brag 意为神气的、一流的，见于诗行描写。

items.en: The noun and the card game name appear; Shakespeare uses brag both as noun and adjective.
items.cn: 十六世纪出现名词用法及纸牌戏名；莎翁笔下 brag 兼作名词与形容词。

items.en: Derivatives braggart, braggadocio (coined in Spenser), and bragging rights spread.
items.cn: 派生词 braggart、braggadocio（斯宾塞所创）与 bragging rights 流行开来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the verb, noun, and the phrase bragging rights; the adjective is archaic.
items.cn: 现代英语保留动词、名词与 bragging rights 短语；形容词义已属古旧。

note.en: Brag heads a noisy family of boast words; its sound twins bray and brace are unrelated.
note.cn: brag 是一片吹嘘之词的源头；音近的 bray、brace 与之无关。

entries.definition: a person who brags constantly
entries.definitionCN: 吹牛者；同根表人名词

entries.definition: empty, swaggering boastfulness
entries.definitionCN: 空洞的大话；同根拟意大利式派生词

entries.definition: one who brags
entries.definitionCN: 吹嘘者；动词加 -er

entries.definition: a donkey's loud cry
entries.definitionCN: 驴叫；拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a pair, or to steady
entries.definitionCN: 一对；支撑；拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to talk with pride, often more neutral than brag
entries.definitionCN: 夸耀；语气常较 brag 中性

entries.definition: to boast gleefully, especially after winning
entries.definitionCN: 欢然自得地夸口；尤指胜后得意

entries.definition: to take spiteful pleasure in success
entries.definitionCN: 幸灾乐祸地自得；侧重内心而非言语

entries.definition: to walk or behave with arrogant pride
entries.definitionCN: 昂首阔步；跋扈自大；以举止代替言语

entries.definition: to boast, in literary use
entries.definitionCN: 夸耀（书面语）

normalIntro.en: The family is rich: brag, braggart, bragging rights all grow from one short word.
normalIntro.cn: 词族丰富：brag、braggart、bragging rights 都由这个短词长出。

normal.en: brag takes the pattern brag about something.
normal.cn: brag 常用搭配为 brag about something。

normal.en: -art in braggart marks the habitual doer.
normal.cn: braggart 中的 -art 标示惯常为之者。

normal.en: braggadocio was coined by the poet Spenser for a boastful character.
normal.cn: braggadocio 由诗人斯宾塞为其笔下自负角色所创。

normal.en: bragging rights means the earned privilege to boast.
normal.cn: bragging rights 指赢来的夸耀资格。

normal.en: the card game brag is the ancestor of poker.
normal.cn: 纸牌戏 brag 是扑克的前身。

abstract.en: Picture a chest pushed out and a finger drumming on it.
abstract.cn: 想象挺起的胸膛和敲在胸上的手指。

abstract.en: Words ahead of deeds: the cart of talk before the horse of work.
abstract.cn: 言先于行：话这辆车跑在了活这匹马前面。

abstract.en: A balloon of sound: loud at first, empty at the pin.
abstract.cn: 声音的气球：起时轰响，针一刺便瘪。

examples.en: He loves to brag about how little he studied and still passed.
examples.cn: 他爱吹嘘自己几乎没复习还考过了。

examples.en: All that bragging collapsed when the project missed its deadline.
examples.cn: 项目错过期限，所有的大话随之破产。

examples.en: The old sailors bragged of storms no one else had survived.
examples.cn: 老水手们夸口经历过无人幸免的风暴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不赖格」——满嘴「不赖不赖我最不赖」：连声自夸「不赖」的格调，就是 brag。

root: 中古英语 brag，一般认为系拟声词（摹写大而响的声音），或与古诺斯语 braka（爆裂作响）有关；更早来源不确定，非拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: From loud sound to proud talk, then to the statement, the grounds, the game of bluffs, and the old sense of first-rate.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项由响声到夸口之言，再到大话本身、夸耀资本、纸牌戏，及旧义的「上等」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a swollen voice pushing pride out of the mouth
core.cn: 核心意象：膨胀的声音把骄傲挤出嘴巴

branches.en: the mouth at work: boasting of self and of one's own
branches.cn: 嘴上的功夫：夸自己、夸自己人

branches.en: claims before deeds: victory declared early
branches.cn: 言先于行：提前宣告胜利

branches.en: what talk leaves behind: the boast and its grounds
branches.cn: 言谈的产物：大话及其资本

branches.en: talk as play: the bluffing card game
branches.cn: 言语成戏：以虚张声势为核的纸牌

branches.en: loud becomes fine: thunder and the first-rate
branches.cn: 响即是好：雷声与「上等」旧义

intro.en: Brag is a bare root with productive English suffixes hung on it.
intro.cn: brag 是裸词根，其上挂着能产的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognates exist; the family is Germanic and imitative.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁同源词；该词族属日耳曼语且为拟声性质。

items.meaning: to make a loud noise; to boast
items.example: the root of the whole family
items.exampleCN: 整个词族的根基

items.example: a bragger talks big
items.exampleCN: bragger 即吹牛之人

items.example: braggart mocks the constant boaster
items.exampleCN: braggart 讽刺惯于吹嘘者

items.example: braggadocio imitates Italian names
items.exampleCN: braggadocio 模仿意大利人名

items.example: bragging is the act itself
items.exampleCN: bragging 指吹嘘行为

items.example: bray differs from brag by one letter
items.exampleCN: bray 与 brag 仅差一字母

items.example: boast is the milder twin
items.exampleCN: boast 是语气较温和的近义词

items.example: crow after winning, brag before
items.exampleCN: 胜后曰 crow，胜前曰 brag

definition_zh: 冲动性；易冲动的倾向；不加思索就行动的特质
definition_en: the tendency to act suddenly on urges without stopping to think
core_image: 脚下的刹车片磨得很薄，车还是滑出去半米才停住
scene: 停车场的出口，一位司机差点撞上柱子， The report blamed impulsiveness rather than poor brakes for the crash.
sceneCN: 这里 impulsiveness 指「不加思索就行动的倾向」（第 1 个义项：易凭冲动行动的倾向）；句意为报告把这次碰撞归因于冲动，而不是刹车不良。图中可辨识物件：停车场、柱子、刹车痕、事故报告。

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多次冲动表现）
名词（冲动性，心理学用语）

senses.title: The tendency to act on a sudden urge
senses.titleCN: 凭一时冲动行事的倾向
senses.definition: the tendency to act suddenly on a strong urge rather than after thought
senses.definitionCN: 倾向于凭强烈欲望突然行动，而不是先思考
senses.example: Her impulsiveness got her into debt.
senses.exampleCN: 她的冲动让她背上了债。
senses.why: The ending -ness turns the adjective into a standing tendency, so the word names a pattern rather than one act.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ness 把形容词变成一种持续存在的倾向，因此这个词命名的是模式，而不是一次行为。

senses.title: The quality of action done without a pause
senses.definition: the quality of an action that happens before reflection has time to occur
senses.definitionCN: 行为在反思还来不及发生之前就已经做出的性质
senses.example: The impulsiveness of the decision surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定之冲动让所有人都吃惊。
senses.why: A quality can belong to an act as well as to a person, and here it names the missing pause.
senses.whyCN: 一种性质既可以属于人，也可以属于行为，这里它命名的是那个缺席的停顿。

senses.title: A trait measured in psychology
senses.titleCN: 心理学中可测量的特质
senses.definition: in psychology, a measurable trait of responding to urges with little delay
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中，对欲望几乎不延迟就作出反应的可测量特质
senses.example: The study scored impulsiveness on a ten-point scale.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究用十分制给冲动性打分。
senses.why: Once a tendency can be scored, it becomes a variable rather than a moral failing.
senses.whyCN: 一种倾向一旦可以被评分，就成了变量，而不是道德缺陷。

senses.title: A clinical sign of weak regulation
senses.titleCN: 调节能力薄弱的临床征象
senses.definition: in clinical use, a sign that a person has difficulty holding back urges
senses.definitionCN: 在临床上，指一个人难以克制欲望的征象
senses.example: The assessment noted impulsiveness alongside poor sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 评估在记录冲动性的同时，也记录了睡眠不佳。
senses.why: Medicine reads the trait as a symptom, so the same word becomes part of a diagnosis.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这种特质读成症状，同一个词于是成了诊断的一部分。

senses.title: A tendency toward unplanned buying
senses.titleCN: 未经计划就消费的倾向
senses.definition: in commerce, the tendency to buy on a sudden wish rather than a plan
senses.definitionCN: 在商业上，指凭突然的欲望而非计划购物的倾向
senses.example: Discounts are designed to exploit impulsiveness.
senses.exampleCN: 折扣就是为了利用冲动而设计的。
senses.why: Commerce gives the trait a market value: the pause that is missing is the pause before payment.
senses.whyCN: 商业给这种特质标上了市场价值：所缺的那个停顿，正是付款之前的停顿。

senses.title: The rashness often ascribed to youth
senses.titleCN: 常被归给年轻人的莽撞
senses.definition: the rashness that is often attributed to young people and inexperience
senses.definitionCN: 常被归因于年轻与缺乏经验的莽撞
senses.example: They forgave his youthful impulsiveness.
senses.exampleCN: 他们原谅了他年轻人的冲动。
senses.why: Age is used as an excuse for the trait, so the word acquires a social label.
senses.whyCN: 年龄被拿来为这种特质开脱，于是这个词又获得了一个社会标签。

senses.title: Spontaneity visible in a style
senses.titleCN: 风格中可见的自发劲头
senses.definition: the quality of a style that looks spontaneous and unplanned
senses.definitionCN: 某种风格显得自发、未经安排的性质
senses.example: The impulsiveness of the brushwork gives the painting life.
senses.exampleCN: 笔触的冲动感让这幅画有了生气。
senses.why: In art the missing pause becomes a virtue, because freshness is valued over finish.
senses.whyCN: 在艺术里，缺席的停顿反而成了优点，因为新鲜感比精修更受看重。

senses.title: The push outrunning the scale
senses.definition: the abstract condition in which a drive acts before any weighing can take place
senses.definitionCN: 驱动力在任何权衡发生之前就已行动起来的抽象状态
senses.example: At bottom, impulsiveness is a race the scale always loses.
senses.exampleCN: 说到底，冲动性是一场天平总是输掉的赛跑。
senses.why: The whole family rests on a contrast between a push and a balance, and this sense names the race itself.
senses.whyCN: 整个词族都建立在「推力」与「天平」的对照上，这个义项命名的正是那场赛跑。

intro.en: Impulsiveness is impulsive plus the native noun ending -ness, recorded in English usage from the eighteenth century onward. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: impulsiveness 由 impulsive 加本族语名词词尾 -ness 构成，英语用法自十八世纪起有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: The base noun impulsus named a push or shock, from impellere, to drive into.
items.cn: 基础名词 impulsus 指推击或冲击，来自表示「推入」的 impellere。

items.en: The adjective impulsive entered English in the seventeenth century, first for physical pushes and then for sudden human acts.
items.cn: 形容词 impulsive 在十七世纪进入英语，先指物理上的推动，后指人的突然行为。

items.en: The ending -ness turns an adjective into a noun of quality, and it has been productive in English since Old English.
items.cn: 词尾 -ness 把形容词变成表示性质的名词，自上古英语以来一直是能产后缀。

items.en: The noun became common in moral writing and later in psychology, where it names a measurable trait.
items.cn: 这个名词先在道德论述中常见，后来进入心理学，用来命名一种可测量的特质。

items.en: Source uncertain: reference works give different first dates for the noun, and the exact route from moral comment to clinical use is not documented in one line.
items.cn: 来源不确定：各家参考资料给这个名词的首见年代不一；从道德评语走向临床用语的具体路径，也没有单一文献记录。

note.en: The first group is built on the same impulse stock but differs in form or prefix; the second holds nouns of haste and self-drive.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个 impulse 词干上，只是形态或前缀不同；第二组是表示仓促与自发的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a person or act moved by a sudden push; impulsiveness is the noun for that quality.
entries.definitionCN: 描述被突然推力带动的人或行为的形容词；impulsiveness 是表示该性质的名词。

entries.definition: The push itself; impulsiveness names the standing tendency to follow such pushes.
entries.definitionCN: 推力本身；impulsiveness 命名跟随这种推力的持续倾向。

entries.definition: The clinical and psychological term for the trait; it is close to impulsiveness but belongs to professional registers.
entries.definitionCN: 指该特质的临床与心理学术语；与 impulsiveness 相近，但属于专业语域。

entries.definition: The quality of being driven by a compulsion that feels unavoidable; it is stronger than a passing urge.
entries.definitionCN: 被一种似乎无法避免的强迫驱使的性质；比一时的欲望更强。

entries.definition: The quality of acting too quickly and without seeing the risk; it is more clearly critical than impulsiveness.
entries.definitionCN: 行动过快且没看到风险的性质；比 impulsiveness 更明显带批评意味。

entries.definition: The quality of doing something too quickly; it need not involve an inner urge at all.
entries.definitionCN: 做事过快的性质；它完全可以不涉及内在欲望。

entries.definition: The quality of arising freely from oneself; it is usually praised, while impulsiveness is often warned against.
entries.definitionCN: 自由地出于自身的性质；它通常受称赞，而 impulsiveness 常被警告。

entries.definition: Rushed forcefulness of movement or feeling; it comes from a different root and adds violence that impulsiveness need not have.
entries.definitionCN: 动作或情绪上的猛烈冲劲；它来自不同词根，多了 impulsiveness 未必有的猛烈。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real adjective base, the native noun ending, the real family and the phrases the noun keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的形容词基础、本族语名词词尾、真实的同族词，以及这个名词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: impulsive plus -ness: the ending turns a way of acting into a standing trait.
normal.cn: impulsive 加 -ness：这个词尾把一种行事方式变成一种持续的特质。

normal.en: The family runs impulse, impulsive, impulsively, impulsiveness and impulsivity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 impulse（冲动）、impulsive（冲动的）、impulsively（冲动地）、impulsiveness（冲动性）、impulsivity（冲动性，心理学用语）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: sheer impulsiveness, a trait of impulsiveness, impulsiveness score.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：纯粹的冲动、冲动性的特质、冲动性得分。

normal.en: Psychology prefers the shorter technical doublet impulsivity, while everyday speech uses impulsiveness.
normal.cn: 心理学更爱用较短的技术对偶词 impulsivity，日常口语则用 impulsiveness。

normal.en: The word names the missing pause, so any phrase about stopping to think is a fair test of its meaning.
normal.cn: 这个词命名的是那个缺席的停顿，因此任何关于「停下来想一想」的说法都能检验它的含义。

abstract.en: Picture worn brake pads that let the car slide past the line.
abstract.cn: 想象磨薄的刹车片，让车滑过了停止线。

abstract.en: Picture a hand already in the jar before the question is asked.
abstract.cn: 想象问题还没问出口，手已经伸进罐子里。

abstract.en: Picture a runner who starts on the gun and never checks the lane.
abstract.cn: 想象一名听见枪响就冲出去、从不看道的跑者。

examples.en: His impulsiveness made the apology necessary.
examples.cn: 他的冲动让那句道歉成了必要。

examples.en: The questionnaire measures impulsiveness in adolescents.
examples.cn: 这份问卷测量青少年的冲动性。

examples.en: Age had not cured her impulsiveness.
examples.cn: 年纪并没有治好她的冲动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一木跑媳妇，拿死」——冲出去就收不住的那股劲 → impulsiveness 冲动性

root: 由 impulsive 加本族语名词词尾 -ness 构成；impulsive 出自 impulse，后者来自拉丁 impulsus，再追溯到 impellere = in-「进入」+ pellere「推、驱动」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one missing pause: a tendency, a quality of acts, a measured trait, a clinical sign, a shopping habit, the rashness of youth, a praised spontaneity and finally a race the balance always loses.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个缺席的停顿展开：一种倾向、行为的一种性质、被测量的特质、临床征象、购物习惯、年轻人的莽撞、被称赞的自发，最后是一场天平总是输掉的赛跑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: brake pads worn thin, and the car still slides half a metre past the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：刹车片磨得很薄，车还是滑出去半米才停住。

branches.en: URGE AND ACT: a push arrives and the deed follows before reflection.
branches.cn: 欲望与行为：推力一到，行为就在反思之前跟着发生。

branches.en: TRAIT AND SIGN: the same tendency becomes a score and then a symptom.
branches.cn: 特质与征象：同一种倾向先变成分数，再变成症状。

branches.en: MARKET AND YOUTH: the missing pause is sold to shoppers and excused in the young.
branches.cn: 市场与年轻：缺席的停顿被卖给消费者，也被拿来为年轻人开脱。

branches.en: ART: in a style the missing pause can turn into freshness.
branches.cn: 艺术：在风格里，缺席的停顿可以变成新鲜感。

branches.en: THE RACE: drive and deliberation compete, and drive starts first.
branches.cn: 赛跑：驱力与权衡在比，而驱力先起跑。

intro.en: Impulsiveness is a chain of three pieces: a Latin verb of driving, an adjective ending and a native noun ending.
intro.cn: impulsiveness 是三段接起来的：表示驱动的拉丁动词、形容词词尾，以及本族语名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin pellere gives impulse and impel, the ending -ive turns impulse into a tendency, and the native -ness turns that tendency into a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pellere 衍生 impulse 与 impel，词尾 -ive 把 impulse 变成倾向，本族语词尾 -ness 再把这种倾向变成名词。

items.example: Its stem survives in propel and repel.
items.exampleCN: 它的词干留在 propel（推进）与 repel（击退）里。

items.example: The impulse came without warning.
items.exampleCN: 这股冲动来得毫无预兆。

items.meaning: tending to; having the nature of
items.example: The same ending builds compulsive and repulsive.
items.exampleCN: 同一词尾也构成 compulsive（强迫性的）与 repulsive（令人反感的）。

items.example: He is impulsive by nature.
items.exampleCN: 他天生冲动。

items.example: The same ending builds rashness and boldness.
items.exampleCN: 同一词尾也构成 rashness（鲁莽）与 boldness（大胆）。

items.meaning: the tendency to act on urges
items.example: Impulsiveness can be measured.
items.exampleCN: 冲动性可以被测量。

items.example: She agreed impulsively.
items.exampleCN: 她冲口就答应了。

items.meaning: the trait as a technical variable
items.meaningCN: 作为技术变量的冲动性
items.example: Impulsivity is studied in clinics.
items.exampleCN: 冲动性在临床中被研究。

definition_zh: 否认；否定；使无效；取消
definition_en: to state that something is not true, to make something ineffective, or to deny a proposition
core_image: 在整句话上盖一枚红色“否”字章，把整行划掉
scene: 这里指「否认」。 A lawyer stamps VOID across a clause to negate it, while the clerk crosses out the whole line.
sceneCN: 这里 negate 是「使无效、取消」（第 4 个义项：用正式手段使条款或行为失效）；句意：律师在一项条款上盖下“作废”章，使它失效，书记员把整行划掉。图中可辨识物件：合同纸、红色“作废”章、被划掉的条款、书记员的笔。

derivatives.zh: 否定的；负面的；负片；负数

senses.title: Deny a statement: say it is not true
senses.titleCN: 否认一句话：说它不成立
senses.definition: to state that a claim or statement is false
senses.definitionCN: 声明某项主张或说法是假的
senses.example: The witness negated every claim in the report.
senses.exampleCN: 证人否认了报告中的每一项主张。
senses.why: The Latin verb negare meant 'deny, say no'. Negating a statement is simply placing a no against it, so the word begins as a spoken refusal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 negare 意为“否认、说不”。否定一句话，就是在这句话前面放一个“不”，因此这个词最初是一个说出口的拒绝。

senses.title: Deny the value or existence of an idea
senses.titleCN: 否定一个观念的价值或存在
senses.definition: to reject the truth, value, or reality of an idea rather than of a single sentence
senses.definitionCN: 否定一个观念的真实性、价值或存在，而不是否定某一句话
senses.example: Nothing in the new evidence negates the value of the old method.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据中没有任何东西能否定旧方法的价值。
senses.why: The same 'say no' moves from a sentence to a whole idea. What is denied is no longer a wording but the standing of a belief.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“说不”从一句话移到整个观念。被否认的不再是措辞，而是一种信念的地位。

senses.title: Cancel out an effect: make an advantage useless
senses.titleCN: 抵消效果：让优势失去作用
senses.definition: to make the effect of something ineffective, so that its benefit disappears
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物的作用失效，使其好处消失
senses.example: Heavy rain negated the advantage of our early start.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨抵消了我们提早出发的优势。
senses.why: From 'say no to a claim' the word extends to 'say no to an effect': the advantage is treated as cancelled, as if a line were struck through it.
senses.whyCN: 从“对主张说不”扩展到“对效果说不”：优势被当作已被注销，就像上面划了一道线。

senses.title: Void a clause or a formal act
senses.titleCN: 使条款或正式行为作废
senses.definition: to cancel the legal force of a clause, order, or formal act
senses.definitionCN: 取消条款、命令或正式行为的法律效力
senses.example: The court negated the clause that barred workers from suing.
senses.exampleCN: 法院使那条禁止工人起诉的条款失效。
senses.why: A legal act exists by being valid. Saying no to its validity makes it nothing, so negate here means to render null and void.
senses.whyCN: 法律行为靠“有效”而存在。对它的有效性说不，就使它归零，因此这里的 negate 意为“使失效、作废”。

senses.title: Logical negation: deny a proposition
senses.titleCN: 逻辑否定：否定一个命题
senses.definition: in logic, to form the proposition that is true exactly when the original is false
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑中，构造一个当原命题为假时恰好为真的命题
senses.example: To negate 'all swans are white' is to assert that at least one swan is not white.
senses.exampleCN: 否定“所有天鹅都是白的”，就是断言至少有一只天鹅不是白的。
senses.why: Logic turns the spoken no into an operator. Negation does not merely disagree; it reverses the truth value of the whole proposition.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑把口头的“不”变成一个运算符。否定不只是不同意，而是把整个命题的真值翻转过来。

senses.title: Grammatical negation: mark a clause with not
senses.titleCN: 语法否定：用 not 一类词标记小句
senses.definition: in grammar, to make a clause negative with words such as not, never, no, or nothing
senses.definitionCN: 在语法中，用 not、never、no、nothing 等词使小句变为否定
senses.example: Adverbs such as 'never' negate the clause they appear in.
senses.exampleCN: never 这类副词会使其所在的小句变为否定。
senses.why: The same neg- morpheme appears in not and no. Grammar gives the refusal a fixed slot, so negate names the mechanical process of marking a clause negative.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 neg- 词素也出现在 not 与 no 中。语法为拒绝提供了一个固定位置，因此 negate 也指把小句标成否定的机械过程。

senses.title: Rebut a motion in debate
senses.definition: in formal debating, to oppose and argue against a motion so that it is defeated
senses.definitionCN: 在正式辩论中反对并论证击败一项动议
senses.example: The second speaker negated the motion with three independent arguments.
senses.exampleCN: 第二位辩手用三个独立论点驳倒了这项动议。
senses.why: A motion is a proposal put forward for acceptance. To negate it is to say no to the proposal as a whole, which in debate means arguing the other side.
senses.whyCN: 动议是提出来等待通过的提案。否定它，就是对整个提案说不；在辩论中，这就是站到另一边论证。

senses.title: Neutralize a military capability
senses.definition: to make an enemy capability or weapon ineffective, so that it no longer counts
senses.definitionCN: 使敌方能力或武器失效，使其不再构成作用
senses.example: The new battery negated the enemy's artillery range.
senses.exampleCN: 新的炮台使敌方火炮的射程优势失效。
senses.why: In warfare an advantage is cancelled as a claim is cancelled: the capability is still there, but its effect is struck out.
senses.whyCN: 在战争中，优势像主张一样被注销：能力还在，但它的作用被划掉了。

senses.title: Flip the sign of a number
senses.definition: in mathematics and computing, to reverse the sign of a value, turning positive into negative or the reverse
senses.definitionCN: 在数学与计算中，反转一个值的符号，把正变负或把负变正
senses.example: The program negates the value before storing it.
senses.exampleCN: 程序在存储该值之前先把它取负。
senses.why: If a number has a direction, negating it sends it the opposite way. The 'no' becomes a mirror: the same magnitude, the opposite sign.
senses.whyCN: 如果数带有方向，取负就把它送向相反方向。“不”在这里变成一面镜子：大小相同，符号相反。

senses.title: Cancel a result: wipe out a score or outcome
senses.titleCN: 取消结果：抹掉得分或成果
senses.definition: to cancel an achieved result, such as a goal or a gain, so that it no longer stands
senses.definitionCN: 取消已经取得的结果，如进球或收益，使其不再成立
senses.example: A foul in the final second negated the winning goal.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一秒的犯规使那粒制胜球失效。
senses.why: A result stands only if it counts. Negating it removes it from the record, which is the same 'strike it out' gesture applied to an outcome.
senses.whyCN: 结果只有在“算数”时才成立。否定它，就是把它从记录中划掉，这是同一个“划掉”动作用在成果上。

intro.en: Negate is built on Latin negare 'deny, say no', whose neg- is the same negative element as PIE *ne- 'not'. English gained the verb late, by back-formation from negation or directly from the Latin participle negatus.
intro.cn: negate 建立在拉丁语 negare“否认、说不”之上，其中的 neg- 与原始印欧语 *ne-“不”是同一个否定成分。英语较晚才得到这个动词，途径是从 negation 逆构，或直接取自拉丁语过去分词 negatus。

items.en: Latin negare 'to deny, say no', with past participle negatus and the noun negatio, is the source of the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 negare“否认、说不”，及其过去分词 negatus 和名词 negatio，是整个词族的来源。

items.en: Negare goes back to PIE *ne- 'not', the same element behind English no and not; neg- is thus a negative morpheme, not a root meaning 'thing'.
items.cn: negare 可追溯至原始印欧语 *ne-“不”，英语的 no 与 not 也出自同一成分；因此 neg- 是否定词素，而不是表示“物”的词根。

items.en: Negation is recorded in the 15c., arriving through Old French negacion and Latin negationem, both from negare.
items.cn: negation 记录于 15 世纪，经古法语 negacion 与拉丁语 negationem 传入，二者都出自 negare。

items.en: A few isolated uses of the verb negate appear in the 1620s, but they did not establish the word.
items.cn: 动词 negate 在 17 世纪 20 年代有个别用例，但并未使这个词立足。

items.en: The verb is established in 1795, either back-formed from negation or taken directly from the Latin participle negatus.
items.cn: 该动词于 1795 年确立，或由 negation 逆构而来，或直接取自拉丁语过去分词 negatus。

items.en: The neg- family remains visible in negative, deny, abnegate, renegade and negligible, all built on the same 'say no' element.
items.cn: neg- 词族仍可见于 negative、deny、abnegate、renegade、negligible，它们都建立在这个“说不”的成分上。

note.en: The first group shares neg- or a similar shape, sometimes with a different sense of the same element; the second group shares the idea of denying or cancelling.
note.cn: 第一组共享 neg- 或相近词形，其中有的虽是同一成分却另有一义；第二组共享“否认或取消”的意思。

entries.definition: to discuss in order to reach an agreement. It comes from Latin negotium 'business', literally nec otium 'not leisure', so its neg- means 'not' but points to work rather than denial.
entries.definitionCN: 谈判；协商。它来自拉丁语 negotium“事务”，字面是 nec otium“并非闲暇”，所以它的 neg- 虽也表示“不”，指向的却是工作而非否认。

entries.definition: too small to matter. It comes from neglegere 'to neglect', literally 'not to pick up', with neg- 'not' plus legere 'to pick'.
entries.definitionCN: 微不足道的。它来自 neglegere“忽视”，字面是“不去拾起”，由 neg-“不”加 legere“拾取”构成。

entries.definition: expressing denial, or below zero. It is the adjective from negare, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 否定的；负的。它是 negare 的形容词形式，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: to state that something is not true or that one does not possess it. It is the everyday verb, while negate often sounds formal.
entries.definitionCN: 否认某事为真，或声称自己不具有某物。它是日常动词，而 negate 常显得正式。

entries.definition: to make a law, contract, or result legally invalid. It stresses the legal effect that negate can also carry.
entries.definitionCN: 使法律、合同或结果在法律上无效。它强调 negate 也能携带的那层法律效力。

entries.definition: to prove a statement or argument wrong by evidence. It goes further than negate, which may only deny.
entries.definitionCN: 用证据证明某说法或论点错误。它比 negate 更进一步，因为 negate 可以只是否认。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: neg- is the negative element shared with no and not, and the family includes negation, negative, deny, abnegate and renegade.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：neg- 是与 no、not 共享的否定成分，词族包括 negation、negative、deny、abnegate、renegade。

normal.en: neg- is the same negative piece as in no and not: negate is literally 'to no' a statement.
normal.cn: neg- 与 no、not 中的否定成分相同：negate 字面上就是对一个说法“说不”。

normal.en: negation, negative and negator are the noun, adjective and agent built on the same stem.
normal.cn: negation、negative、negator 是同一词干上的名词、形容词与施动者。

normal.en: deny, abnegate and renegade all keep negare 'to deny': to deny a claim, to deny oneself, and to deny one's faith.
normal.cn: deny、abnegate、renegade 都保留 negare“否认”：否认主张、否定自我、否认信仰。

normal.en: In logic a negation reverses truth value; in grammar not, never and no do the same work in a clause.
normal.cn: 逻辑中否定翻转真值；语法中 not、never、no 在小句里做同样的工作。

normal.en: The legal picture is a stamp marked VOID: the clause still exists on paper, but its force has been struck out.
normal.cn: 法律画面是一枚“作废”章：条款仍在纸上，但它的效力已被划掉。

abstract.en: A red no stamped across a whole page: not one word is corrected, the entire page is refused.
abstract.cn: 整页纸上盖一个红色“不”：一个字都没改，整页都被拒绝。

abstract.en: Two mirror-image numbers, plus three and minus three: negation keeps the size and flips the direction.
abstract.cn: 两个镜像数字，正三与负三：否定保留大小，只翻转方向。

abstract.en: A door marked NO ENTRY still has a handle: the thing exists, but its use has been negated.
abstract.cn: 一扇写着“禁止入内”的门仍有把手：东西还在，但它的用途已被否定。

examples.en: The new evidence negated the claim that the lake was safe for swimming.
examples.cn: 新证据否定了这个湖可以安全游泳的说法。

examples.en: One late goal negated everything the visiting team had built in the first half.
examples.cn: 一粒迟来的进球抹掉了客队在上半场建立的一切。

examples.en: In formal logic, you negate a proposition by asserting that it is false.
examples.cn: 在形式逻辑中，你通过断言一个命题为假来否定它。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「你盖特」——你盖的章一律被划掉、被说“不算” → negate 否定、使无效

root: 源自拉丁语 negare“否认、说不”，来自原始印欧语 *ne-“不”；neg- 是否定词素，与英语 no、not 同源，不是表示实物的词根。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of negate all come from one gesture: putting a no against something. The no can fall on a statement, an idea, an effect, a clause, a proposition, a clause in grammar, a motion, a weapon, a number, or a result.
sensesIntro.cn: negate 的十个义项都来自同一个动作：对某样东西说“不”。这个“不”可以落在陈述、观念、效果、条款、命题、语法小句、动议、武器、数字或结果上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red no stamped across a line until it no longer counts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个红色“不”盖在一行字上，直到它不再算数。

branches.en: SPOKEN DENIAL: refusing a statement, then refusing a whole idea.
branches.cn: 口头否认：先拒绝一句话，再拒绝整个观念。

branches.en: STRIKING OUT: cancelling an effect, and wiping out a result that had already been achieved.
branches.cn: 划掉：抵消一种效果，以及抹掉已经取得的结果。

branches.en: FORMAL CANCELLATION: voiding a clause in law, and defeating a motion in debate.
branches.cn: 正式取消：在法律上使条款作废，在辩论中驳倒动议。

branches.en: LOGIC AND GRAMMAR: reversing a proposition's truth value, and marking a clause with not.
branches.cn: 逻辑与语法：翻转命题的真值，以及用 not 标记小句。

branches.en: TURNING TO THE OPPOSITE: neutralizing a capability, and flipping the sign of a number.
branches.cn: 转向反面：使能力失效，以及翻转数字的符号。

intro.en: Negate is neg- 'no' plus the verb ending -ate. English builds negation, negative, negatively, negator and abnegation on the same stem, while deny, renegade, negligible and negotiate carry the same negative element in other shapes.
intro.cn: negate 是 neg-“不”加动词词尾 -ate。英语在同一词干上构造出 negation、negative、negatively、negator、abnegation；而 deny、renegade、negligible、negotiate 以别的形态携带同一个否定成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin negare 'to deny, say no' and its participle negatus are the direct source; negatio and negativus supply the noun and adjective patterns.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 negare“否认、说不”及其分词 negatus 是直接来源；negatio 与 negativus 提供了名词与形容词的模式。

items.meaning: to deny, cancel, or make ineffective
items.meaningCN: 否认；取消；使无效（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The new rule negates the old exemption.
items.exampleCN: 新规定使旧的豁免失效。

items.meaning: the act or result of denying; a negative statement
items.meaningCN: 否定；否定句（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The negation of a true statement is false.
items.exampleCN: 真陈述的否定是假的。

items.meaningCN: 否定的；负面的；负的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The test gave a negative result.
items.exampleCN: 检测结果呈阴性。

items.meaning: in a denying or harmful way
items.meaningCN: 否定地；负面地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The delay affected the project negatively.
items.exampleCN: 延误对项目产生了负面影响。

items.meaning: a word or person that negates
items.meaningCN: 否定词；否定者（-or 构成施动名词）
items.example: In English, 'not' is the commonest negator.
items.exampleCN: 在英语中，not 是最常见的否定词。

items.meaning: to renounce or deny oneself something
items.meaningCN: 放弃；克制（ab-“离开”+ neg-“否认”，即把欲望否认掉）
items.example: The monk abnegated all personal possessions.
items.exampleCN: 这位修士放弃了所有个人财物。

items.meaning: a person who deserts a cause or faith
items.meaningCN: 叛教者；变节者（字面是“再次否认”自己的信仰）
items.example: The party called him a renegade for joining the rival camp.
items.exampleCN: 该党称他为变节者，因为他加入了对手阵营。

items.meaning: to state that something is not true
items.meaningCN: 否认；拒绝给予（de- 加强 + neg-“说不”）
items.example: She denied ever seeing the letter.
items.exampleCN: 她否认曾见过那封信。

items.meaning: too small or unimportant to consider
items.meaningCN: 微不足道的（字面是“不值得拾起”，neg-“不”+ leg-“拾取”）
items.example: The difference in cost was negligible.
items.exampleCN: 成本上的差别微不足道。

items.meaning: to discuss in order to reach an agreement
items.meaningCN: 谈判；协商（neg-“不”+ otium“闲暇”，即“不是闲事”的事务）
items.example: The two sides negotiated for six hours.
items.exampleCN: 双方谈判了六个小时。
